description: Postdoc - automated screening of electrolyte additives for aqueous batteries Job ID: 1078 Location: Geesthacht Application deadline: 11/26/2026 The postdoctoral candidate will work within an international research project focused on improving the performance and long-term stability of aqueous batteries through the development of advanced electrolyte additives. The central objective of the project is to establish an integrated high-throughput workflow combining robotic electrolyte preparation, automated electrochemical testing, and machine-learning-assisted analysis. The work involves extensive experimental laboratory activities, automated testing, electrochemical characterization, data analysis, and close cooperation with industrial project partners. The candidate will contribute to the development of reproducible and data-driven battery research workflows for sustainable, safe, and cost-effective stationary energy-storage technologies. The position is full-time (39 h/week) and fixed-term for 18 months, starting in February 2027. Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position. Your tasks - Develop and optimize automated high-throughput workflows for the preparation and electrochemical screening of aqueous electrolyte formulations. - Systematically screen a broad range of electrolyte additives and generate high-quality datasets linking electrolyte composition to battery performance. - Perform electrochemical characterization using techniques such as galvanostatic cycling, cyclic voltammetry, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. - Analyze large experimental datasets and contribute to the development and validation of machine-learning and quantitative structure-property relationship models. - Publish your results in leading peer-reviewed journals and present them at international conferences, write project reports. - Collaborate closely with researchers, data scientists, and industrial partners working on electrolyte synthesis, battery development, modelling, and scale-up. Your profile Recruitment requirement - A PhD in the subject areas of Materials science, Electrochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Energy Engineering, or similar. Required knowledge and personal skills - Strong background in electrochemistry and aqueous battery technologies. - Hands-on laboratory experience and interest in experimental research. - Experience with electrochemical measurements and data analysis. - Interest in automated experimentation and data-driven materials research. - Ability to work independently and as part of an interdisciplinary research team. - Knowledge of techniques such as EIS, cyclic voltammetry, hydrogen evolution, and electrode degradation. - Very good English language skills (at least B2/C1 level according to CEFR). Desired knowledge and personal skills - Experience with aqueous batteries, metal-anode batteries, or electrolyte development. - Experience with materials characterization techniques, such as microscopy, X-ray methods. - Experience with automated experimentation, robotics, data science, or machine learning is advantageous. Reach out with your CV and motivation letter expressing your interest and experience in the proposed topic. Got questions before applying? Contact Prof. Zheludkevich (Mikhail.zheludkevich@hereon.de), Dr. Lamaka (Sviatlana.lamaka@hereon.de) or Dr. Snihirova (darya.snihirova@hereon.de). Interested? We are looking forward to receiving your application. Horizon Europe - MSCA Marie Curie Grant Agreement Number 101312169 Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Offer Description Università di Pisa (UniPi) seeks a highly motivated PhD candidate for a fully funded international doctoral position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN), project MicroMan4Health: Data-Centric Micromanufacturing Platform Towards Added Value in the Health Sector ( www.microman4health.eu ). The shift from process-centric to data-centric micromanufacturing constitutes a paradigm evolution in how knowledge, control and value are created in micromanufacturing platforms for the health sector. About the Host Università di Pisa is a leading Italian university where thousands of students are educated each year across a wide range of scientific and technological disciplines. UniPi has always aimed at the quality and innovation of teaching and research by developing a fruitful relationship with the economic and industrial sectors. The Department of Civil and Industrial Engineering (DICI) provides full education in the field of advanced manufacturing processes and smart manufacturing systems. The DICI laboratories are equipped with state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities, including sink EDM, SEM and metallographic preparation, surface metrology, and various additive manufacturing technologies (metal and non-metal). UniPi is in Tuscany, a dynamic region with a strong industrial and technological ecosystem and a wonderful work-life balance. Research Background & Focus Research Background: Micro-surgical instruments and miniature metallic components for minimally invasive devices require sub-100 µm dimensional accuracy, stable surface integrity and compliance with stringent certification requirements. Micro-wire EDM is one of the few processes capable of shaping hard metallic materials at this scale, but its behaviour is governed by stochastic discharge phenomena and is still described largely through empirical relations. Machining, in-line monitoring and metrology data are generated along the process chain but rarely integrated, so deviations affecting quality or robustness are detected only after the fact. Research Focus: The research addresses the challenge of achieving deterministic and reliable micro-wire EDM manufacturing for medical micro-surgical instruments, where small variations in discharge behaviour, wire–workpiece interaction and thermal effects can significantly affect dimensional accuracy and surface integrity. The project aims to bridge process physics, real-time monitoring and data-driven modelling to understand and predict how machining conditions translate into final component quality. A central challenge is to transform process and metrology data into actionable knowledge, enabling early detection of instabilities and more accurate, adaptive control of micromanufacturing processes. Research Objectives: The doctoral project aims to develop an integrated modelling framework able to predict product performance in micro-wire EDM, starting from a multiscale and micro-physical analysis of the process. High-fidelity physical models will be combined with reduced-order, data-driven surrogate models describing subprocesses for which experimental data exist, but deterministic knowledge is still incomplete, with the objective of progressively replacing empirical formulations with physics-informed ones as new insights emerge. Key Objectives & Acquired Competences Construction of a hybrid modelling chain coupling physics-based discharge modelling with data-driven predictors, capturing wire wear, discharge dynamics and heat-affected zones and their causal impact on final component features. Integration of machining, in-line monitoring, metrology and testing data into early R&D and design workflows through advanced data analytics and validated simulation environments. Development of a structured process–product data-management architecture enabling traceability, knowledge extraction and early-warning indicators for deviations affecting quality or robustness. Assessment of advanced materials and wire configurations (coated wires, high-tensile alloys, optimised dielectric fluids) to improve cutting stability, surface integrity and dimensional accuracy. Establishment of a real–virtual testing bench combining in-situ monitoring, digital twins and model-based quality assessment, with AI-supported analytics processing monitoring signals and providing real-time feedback for model updating. Benchmarking process parameters, quality metrics and sustainability indicators to ensure cross-validation of the modelling approaches. Expected Results & KPIs A validated workflow integrating machining data, in-situ monitoring signals and metrology outputs into a unified knowledge base (data ingestion completeness above 90%; at least 20% reduction in manual data-processing effort). A software prototype implementing hybrid physics-based and data-driven models (prediction accuracy of at least 80% for dimensional accuracy and surface roughness; computational runtime reduced by at least 30% with respect to full physical simulations). Predictive models for machining outcomes and early detection of process anomalies (early-warning detection rate of at least 75%; process repeatability improved by at least 20%; scrap rate reduced by at least 15% in controlled validation tests). Quantified and experimentally validated surface-integrity descriptors, including microstructural alterations and recast-layer metrics (recast-layer thickness variability within ±10% across repeated runs; tolerance windows compatible with ISO 13485 and medical device requirements). Evidence-based knowledge on advanced wire materials, coatings and dielectric conditions (cutting stability or MRR improved by at least 15% for at least one advanced configuration; wire wear or breakage frequency reduced by at least 20%). Validation, Industrial Relevance & Secondments Industrial Relevance: The project combines the long-standing expertise of Università di Pisa in electrical discharge machining (discharge modelling, process monitoring, optimisation strategies and innovative dielectric-fluid formulations), with the requirements of industrial and academic partners of the network. Secondments & Research Mobility: Three secondments are planned, with a primary focus on the industrial experience at MMIMicro (3 months), where the researcher will work on the definition of tolerances and functional constraints for micro-components used in robotic micro-surgical assemblies, evaluate prototype parts and micro-metrology tools, and validate the proposed monitoring approach on industrial equipment. A complementary secondment at KU Leuven (2 months) will support benchmarking against the activities of DC5 and the development of shared guidelines for assessing hybrid modelling approaches. Finally, Politecnico di Milano (1 month) will provide expertise in advanced simulation and CAM for micro-milling, enabling a direct benchmark between micro-wire EDM and micro-milling. Technical Skills B.1 Strong interest and hands-on experience in precision and micro-manufacturing, ideally including non-conventional processes such as EDM or micro-wire EDM. B.2 Experience in physics-based and numerical modelling (FEM, thermal or multiphysics simulation) and interest in reduced-order or surrogate modelling. B.3 Hands-on experience in data-driven modelling, machine learning, digital-twin concepts and programming (e.g. Python or similar). B.4 Experience with experimental setups, laboratory and measurement equipment, process monitoring and signal acquisition. B.5 Familiarity with surface and microstructural characterisation (surface topography, SEM, metallographic analysis, recast layer assessment) is an asset. B.6 Practical knowledge of design of experiments (DoE), statistical analysis and scientific presentation. B.7 Awareness of data management, traceability and medical-device quality frameworks (e.g. ISO 13485) is an asset. C. The monthly gross salary will comprise a living allowance (approximately € 4,000/month, to be corrected with the country factor of the recruiting institution), mobility allowance (€ 710/month) and if applicable a family allowance (€ 660/month) and if applicable other allowances according to Grant Agreement of Project MicroMan4Health. Candidates must have a master's degree or a similar degree with an equivalent academic level in mechanical, manufacturing, materials, mechatronic or biomedical engineering, or a closely related discipline (or equivalent), master’s degree that gives access to a PhD program in the country where it was obtained and meets the admission requirements of the PHD program of the university for this position. Approval and Enrollment in the PhD Programme The activation of the Phd position is subject to academic approval by the University, to be made after the end of the selection process. The interview, reserved only to applicants passing the qualification rate, will be held at the University of Pisa, Department of Civil and Industrial Engineering, Largo Lucio Lazzarino 2, Pisa, Italy. Candidates unable to attend the interview at the University of Pisa will be allowed to be interviewed via web or conference call. The Selection committee is appointed to establish the duly examination of the candidates and shall acquire each candidate’s copy of an identity card or passport. description: 4 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company University of Groningen Research Field Medical sciences » Medicine Neurosciences » Neurobiology Psychological sciences » Psychology Researcher Profile Recognised Researcher (R2) Application Deadline 26 Nov 2026 - 23:00 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? No Offer Description Are you an experienced researcher with a passion for evidence synthesis, systematic review methodology and innovative approaches to scientific knowledge integration? Do you want to contribute to an ambitious international research programme aiming to improve the understanding and clinical use of biomarkers and endpoints related to reward, motivation and impulsivity across major depressive disorder, Alzheimer’s disease and obesity? The University of Groningen is looking for an enthusiastic and scientifically strong Postdoctoral Researcher in Living Evidence Synthesis, Systematic Reviews and AI-supported Evidence Research. In this position, you will play a central role in developing and maintaining a structured living evidence framework that continuously integrates new scientific knowledge with emerging findings from a large, interdisciplinary research programme. You will combine advanced systematic review and meta-analysis methods with innovative approaches to evidence surveillance and large language model (LLM)-supported research. This is an exciting opportunity for a researcher who wants to work at the intersection of evidence synthesis, clinical research, biomarker science and artificial intelligence, while contributing to research with potential relevance for patients, clinicians, regulators, health technology assessment bodies and healthcare systems. What are you going to do? As a Postdoctoral Researcher, you will take a leading role in the implementation and coordination of the project's living evidence activities. You will work closely with researchers across different disciplines and with international academic, clinical and societal partners. Your main responsibilities will include: Implementing and further developing a structured living evidence synthesis framework for continuously identifying, evaluating and integrating emerging evidence. Coordinating the ongoing living evidence synthesis , ensuring that evidence is systematically monitored, critically appraised, synthesised and updated throughout the five-year research programme. Conducting systematic and living systematic reviews on reward, motivation and impulsivity biomarkers and endpoints across major depressive disorder, Alzheimer’s disease and obesity. Conducting and coordinating meta-analyses , including analyses of predictive and monitoring performance, sensitivity to change, cross-disease comparability and the potential applicability of biomarkers and endpoints across diagnostic groups. Synthesising evidence from a broad range of modalities, including neuroimaging, electrophysiology, biosamples, behavioural and cognitive measures, and digital phenotyping. Implementing and critically evaluating LLM-supported methods for literature searching, deduplication, screening and structured data extraction. Ensuring that AI-supported evidence synthesis processes are transparent, reproducible, auditable and subject to appropriate human validation. Developing and maintaining structured, machine-readable evidence maps, metadata and versioned evidence updates. Assessing methodological heterogeneity, strength and consistency of evidence, knowledge gaps, clinical relevance and translational potential. Contributing to the development and application of harmonised outcome domains and evidence-grading and prioritisation frameworks. Integrating evidence from longitudinal cohorts, clinical studies and other research activities to support hypothesis generation, refinement and prioritisation. Contributing methodological expertise to the interpretation of biomarker and endpoint evidence and to the identification of promising areas for further validation. Preparing high-quality scientific publications, systematic review reports, meta-analysis papers and project deliverables. Communicating findings to a diverse range of scientific and non-scientific audiences. Contributing to scientific coordination, progress monitoring and reporting within this international collaborative research programme. You will have considerable scientific responsibility and scope to further develop the methodological approaches used for living evidence synthesis. The position therefore offers an excellent opportunity to establish or strengthen an independent research profile in systematic review methodology, evidence synthesis and AI-supported research. Where to apply Website https://www.academictransfer.com/en/jobs/365270/postdoctoral-researcher-living-… Requirements Specific Requirements We are looking for an independent and collaborative researcher with a strong methodological background and a genuine interest in developing innovative approaches to evidence synthesis. You have: A PhD in biomedical sciences, psychology, neuroscience, medicine, or a related discipline. Demonstrable experience conducting systematic reviews and evidence syntheses , preferably including living systematic reviews or evidence surveillance. Solid expertise in quantitative evidence synthesis and meta-analysis. A strong understanding of methodological quality, risk of bias, heterogeneity and critical appraisal of scientific evidence. Experience with statistical analysis and reproducible research workflows, preferably using R, Python or comparable statistical/programming tools An interest in, or experience with, artificial intelligence, natural language processing or large language models applied to research workflows. The ability to critically assess the opportunities and limitations of AI-supported systematic review methods. Experience working with complex or heterogeneous evidence is an advantage, particularly evidence involving biomarkers, clinical endpoints, neuroimaging, electrophysiology, biosamples, behavioural measures or digital phenotyping. Excellent scientific writing skills and the ability to translate complex methodological and scientific findings into clear reports and publications. Strong organisational and project-coordination skills, including the ability to manage multiple interconnected research activities and deadlines. The ability to work independently while actively contributing to a large, interdisciplinary and international research team. Excellent communication skills and a willingness to engage with researchers and stakeholders from different disciplines and professional backgrounds. Excellent command of written and spoken English . Experience with one or more of the following would be particularly valuable: Living systematic reviews or living evidence platforms. Evidence mapping and evidence surveillance. Systematic review automation. Machine-readable evidence structures and structured metadata. Reproducible and version-controlled research workflows. LLM-supported literature screening or data extraction. Biomarker or endpoint validation. Research in major depressive disorder, Alzheimer’s disease or obesity. Stakeholder-informed evidence synthesis or research prioritisation. Most importantly, you are intellectually curious, methodologically rigorous and motivated to develop new approaches to synthesising rapidly evolving scientific evidence. Additional Information Benefits What can you expect from us? 232 vacation hours per year, based on a 38-hour workweek (1.0 FTE). You can also work more or fewer hours in exchange for more or fewer free hours. For example, with a 40-hour workweek, you save 96 extra free hours, and with a 36-hour workweek, you lose 96 hours. End-of-year bonus of 8.3% and 8% holiday allowance. Extensive opportunities for personal and professional development. Selection process Interested? Does this vacancy appeal to you? If so, click on the button below and apply straightaway. Please add the following documents to your application: CV (incl. 2 references), Cover letter. Information about applying When scheduling meetings, we will take your schedule into account as much as possible. The University of Groningen considers social safety important. We strive to be a university where staff and students feel respected and at home, regardless of differences in background, experiences, perspectives, and identity. For more information, see also our page about our diversity policy . Our selection procedure follows the guidelines of the NVP application code Acquisition is not appreciated. Dataphyte Foundation, in partnership with the Center for International Private Enterprise (CIPE), invites applications from Nigerian journalists to join a two-month investigative journalism fellowship on foreign-funded infrastructure reporting. The Foreign-Funded Infrastructure Accountability (“Infra-Watch”) Media Fellowship will train five Journalists to investigate and report on how foreign-financed infrastructure projects in Nigeria are funded via Official Development Assistance (ODA), Private Public Partnerships (PPPs), bilateral and multilateral debt financing, how the infrastructure contracts are managed, and the projects implemented, and compared to global best practices. This fellowship is part of Dataphyte’s Mobilising Data for Infrastructure Governance and Corrosive Capital Monitoring in Nigeria project. Fellows will work with data from Dataphyte’s Anfani portal and CIPE’s Infrastructure Watch platform for their investigation. Eligibility The fellowship is open to Nigerian Journalists who meet all of the following criteria: Work as an accountability, investigative, business or economy Journalist as staff or freelancer. Have a track record of published or broadcast stories, with an interest in public finance, infrastructure, debt or procurement reporting. Can commit to full participation in all training sessions, mentorship and reporting milestones throughout the fellowship. Have their employer’s consent to take part (staff journalists only). Women Journalists and applicants outside Lagos and Abuja are strongly encouraged to apply. Benefits Training on foreign development financing structures, loan contracts, procurement and corrosive capital risks. Hands-on training in using Anfani Beneficial Ownership and CIPE Infrastructure Watch data for investigations. Mentorship support from Dataphyte’s editorial team.. Funding to produce one investigative report on a foreign-funded infrastructure project. Publication and promotion of fellows’ stories through Dataphyte’s platforms. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the application form using the link below and upload the required supporting documents. A sample of published report or multiformat production, on external aid and debt financing, especially on infrastructure projects. A story pitch on one foreign-funded infrastructure project you wish to investigate. ( Pitch Template ) A letter of consent from your employer (staff Journalists only). Application Timeline Call opens Thursday 19 November 2026 Application deadline Friday 27 November 2026 Shortlisted applicants contacted Friday 5 December 2026 Fellowship duration Three months. Start date to be announced to shortlisted applicants . For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the Dataphyte Foundation Infra-watch Media Fellowship

description: 29 Oct 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company NTNU Norwegian University of Science and Technology Department Department of Energy and Process Engineering Research Field Engineering » Mechanical engineering Engineering » Thermal engineering Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Positions PhD Positions Application Deadline 27 Nov 2026 - 23:59 (Europe/Oslo) Country Norway Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Horizon Europe - MSCA Marie Curie Grant Agreement Number 101311533 Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description This is NTNU NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim. At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world. You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here. About the position A 3-year PhD position is available at the Department of Energy and Process Engineering as part of the HORIZON Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action (MSCA) Doctoral Network “SurPhase”. Efficient boiling and condensation are fundamental to thermal management in refrigeration, air conditioning, electronics cooling and energy systems. The transition toward slow Global Warming Potential refrigerants is essential for reducing environmental impact, but these fluids introduce new challenges associated with altered wetting behaviour, nucleation, liquid and vapour transport, dryout and flooding. This PhD project will experimentally investigate droplet shedding, film breakup, flooding, heat transfer coefficient and pressure drop in ribbed and finned micro structured surfaces during flow condensation of low surface tension refrigerants. The successful candidate will work at at the Thermal Two-Phase Flow Laboratory ( http://folk.ntnu.no/fernandi/ ) at NTNU’s main Gløshaugen campus in Trondheim, Norway. Experiments will be conducted with state-of-the-art equipment and experimental techniques. The candidate will be part of a friendly working environment, with close interaction with our postdoc, PhD and MSc candidates working in our group. The position will be supervised by Professor Maria Fernandino. Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department. About the project SurPhase is a Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network training 12 doctoral candidates in surface engineering and phase-change heat transfer for low-global-warming-potential refrigerants. SurPhase brings together four academic beneficiaries: the University of Birmingham, Sabanci University, Norwegian University of Science and Technology and University of Padova, supported by Ericsson, Arçelik, Fraunhofer IFAM, ANSYS and Hexxcell. The programme combines academic and industrial research, international mobility, network-wide training and cross-sector secondments. Duties of the position Design, planning and running of condensation experiments Contribute to academic publications, project reports and other dissemination activities Participate in meetings with supervisors and colleagues Engage in secondments as part of the project training activities Participate in structured training programs and network eventsorganized by the consortium Collaborate with other doctoral candidates in the consortium Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required selection criteria To apply for this MSCA Training position, applicants must fulfil the following criteria: At the time of recruitment by the host organisation, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in the country of the recruiting beneficiary for more than12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding their recruitment date. Applicants must be willing and able to undertake the planned international academic and industrial secondments within the SurPhase network. General required selection criteria: You must meet the requirements for admission to the Faculty's Doctoral Programme , see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information. You must have a relevant Master's degree in mechanical engineering, thermal engineering, applied physics or equivalent. description: 8 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Lunds universitet Department Lund University, LTH, Department of Computer Science Research Field Computer science Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 27 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Sweden Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Description of the workplace The position is within the Software Development and Environments division, part of the Department of Computer Science. The division is exploring novel tools, languages, and methods for supporting software development, and conducts research in a variety of topics that include refactoring, program analysis, compiler construction, declarative specification languages, distributed development environments, and automatic program repair. Its research involves strong collaborations both locally within Lund University, internationally with other universities, and with industrial partners, such as ABB and Ericsson, including research driven by industrial PhD students. The division currently has twelve members, and regularly organises group activities to foster a positive working environment. The division is actively developing the JastAdd metacompilation framework, which is the foundation for several compilers and software tools, including the division's ExtendJ extensible Java compiler and the static analysis tools IntraJ and MetaDL. More about the Software Development and Environments group (sde.cs.lth.se/) More about JastAdd (jastadd.cs.lth.se/web/) More about ExtendJ (extendj.org) More about MetaDL (github.com/lu-cs-sde/metadl) Being a doctoral student As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. As a doctoral student, you will learn to approach questions and challenges scientifically. In short, this means that you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree. More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. Subject and project description This research project aims to develop novel tools and techniques that enforce rigid guard-rails during software refactoring and other forms of software evolution. We assume an unreliable source of program transformations, such as a human developer or a large language model. The guard-rail mechanism will then inspect, steer, and augment any sequence of program transformations to detect and recover from unintended behavioural change. The position is funded by the Excellence Center at Linköping – Lund in Information Technology (ELLIIT), and it is a collaboration with the Natural Language Processing group at Linköping University, part of the division of Artificial Intelligence and Integrated Computer Systems. More about ELLIIT (elliit.se) More about the Division of Artificial Intelligence and Integrated Computer Systems at Linköping University (liu.se/en/organisation/liu/ida/aiics) Work duties You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences. The work duties include: Research on automatic program analysis and program transformation applied to preventing unintended behavioural change during refactoring and similar program evolution tasks. You will work towards exploring approaches that can aid real-world software evolution, and examine qualitative aspects of these approaches. Applying appropriate research methods: depending on the trajectory of this research, different and possibly novel methodologies may be required to provide robust answers to the underlying research questions. You will learn, apply, and possibly support the development of suitable methods. Artefact-oriented activity: You will develop software tools, algorithms, and other software components. These should be evaluated in realistic scenarios and integrated with, as well as shared within, the project team. Presentation and collaboration: You will present your research findings at the annual ELLIIT workshop in southern Sweden and discuss your work at meetings with academic project partners, including personal meetings with our collaboration partners in Linköping. Interaction with the industry: You will have opportunities to discuss your work and collaborate with industrial researchers, especially in Lund. The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (limited to a maximum of 20% of working hours). Qualifications To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below. Admission requirements A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in computer science if the applicant has: at least 60 second-cycle credits at an advanced level with relevance for the research topic, or an MSc in Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Information and Communication Technology, Engineering Physics or Engineering Mathematics. Additional requirements In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: Knowledge or experience in at least one of the following areas (demonstrated e.g. in the form of a university course, or through professional experiences or contributions to relevant open source projects): o compiler construction, or o the foundations of static program analysis. good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems. good written and oral communication skills. good ability to cooperate. very good knowledge of English, in speech and writing. very good programming experience (demonstrated e.g. in the form of professional experiences, contributions to open source projects, or outstanding results in university courses). persistence and the ability to plan and structure your own work curiosity and willingness to learn and adopt new techniques, especially within the cross-disciplinary scope of the project Other qualifications (advantages) For the doctoral programme in question, it is advantageous if you can demonstrate experience or knowledge in one or more of the following subjects: developing automatic program transformation tools, such as o refactoring tools, or o meta-programming tools. software development in teams, especially in the context of: o professional software engineering, o open source projects, or o legacy software engineering projects. dynamic program analysis. programming in Java. functional or declarative programming (logic programming, reference attribute grammars etc.). natural language processing, machine learning, and/or applying large language models, such as o working with the underlying machine learning techniques, such as latent/embedding spaces, representation learning, or transformers, o training or fine-tuning such models, or o applying them to software development / software engineering tasks. systematic evaluation of software systems and relevant statistical methods. systems programming. areas of discrete mathematics with relation to program analysis (lattice theory, type theory, Galois connections etc.). We offer Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. This project additionally offers collaboration opportunities with Linköping University via its joint supervision structure, and industrial outreach opportunities via ELLIIT, such as the annual ELLIIT workshop. More about working at Lund University on lu.se. About the employment The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, with intended start date in the spring of 2027 or according to agreement, but no later than 2027-12-31. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§. More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages. How to apply Applications shall be written in English and include: CV and a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the doctoral programme/employment and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background. Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral programme project. Other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.) We welcome your application. description: 8 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Karolinska Institutet (KI) Research Field Medical sciences » Medicine Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 27 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Sweden Type of Contract Not Applicable Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research? Join the research group of Sophie Bensing at the Department of Medicine, Solna, Division of Experimental Endocrinology based at the Centre for Molecular Medicine (CMM). Our group combines and develops novel single cell genomics approaches to understand how transcriptional regulation and alternative splicing shape immune cell states, with a particular focus on T-cell regulation, endocrine organs and autoimmune disease. We are particularly interested in how immune cells respond immediately to stimulation and how these early molecular events may shape later cell fate and functional outcomes. We are looking for 1-2 research assistants that will work at the interface of experimental and computational biology, single-cell technologies and immunology in a collaborative, method-driven research environment. Your mission As a research assistant, you will be tasked with providing experimental and practical support for ongoing projects within multi-omic method development and time-course and pertubation focused experiments untangling how immediate response might drive transient cell states and fates. Main responsibilities: Process, prepare and quality control for single-cell transcriptomics experiments as well as RNA extraction, cell culture, according to established protocols Assist with analysis of single cell sequencing data Organize experimental data, maintain accurate laboratory records and contribute to preliminary analysis Collaborate with team members, present progress in group meetings and support routine laboratory operations Your profile We are looking for 1-2 enthusiastic, motivated, and collaborative early-career research assistants with an interest in experimental biomedical research, single cell methods and transcriptional regulation. You should be well organized, eager to learn and comfortable working with biological samples and established protocols. Required qualifications: A Master’s degree in Biomedicine, Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Biotechnology, or a related field, or an equivalent degree expected to be completed before the start of employment Documented hands-on experience in a biological or biomedical laboratory, including relevant thesis research Ability to follow experimental protocols precisely and maintain structured laboratory records Good communication skills in English, both spoken and written Ability to work independently on assigned tasks and collaborate effectively with colleagues Meritorious qualifications: Experience with one ore more of the following: RNA extraction, cell culture, FACS sorting, single cell RNA-seq, CRISPR assays, spheroid/organoid cultures, and animal work Familiarity with single-cell transcriptomics, sequencing sample preparation or basic bioinformatics Experience presenting scientific findings or contributing to multidisciplinary research What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment with wide-ranging expertise and interests. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. Karolinska Institutet is also a state university, which entitles you to several good benefits through our collective agreement. And you get to practice freely in our modern wellness facilities, where trained staff are on site. Location The position is located within the Department of Medicine, Solna. The department consists of ten divisions and each division consists of several research groups. The position is located within the research group of Sophie Bensing within the Division of Experimental Endocrinology, with research activities connected to immune regulation, single-cell genomics, endocrinology and autoimmune disease. --[Video about Karolinska Institutet, how we all work towards "a better health for all"] -- Application KI applies individual and differentiated salary setting in accordance with our collective agreements RALS and RALS-T. The application is to be submitted through the Varbi recruitment system.In this recruitment, you will apply with your CV without a personal letter. Instead, you will answer some questions about why you are applying for the job in the application form. Want to make a difference? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Description of the Workplace The PhD project will be conducted in neurosurgery, with a focus on malignant brain tumours. The research group conducts experimental and translational research in neurosurgery, with close links to clinical practice. The research integrates preclinical brain tumour models, cell-based methods, and studies of human biological samples. The doctoral student will become part of a multidisciplinary research environment in which experimental and clinical expertise are closely integrated. Within the research group, we strive to conduct internationally competitive research while also maintaining a positive working environment characterised by respect and consideration. We also place great importance on ensuring that everyone feels involved, stimulated and supported. The Department of Clinical Sciences in Lund is recruiting a doctoral student in the third-cycle subject of Medical Science – Neurosurgery, within the doctoral project “Multimodal treatment of malignant brain tumours”. The position is based at the Faculty of Medicine, Lund University, in an international and interdisciplinary research environment. Work Assignments As a doctoral student, you will primarily undertake doctoral studies through independent research under supervision within the project “Multimodal treatment of malignant brain tumours”. The doctoral project focuses on local treatment of malignant brain tumours and how local neurosurgical treatment strategies can affect tumour cells and the tumour immune microenvironment. The project includes local drug delivery and chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and experimental laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT). Treatment effects will be studied in cell-based systems, orthotopic experimental brain tumour models and, where relevant, in human brain tumour and biobank material. The project has a clear translational link to clinical neurosurgery. Aim and Implementation of the Project The aim of this four-year doctoral project is to conduct research in experimental and translational neurosurgery, focusing on malignant brain tumours. The project aims to develop and evaluate local treatment strategies and combination therapies, as well as to investigate their effects on tumour biology and the tumour immune microenvironment. Work Duties The doctoral student’s main responsibility is to undertake doctoral studies through independent research under supervision. The work will be carried out within the framework of the doctoral project “Multimodal treatment of malignant brain tumours”. You will plan, conduct, analyse and document experiments in experimental neurosurgery. The work duties include: working with orthotopic experimental animal models of brain tumours local intracranial or intratumoral administration of drugs or other substances, including the use of micro-osmotic pumps cell culture and cell-based experiments, including performing and analysing in vitro assays experimental combination treatments, including local chemotherapy, radiotherapy and LITT, where relevant handling, processing and analysis of human brain tumour tissue and biobank samples collection, statistical analysis and compilation of experimental data, as well as presentation and publication of research findings active participation in the research group’s scientific activities and in national and international collaborations. Other duties may also be assigned. Qualifications Basic eligibility Eligibility for third-cycle studies requires: a second-cycle (master’s) degree, or completed courses totalling at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 credits are at second-cycle level, or equivalent knowledge acquired in another way. Specific eligibility Specific eligibility requirements include: a relevant second-cycle degree or equivalent qualification in medicine, biomedicine, biology, molecular biology or another closely related field within the life sciences documented research experience in experimental biomedical or neuroscience research relevant to the project or a closely related field documented practical experience of experimental animal techniques relevant to neuroscience or tumour biology research documented experience of cell culture, cell-based experiments and in vitro assays, as well as experience of handling and processing human biobank samples very good oral and written proficiency in English the ability to work independently and with perseverance, combined with strong analytical, writing and collaborative skills. Desirable Qualifications The following qualifications are considered advantageous: a medical degree or equivalent qualification in medicine specific research experience in experimental neuro-oncology experience of orthotopic or other preclinical brain tumour models and local intracerebral or intratumoral drug administration experience of diagnostic imaging in experimental animals experience of translational research combining experimental models with human biological samples documented scientific publications in a field relevant to the project. Assessment criteria Selection among eligible applicants will be based on: scientific maturity and analytical ability motivation, independence and collaborative skills capacity to successfully complete doctoral studies the extent to which the applicant’s background and experience are considered to contribute to the successful completion of the project. Terms of employment The position is a full-time, fixed-term doctoral student position for four years (48 months), in accordance with the Swedish Higher Education Ordinance. The intended start date is 1 February 2027, or as agreed. How to apply Applications are to be submitted via the University’s recruitment system. The application should include a CV and a personal letter justifying your interest in the position and how it matches your qualifications. The application should also include a degree certificate or equivalent and any other document to which you would like to draw attention (copies of grade transcripts, details of referees, letters of recommendation, etc.). Welcome to apply! The Department of Clinical Sciences in Lund is one of six departments within the Faculty of Medicine. The department maintains extensive collaborations both within the faculty and with other units at Lund University. It also has well-established partnerships with Skåne University Hospital (SUS), Region Skåne, and external stakeholders in society and industry. These collaborations support clinical and experimental translational research, development, and education. Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Description of workplace The Division of Rheumatology conducts its experimental research activities at the Biomedical Centre (BMC) in Lund, in close proximity to Skåne University Hospital. The Division is part of the Department of Clinical Sciences Lund (IKVL), one of six departments within the Faculty of Medicine. At the Division of Rheumatology, Professor Anders Bengtsson leads the Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) research group. The group also includes three clinically active rheumatologists with PhDs, two doctoral students who combine their doctoral studies with clinical work, and one full-time doctoral student. A nurse and a biostatistician are also affiliated with the group. The research projects focus on the autoimmune disease SLE, combining clinical characterization of the disease with experimental studies of its underlying disease mechanisms. The Division also includes research groups focusing on arthritis and vasculitis. Within the research group, we are committed to maintaining a positive working environment characterized by respect and consideration in our interactions with one another. We strive to provide a workplace that is stimulating and offers opportunities for professional development for all employees. We continuously work to create an environment that promotes job satisfaction, development and participation. We are committed to both physical safety and a healthy psychosocial work environment. We offer Lund University is a governmental authority, which means you get special benefits, generous holidays, and a favorable occupational pension. Read more on the university's website about being employed at Lund University, Work at Lund University We are seeking a driven and motivated postdoctoral researcher with the ability to work independently and further develop ongoing research projects. The position is full-time. The suggested start date is January 1, 2027, or as agreed upon. Duties and responsibilities The duties are primarily related to the experimental aspects of the research, including the development of various assays. Identify and characterize novel, previously undiscovered platelet autoantigens in SLE and related diseases. Characterize the proteome of cerebrospinal fluid in patients with SLE and investigate the type I interferon system in SLE. Investigate the significance of phospholipid antibodies, neuronal antibodies and other autoantibodies relevant to SLE, particularly those associated with the brain and central nervous system. Process and analyse results from brain imaging studies in combination with other biomarkers. Compile research findings and publish results in scientific journals. Participate in experimental laboratory-based projects initiated by other research groups at the Division of Rheumatology. Actively participate in internal meetings in Lund as well as international conferences. Travel is required. The workplace is in Lund, Sweden. Participation in project meetings, workplace meetings and seminars requires physical presence at the workplace. Other duties may also be assigned. Basis for assessment This is a merit-based position primarily focused on research. The position is intended as an initial step in the academic career, and the selection will be based primarily on scientific merit and potential as a researcher. Particular emphasis will be placed on demonstrated skills within the subject area. Requirements for the position A PhD in rheumatology, with a focus on SLE and the central nervous system. Extensive experience of laboratory work related to autoimmune diseases, including the development and validation of the following methods: ELISA, cell-based reporter gene assays, qPCR, protein purification and protein chemistry methods, as well as bioinformatics work focusing on proteomics of cerebrospinal fluid. Experience in analysing and compiling research results for publication in scientific journals. Experience in reviewing and compiling relevant scientific literature as background material for assay development. Fluency in Swedish, both spoken and written. Good command of English, both spoken and written. Meritorious qualifications Training in Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Good theoretical knowledge of immunology, inflammation and autoimmunity. Specialist knowledge of the complement system. Eligibility Appointment to a post-doctoral position requires that the applicant has a PhD, or an international degree deemed equivalent to a PhD, relevant for the subject of the position. This requirement needs to be met no later than the time when the employment decision is made. We will mainly consider candidates who have completed their PhD degree no more than three (3) years before the last date for applications. Under special circumstances, candidates who have completed their PhD degree earlier may be considered. These circumstances may include leave due to illness, parental leave, clinical work, positions of trust or other similar circumstances. Terms of employment This is a full-time employment limited to 2 years, with the possibility of extension for up to one additional year. Preliminary start is the 1st of January 2027, or according to agreement. The period of employment is determined in accordance with the agreement “Avtal om tidsbegränsad anställning som postdoktor” (“Agreement on fixed-term employment as a post-doctoral researcher” between SACO-S, OFR/S and SEKO, dated November 19, 2021). How to apply The position is sought via the university's recruitment system. The application must include a personal letter (maximum two pages) in which you describe how you meet the qualification requirements and how your research is connected to the COMBAT project. The application must also contain a CV, including a list of publications, a general description of previous research work (maximum one page), a copy of the PhD degree certificate and anything else you wish to refer to (copies of diplomas, grades, information for references, letters of recommendation, etc.) as well as contact information for two references. We are looking forward to your application! description: 8 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Umeå universitet stipendiemodul Department Faculty of Science and Technology, Department of Computing Science Research Field Computer science Researcher Profile Recognised Researcher (R2) First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 27 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Sweden Type of Contract Not Applicable Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description The Department of computing science is offering a postdoctoral scholarship within the project “Artificial Intelligent Agents Supporting Older Adults’ Engagement in Activities to Promote Health”. The scholarship is full-time for two years with access 1 February, 2027 or by agreement. The application deadline is 27 November, 2026 The Department of Computing Science at Umeå University is an international environment for research and education covering a broad spectrum of computer science. The department is internationally renowned for its excellent research and education. We are affiliated with WASP – Sweden’s largest individual research program of all time, coordinate its sister program WASP-HS, which focuses on the consequences of emerging technologies, and are a strong partner in the national strategic research program eSSENCE. We value diversity and actively work to promote an inclusive work environment with a high level of engagement. Read more at: Department of Computing Science. The department's research on ​​responsible and human-centred artificial intelligence that collaborates with humans and enhances human capacity has a strong international position. The Intelligent and Interactive Systems research group conducts multidisciplinary research with a focus on methods and tools for the design, analysis and evaluation of socially intelligent systems that aim to collaborate with humans in learning and decision-making tasks, often with the aim of improving health. Visit: Interactive and Intelligent Systems Project description The project “Artificial Intelligent Agents Supporting Older Adults’ Engagement in Activities to Promote Health” is funded by the Kempe Foundation. The aim of the project is to explore how the concepts of a digital companion could be developed to support older adults in daily activities perceived as important to maintain health and wellbeing. The aim is to explore how an AI based instrument needs to function to be useful for both older adults in daily activities and occupational therapists in clinical practice. The project will explore methods for tailoring support provided by the agent using dynamic and adaptive modeling whilst addressing computational challenges the collaborative aspects of human-agent dialogue and interaction pose. This will contribute to constructing individualized, AI-based interventions that can be updated using individual characteristics that may change over time, e.g. motivation, health, capability, and activity. Outputs from this project will include new models and estimation tools, and will inform the design of the ongoing development of interventions, as well as future interventions to promote life-long learning and activity engagement. This postdoctoral scholarship is financed by the KEMPE Foundations (Stiftelserna J.C. Kempes och Seth M. Kempes minne) . The scholarship is tax-free and amounts to 750,000 SEK for two years, corresponding to 375,000 SEK per year. Qualifications To qualify as a postdoctoral scholarship holder, the postdoctoral fellow is required to have completed a doctoral degree or a foreign degree deemed equivalent to a doctoral degree. This qualification requirement must be fulfilled no later than at the time of the decision about scholarship recipient. Priority should be given to candidates who completed their doctoral degree, according to what is stipulated in the paragraph above, no later than three years prior. If there are special reasons, candidates who completed their doctoral degree before that may also be eligible. Special reasons include absence due to illness, parental leave, appointments of trust in trade union organisations, military service or similar circumstances, as well as clinical practice or other forms of appointment/assignment relevant to the subject area. Applicants must have earned a PhD in Artificial Intelligence or a subject relevant for the position, such as, computer science, or cognitive science. Strong research merits and excellent publications in the area of the position are required. Proficiency in English, both spoken and written, is required. Additionally, the postdoctoral candidate should submit a research plan outlining their research interests in relation to the project. The candidate is expected to have expertise in artificial intelligence, in particular human-agent interaction, collaboration and teaming, as well as user modelling, as demonstrated by publications and other scientific output. Ideal candidates are research driven, organized, and interested in addressing challenging problems and contribute to innovative solutions. Demonstrated skills in formal methods, machine learning, neurosymbolic programming, multi-agent systems and computational argumentation are meriting. Application The application should be written in English or Swedish, and attached documents should be in Word or PDF format. The application should be registered via Umeå University’s e-recruitment system Varbi and submitted by the deadline 27 November, 2026. A full application should include: Cover letter describing your research interests relative to the above topics and why why your expertise is appropriate for the scholarship, A research plan (no more than three pages, references excluded) that outlines research interest in relation to the scholarship. The research plan should be written in English. Curriculum vitae (CV) including a complete list of scientific publications, Verified copy of doctoral degree certificate or documentation that clarifies when the degree of doctor is expected to be obtained, Verified copies of other diplomas, list of completed academic courses and grades, Copy of doctoral thesis and maximum 5 original research publications relevant to the above topics, numbered according to the publication list, Other documents that the applicant wishes to claim. Contact information to two persons willing to act as references. Further information For further information, please contact Prof. Helena Lindgren helena.lindgren@umu.se Welcome with your application! We look forward to receiving your application! Not funded by a EU programme Reference Number 2026-10663 Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description The position will be hosted at Inria Centre at Université de Lorraine . The Research Engineer will work in close collaboration with the coordinators of PILOT: Myriam Lewkowicz, Claudia Ignat, and François Charoy . The PILOT project is recruiting a Research Engineer to contribute to the design and implementation of a repository dedicated to long-term collaboration. The position is part of the French PEPR eNSEMBLE research program, funded by France 2030, which aims to redefine digital collaboration through sociotechnical models and interoperable, secure, and sovereign collaborative platforms. PILOT, one of the 5 targeted projects of PEPR eNSEMBLE, focuses on practices and infrastructures for long-term collaboration. It draws on emerging work practices, technological opportunities, regulatory change, and organizational contexts to design socio-technical systems that support sustainable collaboration over time. Useful links: - PEPR eNSEMBLE website: https://www.pepr-ensemble.fr - PILOT project page: https://www.pepr-ensemble.fr/en/pilot-practices-and-infrastructures-for-long-term-collaboration/pepr-ensemble The Research Engineer will play a central role, particularly for Axis 1 “Understanding current and future forms of long-term collaboration,” by designing, developing, and maintaining a repository of up-to-date analyses, use cases, and reports on emerging forms of long-term collaboration, including their challenges and limitations. This repository is intended as a living resource to support reflexivity, comparison, and concept building, and to provide a foundation for the project’s later work on guidelines, tools, and visions. The repository will be developed as a structured and sustainable resource gathering analyses, empirical cases, reports, and other project outputs relevant to long-term distributed collaboration. It is intended to serve as a national and international reference point for researchers, managers, policymakers, and other organizations seeking resources to support long-term collaboration (Li et al., 2021; Randall et al., 2018; Wulf et al., 2015). References Li, Q., Tolmie, P., Weibert, A., Schorch, M., Müller, M., and Wulf, V. (2021). “E-Portfolio: value tensions encountered in documenting design case studies.” Ethics and Information Technology 23(1), 89–93. DOI: 10.1007/s10676-020-09533-3. (2018). “Research into design-research practices: Supporting an agenda towards self-reflectivity and transferability.” In V. Wulf, V. Pipek, D. Randall, M. Rohde, K. Schmidt, & G. Stevens (Eds.), Socioinformatics - A practice-based perspective on the design and use of IT artefacts (pp. 491–540). Oxford: Oxford University Press. Wulf, V., Müller, C., Pipek, V., Randall, D., Rohde, M., & Stevens, G. (2015). “Practice-based computing: Empirically grounded conceptualizations derived from design case studies.” In Designing socially embedded technologies in the real-world (pp. 111–150). London: Springer. Design and implement the repository, including its overall structure, content organization, and technical architecture. Collect, formalize, curate, and integrate project outputs such as analyses, use cases, reports, demonstrators, and related documentation. Define metadata, classification schemes, and content management workflows to support comparison, navigation, reuse, and long-term maintenance of the repository. Work closely with the researchers involved in Axis 1 and with the broader PILOT consortium to ensure the scientific relevance and usability of the repository. Contribute to the dissemination and valorization of project results through documentation, presentations, and exchanges with project partners and stakeholders. Help ensure the repository’s accessibility, coherence, sustainability, and alignment with the broader ambitions of PILOT and PEPR eNSEMBLE. description: 3 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Delft University of Technology (TU Delft) Research Field Engineering » Mechanical engineering Engineering » Precision engineering Physics » Acoustics Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 29 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Develop innovative ultrasound technology to measure the viscosity of flowing fluids in real time. Work closely with the University of Twente and leading industry partners to advance more efficient industrial processes, reduce waste and enable more precise medical applications. Job description Many industrial and medical processes rely on accurate, continuous measurements of fluid properties, such as flow rate and viscosity. These measurements are essential in the production of food, medicines and semiconductor products, as well as in environmental monitoring and medical infusion systems for neonatal care. Reliable, real-time measurements provide immediate insight into processes, helping manufacturers maintain product quality, detect deviations and prevent waste caused by production errors. In this way, better fluid measurement contributes to more efficient manufacturing, improved healthcare and sustainable food production. In this PhD project, you will develop innovative, modular and scalable flowmeters that measure both flow rate and viscosity using ultrasonic surface acoustic wave (SAW) sensing. Although SAW-based sensing principles are already known, the mechanisms behind viscosity measurements are not yet fully understood or commercially applied in ultrasonic flowmeters. Your research will help establish the principles needed for accurate, quantitative measurements. You will work at TU Delft in close collaboration with the University of Twente and leading companies in flow sensing. Combining theoretical modelling with experimental research, you will investigate how ultrasonic waves interact with flowing fluids and translate your findings into new measurement strategies and sensor designs. Your responsibilities As a PhD-researcher you will: Investigating ultrasonic sensing principles and the relationship between fluid flow, viscosity and surface acoustic waves. Developing novel measurement strategies for quantitatively determining the viscosity of flowing fluids. Building a model of the sensing principles and validating it through experiments. Designing and developing an experimental platform for ultrasound-based sensing. Characterising propagation losses, quality factors, wave travel speeds and resonance behaviour. Identifying optimal excitation frequencies to improve measurement accuracy and signal-to-noise ratio. Publishing your findings in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at international conferences and writing your PhD thesis. Contributing to education, for example by supervising MSc students. Your work environment You’ll be part of the Dynamics of Micro and Nanosystems (DMN) section within department of Precision and Microsystems Engineering (PME) of the faculty of Mechanical Engineering . The section studies and develops small-scale systems that move, aiming to better understand their physical properties and use this knowledge to drive future innovations. Its research combines fundamental scientific investigation with close collaboration with industry. You’ll have access to several research facilities that will support your research. At DMN, you'll find an open and friendly environment, with opportunities for professional development and training to successfully develop your academic skills. We do not distinguish between hierarchical levels, and we have a strong collaborative culture. We interact daily and share a drive to strengthen the position of the group as a whole thanks to the growth of each member. Job requirements You have a master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science or a related discipline. You have experience with modelling, experimental research and design. Preferably you have a background in fluid dynamics and/or acoustics. You enjoy working collaboratively and communicate effectively with colleagues and research partners. You are creative, curious and able to approach complex research challenges independently. You are self-motivated and take initiative in setting up, organising and carrying out research. You have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Mechanical Engineering From chip to ship. From machine to human being. From idea to solution. Driven by a deep-rooted desire to understand our environment and discover its underlying mechanisms, research and education at the ME faculty focusses on fundamental understanding, design, production including application and product improvement, materials, processes and (mechanical) systems. ME is a dynamic and innovative faculty with high-tech lab facilities and international reach. It’s a large faculty but also versatile, so we can often make unique connections by combining different disciplines. This is reflected in ME’s outstanding, state-of-the-art education, which trains students to become responsible and socially engaged engineers and scientists. We translate our knowledge and insights into solutions to societal issues, contributing to a sustainable society and to the development of prosperity and well-being. That is what unites us in pioneering research, inspiring education and (inter)national cooperation. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. Do you want to experience working at our faculty? These videos will introduce you to some of our researchers and their work. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204- €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service , offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information For more information about this vacancy, please contact Dr. G.J. (Gerard) Verbiest ( G.J.Verbiest@tudelft.nl ). Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 29th of November 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: A cover letter in which you describe your motivation and specific qualifications for this position (max 1 page). No Offer Description Within the framework of the European project EU-LAC Supercomputing Network for AI (Team Europe Initiative "EU-LAC Digital Alliance"), coordinated by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC), in collaboration with INESC TEC (Portugal), FZJ (Germany), CSC (Finland), IZUM (Slovenia) and CINECA (Italy). This project aims at strengthening cooperation between Europe and Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) in high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence. Inria leads the work package on joint EU-LAC use cases and, more specifically, Use Case 1: a unified methodology for tracing HPC/AI applications and monitoring their performance and energy consumption. This methodology provides the common basis for the other use cases of the project (e.g. large language models adapted to Latin American language varieties, or earthquake and tsunami simulation) and will be deployed in LAC HPC centres selected through an open call. Occasional travel in Europe and Latin America (project meetings, workshops, visits to partner centres) is expected. The recruited person will be responsible for designing and implementing a methodology and an open-source toolkit to collect, store and process HPC/AI application and system traces, with a particular focus on energy consumption (CPU/GPU power draw, node-level energy counters), I/O behavior and resource utilization. This characterization will rely on existing tools wherever possible, such as profiling tools (Darshan, Tau), tracing tools (Recorder), energy measurement interfaces (RAPL, NVML) and the IOPS experiment orchestration framework developed in the team, complemented by the components needed for portable deployment across European and Latin American HPC infrastructures. In addition to that, the person will be responsible for instrumenting the executions of the other use cases of the project and providing them with performance and energy dashboards (time-to-solution, resource utilization, I/O pressure, carbon footprint). They will work with the leads of the other use cases (BSC, CINECA) and with the system administrators of the participating HPC centres, in particular the Latin American centres selected through the open call, whom they will support in adopting the methodology. Finally, the expected results are the toolkit and dashboards, a methodology guide (including GDPR-aligned data anonymization and governance), and a public repository of anonymized traces. IPDPS 2025, Milan, Italy. https://hal.science/hal-04887809 - IOPS (Integrated Orchestration for Parametric Studies), a benchmark orchestration framework developed in the team: https://gitlab.inria.fr/lgouveia/iops Main activities: Studying the state of the art and existing tools for tracing, profiling and energy measurement on HPC systems; Development of the pipeline for collecting, storing and processing traces (energy, performance, I/O, resource utilization) and its open-source release; Running applications and benchmarks on HPC systems using scripts, treating and plotting results; Deployment of performance and energy dashboards for the other use cases of the project; Supporting Latin American HPC centres in adopting the methodology. Additional activities: Writing the methodology guide, reports and research papers (LaTeX); Curating the public repository of anonymized traces (Zenodo or equivalent).
