description: 10 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Luleå University of Technolgoy Research Field Engineering Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 30 Nov 2026 - 12:00 (UTC) Country Sweden Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Are you ready to take the next step in your academic journey? As a doctoral student with us, you will work closely with leading researchers in a strong, international research environment, with access to advanced laboratory equipment and solid funding opportunities. You will be offered secure employment, high-quality supervision, and room to grow, both as a researcher and as a person. The Urban Water Engineering research group at the Department of Civil, Environmental and Natural resources engineering at Luleå University of Technology seeks a driven and committed PhD student to investigate how smart monitoring and predictive modelling can support more effective and environmentally sustainable maintenance of urban drainage infrastructure. The research focuses on understanding sediment accumulation through sensor-based monitoring and data analysis, contributing to improved water quality and urban flood resilience. Take the opportunity to join one of the world’s leading stormwater research groups with an international, creative and dynamic environment and close cooperation with the industry and universities worldwide. The Urban Water Engineering research group has a strong position in research and education on urban water systems, primarily stormwater, small-scale wastewater and sewage systems. The group consists of about 50 members including senior researchers, Swedish and international adjunct professors and about 20 doctoral students. The group has an extensive national and international collaboration network. The group's overall goal is to contribute to the development of sustainable urban water systems. More information on www.ltu.se/water Subject description Urban Water Engineering encompasses the entire urban water system (storm drains, drinking water supply and wastewater) with respect to collection, transport and treatment, as well as organisation and planning. The research aims to encourage a strong economy, clean environment and the wise use of resources, while preserving the public’s health and safety. Project description Stormwater transports a wide range of pollutants from urban environments to receiving waters, posing major challenges for the protection of surface waters and coastal ecosystems. Urban drainage infrastructures, such as gully pots and stormwater ponds, play a critical role by retaining sediments and associated contaminants. However, their performance depends on effective operation and maintenance (O&M), which in practice is often reactive or based on fixed schedules, despite large spatial and temporal variability in sediment accumulation. This PhD project is part of a larger interdisciplinary research initiative aiming to enable a transition towards more data-driven and environmentally responsible maintenance of urban drainage infrastructures. The overall goal is to reduce pollutant loads to coastal and marine environments while supporting sustainable urban water management. The PhD research will focus on developing a data-driven understanding of sediment accumulation processes in urban drainage infrastructures. This includes long-term monitoring using high-resolution sensors to capture sediment dynamics across rainfall events and seasons. Based on these data, predictive models will be developed to estimate sediment accumulation and infrastructure’s remaining functionality. The results will support more effective maintenance strategies by identifying when and where maintenances are needed to maximise environmental performance and operational efficiency. Within this project, the doctoral student will be involved in collaboration with stakeholders in the water and wastewater industry and will communicate results both with the industry and international researchers through LTU's well-established competence network. Duties As a PhD student, you will perform both experimental and theoretical work. You will learn how to collect and analyse scientific data within your research area as well as communicate your results at national and international conferences and in scientific journals. Most of your working time will be devoted to your own research studies, including both research and coursework. In addition, you will also carry out departmental duties, such as teaching and/or assisting in other research projects. You will have two or three supervisors who support you in your work. The research work for this project will specifically include experimental work. Qualifications We seek a candidate with an MSc degree or equivalent or fully completed course requirements of at least 240 ETCS of which at least 60 ETCS are at an advanced level or equivalent. The degree should be within the field of water and environment, environmental engineering, natural resources engineering, civil engineering, or equivalent. Specific knowledge of stormwater management, hydraulics/hydrology, statistics, machine learning, thermodynamics (e.g. heat transfer processes) and programming, as well as experience of sensor-based monitoring, are meritorious. Other important skills are the ability to work independently and take initiative, as well as being able to explore new research areas. English language skills are required since the results will be presented internationally in scientific journals and at conferences. Swedish/Scandinavian language skills are beneficial, as they will facilitate communication with stakeholders and participation in teaching activities. Having a driver’s license is meritorious, as it will facilitate research work. Applicants should provide contact details to minimum two reference persons upon request. For further information about a specific subject see: * General syllabus for the Board of the faculty of science and technology Further information Employment as a PhD student is limited to 4 years, teaching and other department duties may be added to that time with max 20%. Placement: Luleå. Starting: Spring 2027. For each position, a preliminary salary range is provided based on the requirements, responsibilities, and market conditions associated with the role. For further information about the position, please contact Postdoctoral researcher Haoyu Wei, 0920-491728, haoyu.wei@ltu.se Union representatives In case of different interpretations of the English and Swedish versions of this announcement, the Swedish version takes precedence. description: The Erlangen Center for Interface Research and Catalysis (ECRC) at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen–Nürnberg (FAU) invites applications for a PhD student position to join the group of Prof. Jörg Libuda. The position focuses on in situ and operando studies on real and model catalysts for highly selective (de)functionalization reactions. In particular, the role of catalytic modifiers, additives, and activation procedures will be elucidated to establish structure-property relationships. In situ and operando infrared spectroscopy (DRIFTS, PM-IRAS) will be a key component of the experimental toolbox. Where appropriate, additional techniques such as microscopy methods (scanning tunneling microscopy, atomic force microscopy) may be employed as well . description: A PhD position (3 years, with possible extension) is available immediately in the evolutionary genomics group of Henrik Kaessmann at Heidelberg University. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. We are seeking a highly qualified, motivated, and enthusiastic candidate with a keen interest in evolutionary questions and a passion and aptitude for experimental molecular/genomics work, computational/bioinformatics analyses, or both. Projects in our lab usually combine experimental and computational components, with the relative emphasis tailored to the specific project and the candidate’s interests and expertise. Our lab investigates a broad range of questions related to the origins and molecular evolution of organs in mammals and other vertebrates and the underlying genomic changes, with a particular focus on the evolution of gene expression and its regulatory basis (see home.kaessmannlab.org and zmbh.uni-heidelberg.de/kaessmann for more information). As part of this research, we have generated extensive comparative genomics datasets (e.g., single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) across species, based on samples from our unique organ collections, and analyzed them using state-of-the-art bioinformatics approaches, increasingly incorporating AI and deep learning (see, e.g., Sarropoulos et al., Science 2026). This work has provided insights into the origins and functional evolution of protein-coding genes, alternative splicing, long noncoding RNAs, microRNAs, and sex chromosomes across organs and species, as well as their phenotypic implications. We currently offer a range of possible projects addressing the evolution of gene expression and its regulatory basis across expression layers, organs, and species in mammals and other vertebrates. These projects will combine the generation of unique new datasets using cutting-edge experimental approaches (e.g., long-read spatial transcriptomics) across diverse organs, from the brain to the gonads, with state-of-the-art computational and deep-learning approaches. Projects may also include detailed molecular and functional characterization of particularly exciting candidate evolutionary changes using organoid and mouse models, CRISPR-based approaches, and synthetic genomics, supported by the expertise and infrastructure of our local Center for Synthetic Genomics ( www.syn-gen.de ). Specific projects will be developed together with the successful candidates based on their individual interests, expertise, and skills. In our lab, we place great importance on a collaborative, supportive, and positive team spirit. Many of our projects are driven by small, closely interacting teams of experimental and computational researchers who combine complementary expertise and work together enthusiastically. We also greatly value the diverse cultural and international backgrounds of our lab members, which contribute to an open and enriching research environment. The working language of our institute is English, and its members form a highly international community. The ZMBH is located in Heidelberg, a picturesque and vibrant international city on the Neckar River and at the edge of the Odenwald forest. Heidelberg offers an exceptionally stimulating and collaborative research environment, with the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL), German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), Heidelberg Institute for Theoretical Studies (HITS), and Max Planck Institute for Medical Research located in close proximity to the University. For more information about our group and the institute more generally, please visit our website at the ZMBH ( http://www.zmbh.uni-heidelberg.de/Kaessmann/ ). Please submit a CV, a statement of research interests, and the names and contact details of three references to Henrik Kaessmann ( h.kaessmann@zmbh.uni-heidelberg.de ).

The Hurford Youth Fellows Program equips emerging democracy leaders from around the world with the skills, networks, and practical tools to turn youth energy into democratic change. Over the course of four months in Washington, D.C., fellows explore new ideas, initiatives, and innovations, share experiences and lessons learned with activists from other countries, and contribute to the global youth movement for democracy. The International Forum for Democratic Studies at the National Endowment for Democracy (NED) invites emerging youth leaders from around the world to apply for the 2027 Hurford Youth Fellows Program in Washington, DC. Fellowship Dates and Selection: Up to three (3) fellows will be selected for a four-month fellowship, from May 1 through August 31, 2027 . Eligibility Requirements Applicants must be 30 years of age or younger and demonstrate a commitment to—and experience in—advancing youth participation in democracy. Applications are especially encouraged from leaders affiliated with civic organizations, human rights groups, and initiatives working to strengthen democracy. Fellowship Project: Fellows pursue a project addressing a democratic challenge in their country or region and its implications for young people. Projects may explore the political, social, economic, legal, or cultural dimensions of democracy and draw on a range of methods and innovative approaches. They should reflect applicants’ interests and expertise. A study of, or comparison with, democracy in the United States is not expected. In consultation with Fellowships staff and other NED colleagues, fellows develop a tailored plan of action focused on a key challenge, such as countering authoritarian influence, navigating the opportunities and risks of digital technology, or translating youth mobilization into democratic gains. Their work should identify practical approaches and explore how lessons from one context might apply elsewhere. Fellows participate in seminars, roundtables, field trips, and other activities that help them: learn about NED and its core institutes explore pressing challenges and new approaches to advancing democracy connect with government, civil society, academic, and media communities in Washington and beyond build relationships and exchange ideas with other fellows. Financial Support: Each fellow receives a monthly stipend for living expenses, basic health insurance coverage, and roundtrip economy-class travel to and from Washington, D.C., at the beginning and end of the fellowship. description: 95 Application Deadline: November 30th, 2026 Applications are now open for the 2026 FAO Innovation Beyond the Buzzword Video Challenge. At the heart of the challenge are the five types of innovation identified in the FAO Science and Innovation Strategy: technological, social, policy, institutional and financial innovation . FAO’s Office of Innovation invites students, young professionals and creatives from around the world to take part in Innovation Beyond the Buzzword , a global video challenge to make the ideas and approaches behind agrifood innovation easier to understand, more accessible and relevant to a broad audience. Your challenge is to take an idea related to agrifood innovation and bring it to life through a short, engaging and thought-provoking video . We are looking for creative ways to unpack how innovation works, what enables it, what challenges conventional thinking and how different approaches can contribute to more efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems. You do not need to be an innovation expert. What matters is your curiosity, creativity and ability to make complex ideas understandable and meaningful. WHAT COULD YOUR VIDEO EXPLORE? When farmers become innovators : What can we learn from solutions developed by farmers and local communities, and how does this challenge conventional ideas about who drives innovation? When technology meets reality : What makes a new technology genuinely useful, accessible and capable of addressing real needs? When people innovate together : Why can collaboration between farmers, researchers, entrepreneurs, businesses and institutions lead to solutions that none could develop alone? When the rules need to change : How can policies, regulations and incentives enable new ways of doing things? When good ideas struggle to grow : Why do promising innovations sometimes fail to reach those who need them, and what kinds of support, skills and connections can help? When financing opens new possibilities : How can different financing approaches make it possible to test, adopt and scale innovative solutions? When innovation raises difficult questions : How can we ensure that innovation is responsible, inclusive and beneficial to those who need it most? When we imagine different futures : How can exploring possible future challenges help us make better decisions and innovate today? Creative and technical guidance The proposed video should: be designed for a maximum duration of 3 minutes ; use a horizontal (landscape) format ; communicate the selected concept in a way that is clear, engaging and accessible to non-specialist audiences ; connect the innovation concept to an agrifood systems context ; use an original creative approach, which may include live action, animation, motion graphics, illustration, mixed media or other visual formats; At the proposal stage, applicants do not need to produce the final video . Technical and production specifications for shortlisted concepts will be further discussed and refined with FAO during Phase 2. Format and technical requirements for the video Video length : Under 3 minutes. Format : Horizontal (landscape) orientation. Resolution : Full HD (1920 × 1080) or higher is recommended. Audio : Clear and good-quality audio, where applicable. Style : Live action, animation, motion graphics, illustration, mixed media or other creative visual formats are welcome. Accessibility : The content should be clear and engaging for a broad, non-specialist audience. Agrifood context : The selected idea or approach should be illustrated or connected to an agrifood systems context. Originality : visual and audio materials should be original or used with the appropriate permissions and rights. File size : maximum 500 MB. Benefits Selected participants will benefit from direct engagement with FAO experts, receive technical and creative feedback, and gain visibility across FAO channels, reaching broader audiences within the global agrifood innovation community and beyond. Your creativity can help people see innovation differently — not as an abstract buzzword, but as a way to rethink challenges, develop new approaches and create meaningful change. How to apply Please send your proposal to [email protected] by 30 November 2026, using the following subject line: Innovation Video Challenge – [Your first and last name] Please include in your email: Your first and last name ; A short bio or background ; Your creative proposal ; Your storyboard or visual treatment ; A link or attachment to previous work or portfolio material , if available. Selection process Applications will be reviewed based on: Creativity and originality of the proposal; Ability to communicate an idea or approach related to innovation in a clear, engaging and accessible way ; Relevance to agrifood systems ; Clarity and feasibility of the proposed visual approach ; Potential to engage a broad and non-specialist audience . Video Challenge timeline Submission deadline : 30 November 2026 Co-creation and refinement (with shortlisted applicants) : December–February 2027 Final selection, showcase & publication : Early 2027 For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the FAO Innovation Beyond the Buzzword Video Challenge

description: 12 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Itä-Suomen yliopisto Department The Faculty of Health Sciences, School of Pharmacy Research Field Pharmacological sciences » Pharmacy Chemistry Biological sciences Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 30 Nov 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Finland Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description The University of Eastern Finland invites applications for a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) (MSCA-DN) position as part of the PANDORA on discovering Pathomechanisms and Novel Drug Optimization for AMD (Age-Related Macular Degeneration) in part of the Doctoral Network of the European Commission. The position is based on the Kuopio campus, and it is expected to begin no later than 1 February 2027. The position is full-time and will be filled for a fixed term of three years. Read more below and submit your application no later than 30 November 2026. Title, role and research theme We are seeking for a motivated Doctoral Researcher (PhD student) (MSCA-DN) to develop and test various intravitreal drug formulations for targeted drug delivery to the retina. The drug compounds will be obtained from partners in the consortium. The aim is to generate long-acting, safe and stable drug formulation for intravitreal injections. The Doctoral Researcher will generate hydrogel and nanoformulations for prolonged ocular retention and drug release and use advanced physico-chemical methods and cell cultures. utilize cutting-edge techniques: Physico-chemical methods for manufacturing and characterization of drug delivery systems (e.g. microfluidics, nanoparticle tracking analyses, rheological methods) Cell culture methods (e.g. test of cell toxicity and drug potency) Experimental pharmacokinetics (e.g. animal experiments, quantitative LC-MS/MS analytics) Computational modeling (e.g. pharmacokinetic data analysis and simulations). Recent open access research publications from UEF laboratory related to this position: Thermoresponsive hydrogel for long-acting delivery of structurally intact and biologically active Fab fragment and monoclonal antibody - PubMed Novel in vitro model for intravitreal drug dissolution and release studies of small molecules and their long-acting formulations - PubMed Sustained intravitreal dissolution and kinase inhibition by an inhibitory cGMP analogue after its injection as a suspension of a poorly soluble salt - PubMed Barcode lipids for absolute quantitation of liposomes in ocular tissues - PubMed Imaging, quantitation and kinetic modelling of intravitreal nanomaterials - PubMed Ocular pharmacokinetic studies involve experimental studies with rodents and rabbits as well as computational curve fitting and simulations. Overall, the position will provide state-of-the art training in drug delivery using modern methodologies. The results of this research will pave way towards effective treatments in age-related macular degeneration (AMD). In this position, you will be working in the School of Pharmacy at the Faculty of Health Science. This position is a part of the PANDORA ( pathomechanisms and novel drug optimization for AMD ) Doctoral Network of the European Commission. The project aims to test multiple therapies including complement inhibition, anti-oxidants, anti-inflammatory drugs and mitochondria modulators. The results will help design new therapeutic approaches. The PhD candidate will benefit from a network of European experts in different fields (gene therapy, pharmacology, bioinformatics, disease modeling, imaging) and will have the possibility to visit other labs in secondments (lab exchanges). The main duty of the Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) is to conduct research for their doctoral dissertation and to complete postgraduate studies. The total working time is 1,612 hours per year. At the time of signing the employment contract, the recruited researcher must be enrolled in the UEF Doctoral Programme of Health Sciences, which leads to the award of a doctoral degree. Admission to the doctoral programme requires a research plan, which the selected candidate will prepare in collaboration with their supervisors shortly after being accepted to PANDORA. The person appointed to the Doctoral Researcher position will be admitted to the Doctoral Programme in Health Science . Employment relationship and salary The position will be filled for a fixed term of three years, starting on 1 February 2027 at the latest. The position will be filled for a fixed term due to it pertaining to a specific project and own doctoral degree. A trial period is applied to all new members of staff. The salary of the position is based on the salary system of MSCA. The salary consists of living and mobility allowances. The mobility allowance covers additional, private mobility-related costs (e.g., travel and accommodation costs); professional moblility costs under the action are excluded and are covered by the research, training, and networking contribution. If the recruited doctoral candidate has or acquires family obligations during the action duration, i.e., persons linked to them by (i) marriage, or (ii) a relationship with equivalent status to a marriage recognised by the legislation of the country or region where this relationship was formalised; or (iii) dependent children who are actually being maintained by the researcher, the family allowance will be paid as well. The gross salary in this position will be approximately EUR 4,390 per month for the three years, including the mobility allowance (or approximately EUR 4,940, if eligible for the family allowance). Our requirements and expectations Requirements: a Master’s (or equivalent) degree in life sciences or chemistry (pharmacy, cell biology, polymer chemistry or closely related fields) Excellence in oral and written English, with good presentation skills High motivation with interest in retinal pharmacology and drug delivery Work effectively both independently and as part of a team Knowledge of cellular biology, eye biology and/or pharmacology Hands on experience in quantitative chemical analyses and biological research. Background in animal experiments, biomaterial/nanomedicine and computational pharmacology are benefits. Mobility requirement: The Applicant shall not have resided or carried out his/her main activity (work, studies etc.) in Finland for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date (unless as part of a compulsory national service or a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention). shall not already be in possession of a doctoral degree (*). can be of any nationality. *researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will not be considered eligible Your benefits You will have access to the university’s staff benefits, including the opportunity for flexible multi-location work excellent opportunities for professional development and continuous learning extensive occupational health care a broad selection of staff training staff discount on lunch in our campus restaurants, as well as on a range of other services affordable sports services Please read more in the Work at UEF section on our website . You will have an opportunity to work in an interesting, meaningful and diverse role as part of our international, creative, participatory and inclusive academic community. Enjoy your life in Finland! Known for its cleanliness, welfare know-how, modern technology and superb education system, Finland is an exotic and safe country to work in. Please visit the Life in Finland section on our website to learn more. How to apply? Submit your application by using our electronic application form no later than 30 November 2026 by 23:59 (midnight) Finnish time (UTC+2). Please note that you must include the following appendices in your application: A CV (max. 3 pages) ( Template for CV, TENK website ) Copies of your Bachelor’s and Master’s degree certificates and the proof of English proficiency if not evident from academic credentials Copies of a transcript of records of your Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees A copy of your Master’s thesis and any other publications (if available) A motivation letter (max. 1 page), which contains a brief description of why the applicant wishes to become a PhD student within PANDORA Two written recommendation letters (for example, one from the supervisor of the applicant’s Master’s thesis), including the contact details of the referees Other documents to demonstrate the applicant’s merits for the position If your degree certificate is not in English, you must provide official English translations of your degree certificate documents. All translations must be issued by the awarding educational institution or an authorized translator. Each page of the official translation must bear the translator’s stamp and/or signature. Official translations must be accurate translations of the original documents. Translations made by the applicants themselves will not be accepted. Questions? For more information on the PANDORA Doctoral Network, please visit their website . For further information on the position, please contact Professor Arto Urtti, e-mail: arto.urtti@uef.fi . For further information on the application procedure, please contact ttvarbi@uef.fi School of Pharmacy at University of Eastern Finland is an internationally recognized centre in pharmaceutical research. Ocular drug research is one of the spearhead fields at the university, involving activity of seven distinct research groups in the field. The institution is particularly renowned as a leading centre for ocular drug delivery research. At Kuopio Campus we offer a scientific environment that favors creativity for generating groundbreaking ideas, their transfer into reality and their translation towards therapeutics to help patients with impaired vision. The candidate will have the opportunity to interact with other labs and he/she will get exposure to an array of relevant pharmaceutical and biomedical techniques. We offer modern, state-of the art laboratories, facilities, and equipment, as well as participation in training activities of the international and inter-sectorial PANDORA network. We also promote participation in national and international conferences. Where to apply Website https://uef.varbi.com/en/what:job/jobID:988006/type:job/where:39/apply:1 Requirements Research Field Pharmacological sciences Education Level Master Degree or equivalent Research Field Chemistry Education Level Master Degree or equivalent Research Field Biological sciences Education Level Master Degree or equivalent Research Field Pharmacological sciences Years of Research Experience None Research Field Chemistry Years of Research Experience None Research Field Biological sciences Years of Research Experience None Additional Information Work Location(s) Number of offers available 1 Company/Institute Itä-Suomen yliopisto Country Finland City Kuopio Contact City Kuopio Website https://www.uef.fi/en STATUS: EXPIRED Apply now Share this page

The program also provides training in transferable skills and offers financial support for research and conference travel. Doctoral researchers in the Class of Language can further take advantage of the Graduate School’s strong interdisciplinary environment, which includes the Class of Language Education, the Class of Literature, and the Class of Culture and History. For the summer semester 2027, the Class of Language (Graduate School Language & Literature, LMU Munich) invites applications for one funded doctoral position (TV-L E13, 50%; expected start date: April 1, 2027), as well as regular unfunded doctoral program places. Applicants who are admitted but not awarded a scholarship will receive active support in applying for external doctoral funding. Application deadline: December 1, 2026 Further information and access to the online application portal are available at: https://www.en.lipp.uni-muenchen.de/application/index.html Contact: Dr. Markus Wiefarn wiefarn@lrz.uni-muenchen.de

description: APPLICATION PROCESS General information on the application Join a unique research network at the intersection of artificial intelligence and biomedicine. Applications are open annually from September 1 to December 1. Requirements The MPS of BMAI welcomes applications from exceedingly bright and motivated students holding a Master’s degree in computer science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, physics , or the life sciences with a strong computational component in their bachelor's and master's education. Your complete application needs to be submitted through our online application portal from September 1 to December 1, 2026 . Applications by email cannot be accepted. The PhD program starts in September 2027. APPLY HERE For the application, please prepare the following documents: Certificates and transcript of Bachelor’s degree (B. Sc. or equivalent) Certificates or proof of current enrollment and transcript of Master’s degree (M. Sc. or equivalent; experience does not count as an equivalent) Copy of your passport or identity card Academic curriculum vitae Motivation letter Names of up to three potential supervisors from the list of Max Planck School of BMAI fellows Contact details of two referees for recommendations. Note: Recommendations must be submitted by December 10. Non-native English-speaking applicants must provide evidence of their English language proficiency (further details can be found in the FAQs) Selection process Application screening : BMAI Fellows review academic transcripts, CVs, personal statements, and recommendations to identify a shortlist of candidates (December – January). Only applications submitted through the portal can be considered. Scientific interviews : Shortlisted candidates present their previous research and future plans to a panel of AI and biomedical Fellows. Interviews assess scientific excellence, creativity, analytical thinking, and the ability to work across disciplines (January – March). Final matching : Successful candidates are matched to a PhD project and a dual-supervision team based on scientific excellence, motivation, and research interests (March - April). For additional information, please check out the Schools program and FAQ section . If there are any additional questions, please contact the BMAI coordination team by email. We are happy to help you!

No Offer Description Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences, Center of Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence at Tilburg University (TiU) is looking for an enthusiastic new colleague in the domains of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. The postdoc will contribute to the research project “Advancing Research in Palliative Care: Employing Rich Pictures”, a collaboration between Tilburg University, Amsterdam UMC and Amsta Nursing Home. In this project, you will collaborate with prof. dr. Hanneke van Laarhoven, head of the Department of Medical Oncology at Amsterdam UMC and her team. Little is known about the existential concerns of patients in the palliative phase of life. Discussing one's life in this phase can be difficult for patients. Visual aids, like 'Rich Pictures' (RPs), can facilitate this and bring to light concerns that might not otherwise be discussed. RPs can also illustrate changes over time, for instance, after an intervention. Thus, they can also serve as a new research instrument. However, RP analysis is highly labor-intensive and challenging due to the variability in drawing styles, the numerous elements and their complex relationships, and the implicit meanings of specific symbols. By accelerating RP analysis with AI, RPs can also be used as a measurement tool in large-scale research and clinical practice. Your position The postdoc will play a key role in the research team. The key responsibilities include: Extend, develop, and refine AI methods and tools to support the analysis and interpretation of Rich Pictures (RPs). Adapt and improve a user-friendly interface that makes the AI tools accessible to researchers and healthcare professionals. Collaborate closely with humanities researchers and healthcare professionals at Amsterdam UMC and other project partners. Publish research findings in scientific journals and present results at national and international conferences. Where to apply Website https://www.academictransfer.com/en/jobs/365224/postdoctoral-researcher-in-ai-f… Requirements Specific Requirements We understand that no candidate will meet every single requirement. In your application, tell us not only about the qualifications you bring but also about the areas you are eager to develop further and how you envision doing so. We welcome applications from candidates of all genders, ethnicities, backgrounds, and orientations. Your profile The successful candidate should: Hold a PhD in Artificial Intelligence, Cognitive Science, Digital Humanities, Computer Science, or another relevant discipline. Have an interest in and experience with deep learning, computer vision, image analysis, and/or multimodal AI. Possess strong programming skills in Python and experience with relevant AI technologies, such as PyTorch and vision-language models (VLMs), as well as web development frameworks, such as Flask or Django. Have an interest in applying AI to human-centered research, healthcare, or other socially relevant domains. Be interested in working across disciplines, particularly at the intersection of AI, humanities, and healthcare. Have a good command of English, both spoken and written. Hybrid working with home working allowance (€2 p/day) and internet allowance (€25 p/month). Reimbursement sustainable commuting: walking, cycling, and public transport. Options model for additional leave, pension, a bicycle or personal training. Moving allowance (subject to conditions). 30% rule for international employees (if applicable). Pension through ABP. Ample training offer: personal development, leadership, education, research or language courses. Inclusive work culture: everyone welcome, equal opportunities. description: 5 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Delft University of Technology (TU Delft) Research Field Engineering » Design engineering Engineering » Systems engineering Political sciences » Public policy Sociology » Urban sociology Sociology » Social shaping of technology Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 1 Dec 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description We seek a participatory design researcher who can make questions of justice, data rights and shared stewardship concrete in the design and operation of energy data infrastructures. Job Description The Delft University of Technology is hiring a doctoral candidate on the subject of "Energy data sharing for city-level policy making using digital twins". The PhD position is a part of the FEDERATE NWO project. Energy data can help communities, municipalities and grid operators make better decisions about the energy transition. Yet people and organisations who contribute data may have little insight into how it is used, limited influence over the terms of sharing, or no clear way to benefit from the resulting decisions. FEDERATE, aims developing ways to share data across energy systems and digital twins while addressing these questions of trust, power and justice. We are looking for a PhD candidate to lead the research in Work Package 2: Participatory Data Governance for Equitable and Transparent Data-Sharing Processes of the FEDERATE project. You will work with residents, local organisations, municipalities, grid operators and technology partners to design and test governance arrangements that make data sharing understandable, negotiable and accountable. Your research will connect social and organisational design with the technical work on data-sharing interfaces, privacy, forgetting mechanisms and interoperable digital twins. What you will do You will investigate how energy data is currently collected, shared and used, and whose needs, efforts, risks and knowledge are recognised in those processes. Through interviews, data ethnography, stakeholder and power mapping, and participatory workshops, you will build an understanding of both personal energy data and wider energy system data. Working with project partners and communities in Heiloo and Alkmaar, you will: Develop a participatory data governance framework informed by Human-Data Interaction principles of legibility, agency and negotiability, and by Energy Data Justice. Facilitate inclusive workshops with residents, businesses, public authorities and technical partners. You will use methods such as role play, serious games and scenario-based co-design to make competing interests and power differences discussable. Co-design governance roles, decision processes, data access and control arrangements, and ways for people to question, contest or revise data-sharing terms. Design and prototype social and digital interactions that help people understand data practices, join governance processes and exercise meaningful influence. This includes approaches for people who are digitally excluded or less often represented. Explore fair incentives and ways for the value created through data sharing to flow back to those who contribute data, effort or local knowledge. Develop an onboarding playbook and a practical governance and stewardship toolkit, then help test these arrangements in the project’s joint case study. Translate findings into actionable governance requirements and data rights constraints for the project’s technical researchers, while learning from what their prototypes make possible in practice. Publish your research in academic venues and share usable findings with project partners and participating communities. Job Requirements You have a master’s degree in design, human-computer interaction, social sciences, science and technology studies, public policy, information studies, or a closely related field. We welcome candidates whose work crosses these fields. You can demonstrate: Experience with qualitative or participatory research, such as interviews, ethnography, co-design or workshop facilitation. The ability to work respectfully with people who have different forms of expertise and different degrees of power, including communities affected by exclusion or vulnerability. A strong interest in data justice, energy justice, data rights, participatory governance or related approaches to equity and accountability. Design skills to turn research insights into concepts, prototypes, interactions or tools that people can examine and test together. The ability to analyse complex social and organisational settings, communicate findings clearly, and work independently as part of a multidisciplinary team. An interest in learning how data infrastructures and digital twins work, so that you can collaborate closely with technical researchers. You do not need to be a specialist in knowledge graphs, privacy engineering or software development. Spoken Dutch skills, sufficient to independently conduct interviews and facilitate inclusive, participatory workshops with local stakeholders in Heiloo and Alkmaar, including residents, neighbourhood organisations local business and policymakers. Experience in the energy transition, community engagement, data stewardship, service design or interaction design would be valuable. What matters most is your ability to connect careful justice-oriented research with practical design and collaboration across disciplines. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Industrial Design Engineering Matching the evolution of people with the speed of the revolution of technology. This is the focus of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering (IDE). Delft designers act as a bridge between advances in technology and the needs of people, organisations and society to create products, services and systems with purpose. IDE is a leader in design research across the application areas of mobility, sustainability and health, as well as its development of design tools and methods. A 350-strong research team and over 2,000 students work together in our inspiring hall, labs and studios. In close cooperation with industry, the public sector and NGOs we rehearse possible futures in research and education to design for a complex future. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service , offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information For more information about this vacancy, please contact Dr. Natalia Romero Herrera via n.a.romero@tudelft.nl Application procedure Apply via the application button and upload your CV, cover letter that details the motivation and fit to the job requirements, a list of grades of your qualify degrees (BSc, MSc). Incomplete applications will not be considered. description: 3 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Lunds universitet Department Lund University, unit for medical radiation physics Research Field Physics » Other Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 1 Dec 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Sweden Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Description of the workplace At the Department of Medical Radiation Physics, both education and research are conducted across the various fields of medical radiation physics (www.msf.lu.se/) . This project will be performed within the research group in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) (https://www.msf.lu.se/mr-physics-group) , which has its primary focus on development of new techniques for quantitative MRI utilizing different contrast mechanisms. Being a doctoral student As a doctoral student at Lund University, you are expected to complete a PhD programme, specified in your individual study plan. During your studies, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis defence and a doctoral degree. More about being a doctoral student at the Faculty of Science at naturvetenskap.se Doctoral studies | Faculty of Science Subject and project description Diffusion MRI (dMRI) measures microscopic properties in the tissue by studying random motion of water molecules. In dense tissue, diffusion is slow, while it appears to be faster in looser tissue. dMRI can therefore detect cancers that cause the tissue to be abnormally dense. However, current dMRI methods are sensitive but not very specific. This shortcoming can be remedied by controlling how the diffusion is encoded by the MRI scanner, thereby allowing us to learn more about the tissue microstructure in the living human body. For example, we aim to distinguish properties like cell density, cell shape, cell size, blood volume, and cell membrane permeability. These parameters are then evaluated as tentative imaging biomarkers for improved diagnostics or monitoring of disease. The present project will focus on developing methods for enhancing and analysing the acquired images. During your doctoral studies, you will follow the general syllabus for postgraduate education in the subject of Medical Radiation Physics: For current doctoral students | Faculty of Science Your tasks You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral education, which includes participation in research projects and writing a doctoral thesis, as well as completing third cycle courses and seminars. In consultation with you, an individual study plan for your programme will be drawn up. As a doctoral student, you will operate within the MR physics group on the development of methods for accurate and precise assessment of microstructural changes in the brain in various neurological conditions. Tasks and assignments can include image reconstruction, deep learning and programming of the actual MRI scanner. The projects require a strong mathematical foundation and well-developed programming skills. Experimental tasks and the analysis of patient data may also be included. The research projects will be reported in the form of articles submitted for publication in scientific journals, and these will constitute part of the doctoral thesis. In addition to studies, a maximum of 20 % of working time may be spent on teaching (typically by leading exercises or laboratory sessions) and other departmental work. Qualifications To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below. Admission requirements A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in medical radiation physics if the applicant has: Been awarded a degree in medical physics, or an equivalent foreign qualification, or Completed another programme of higher education providing basic eligibility for doctoral studies (240 credits), within which courses amounting to at least 60 higher education credits are directly relevant to the doctoral education, and including the completion of an independent project (master’s degree project) of at least 30 credits. Selection criteria The selection of eligible applicants will be made by taking into account the ability to benefit from the training, based on the following criteria: Results achieved in first- and second-cycle courses or the equivalent, the breadth, depth and relevance first- and second-cycle courses or the equivalent. Of particular relevance are courses in mathematics, mathematical statistics, physics, signal processing, and computational methods, the quality of the second-cycle degree project and other autonomous work, proficiency in spoken and written English, documented knowledge of medical imaging, particularly magnetic resonance imaging and diffusion MRI, documented knowledge of mathematical modelling and numerical optimisation, documented programming knowledge and programming skills and documented experience with languages such as Python, MATLAB, or equivalent, documented knowledge of methods for image processing, image registration, and image correction, documented knowledge of methods for deep learning, experience from project work in scientific or academic environments involving MRI and computational methods, personal qualities deemed to support the ability to carry out the educational components and tasks included in the doctoral education, such as independence, analytical ability, creativity, problem-solving skills, and ability to collaborate. We offer Lund University is a public authority which offers employees particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. More about working at Lund University on lu.se. h ttps://www.lunduniversity.lu.se/about-university/work-lund-university About the employment The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting 2027-01-01, or as soon as possible, according to agreement. Third cycle studies at the Faculty of Science consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§. More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staff-pages. https://www.staff.lu.se/research-and-education/research-support/doctoral-education/terms-employment-doctoral-students Other Contact person: Markus Nilsson ( markus.nilsson@med.lu.se ) Top-ranked candidates may be called for interviews. How to apply Write your application in Swedish or English and include the following attachments: CV and personal letter with a justification of why you are interested in the training place/employment and in what way the research project matches your interests and your educational background. Copies of issued study certificates and/or diplomas. These should prove that you meet the general and specific entry requirements for the doctoral education subject area and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral education project. Copy of the master’s-level (second-cycle) thesis Other information that you wish to provide or refer to (copies of grades, contact details for professional references, letters of recommendation, etc.). We welcome your application. description: 12 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Karolinska Institutet (KI) Research Field Biological sciences Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 1 Dec 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Sweden Type of Contract Other Job Status Full-time Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research? The Department of Microbiology, Tumor and Cell Biology (MTC) at Karolinska Institutet conducts research and teaching within immunology, infection biology, cell biology and cancer. MTC have about 40 research groups and our key words are multidisciplinary, bridging, national and international collaborations. Division Marie Arsenian Henriksson's group investigates how MYC family oncoproteins influence cancer development, cellular differentiation and metabolism, with a particular focus on childhood cancers such as neuroblastoma and medulloblastoma. We aim to understand how oncogenic programs interact with normal developmental processes to shape tumor cell identity and create vulnerabilities that can be exploited for therapeutic intervention. To address these questions, we combine cancer and developmental biology with metabolic studies, human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-based disease models, differentiation strategies, and drug screening. This integrated approach allows us to study tumor development in a human developmental context, identify molecular and metabolic dependencies, and explore new therapeutic strategies. We are a multicultural, dynamic and collaborative group with an extensive network of national and international collaborators, providing a stimulating environment for interdisciplinary research and scientific exchange. Duties A highly motivated, skilled and creative researcher is invited to join our team to investigate the interplay between MYC-driven oncogenic programs, cellular differentiation and metabolism in childhood cancer. The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to research aimed at understanding how MYC/MYCN shapes tumor cell identity and metabolic dependencies, using neuroblastoma and medulloblastoma as disease models. Projects may include the identification and validation of novel metabolic vulnerabilities and therapeutic targets, the development of differentiation-based strategies for aggressive neuroblastoma, and the use of human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-based models to investigate mechanisms of tumor development and therapeutic response. The research may also involve drug and compound screening to identify novel therapeutic strategies. The successful candidate will have a leading role in experimental design, execution and troubleshooting, data analysis and interpretation, and presentation and publication of results. We are looking for a researcher who is able to develop and pursue their own scientific ideas while working collaboratively within the group and with national and international collaborators. Experience in grant writing and supervision or mentoring of Bachelor’s and Master’s students is highly desirable. Entry requirements Postdoctoral scholarships may be established for foreign researchers who pursue their merit in Sweden. A foreign researcher is a person living in another country who comes to Sweden with the intention of only staying in Sweden for all or part of their postdoctoral education at KI. Persons who are resident in Sweden and/or have carried out all or part of their academic education at KI or some other educational institution in Sweden cannot be considered for scholarships. The purpose of scholarships for postdoctoral qualification is to promote internationalization and contribute to research qualification after a doctorate or equivalent. A scholarship for carrying out postdoctoral research can be granted for a maximum of two years within a four-year period following the receipt of a doctoral degree or equivalent. To be eligible for a postdoctoral scholarship, the person must have obtained a doctorate, or a foreign degree deemed to be equivalent to a doctorate. Applicants who have not completed a doctorate at the end of the application period may also apply, provided that all requirements for a completed degree are met before the (intended) start date of the post-doctoral education. In addition to aforementioned requirements for the position: We are looking for an enthusiastic and driven researcher with a strong interest in cancer biology and a motivation to explore new directions in cancer therapeutics. The candidate should have a high degree of scientific independence, while working collaboratively and contributing to a positive and supportive research environment. The applicant should hold a Ph.D. in Biomedical Science or a related field and have a solid background in cancer biology. Experience in tumor metabolism, cancer cell signalling and/or target identification is particularly relevant. The candidate should be familiar with a broad range of molecular and cellular biology techniques, including: Advanced mammalian cell culture, drug testing and immunofluorescence 3D cell culture and tumor spheroid models Molecular biology techniques, including PCR, cloning and Western blotting Lentiviral transduction and genetic manipulation Protein-protein interaction assays, including proximity ligation assays Imaging techniques and quantitative image analysis Lipidomics, proteomics and RNA sequencing sample preparation Basic analysis and interpretation of omics data Experimental validation of candidate compounds and drug-response assays In vivo studies in mice, tumor monitoring and tissue collection Immunohistochemistry and analysis of tumor samples Fluency in English is a requirement. Meritorious for the position: Experience in MYC biology, neuroblastoma or medulloblastoma is an advantage. What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment with wide-ranging expertise and interests. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Here, we conduct innovative medical research and provide the largest range of biomedical education in Sweden. At KI, you get to meet researchers working with a wide range of specialisms and methods, giving you ample opportunity to exchange knowledge and experience with the various scientific fields within medicine and health. It is the crossover collaborations, which have pushed KI to where it is today, at the forefront of global research. Several of the people you meet in healthcare are educated at KI. A close relationship with the health care providers is important for creating groundbreaking top quality education and research. Students and employees have free access to our modern gym facilities with trained staff on site. Location: Solna Type of scholarship The amount is tax free and it is set for twelve months at a time, paid out on a six months basis. In exceptional cases, shorter periods may be acceptable. Application process An application must contain the following documents in English or Swedish: A complete curriculum vitae, including date of the thesis defence, title of the thesis, previous academic positions, academic title, current position, academic distinctions, and committee work A complete list of publications A summary of current work (no more than one page) The application is to be submitted on the Varbi recruitment system. Want to make a difference? Join us and contribute to better health for all! description: 12 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company CNRS Department Institut de Chimie et des Matériaux Paris-Est Research Field Chemistry Physics » Chemical physics Physics » Biophysics Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 2 Dec 2026 - 23:59 (UTC) Country France Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Hours Per Week 35 Offer Starting Date 4 Jan 2027 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description The doctoral candidate will benefit from a unique interdisciplinary environment combining the expertise of CNRS-ICMPE and CEA-NIMBE in polymer chemistry, soft matter, advanced characterization, and data-driven materials discovery. The candidate will be hosted within the Molecular Chemistry and Macromolecular Materials (C3M) department at CNRS-ICMPE, a multidisciplinary research environment dedicated to the design and synthesis of advanced functional materials. Research activities focus on controlled polymer synthesis, macromolecular engineering, polymer self-assembly, nanoparticle design, and the development of stimuli-responsive polymer systems for biomedical applications, with particular expertise in Polymerisation-Induced Self-Assembly (PISA) and nanomedicine. The project will also involve research activities at CEA-NIMBE, a leading institute in materials science and advanced characterization. The candidate will have access to the FastNano Liquid platform, enabling operando monitoring of PISA processes through SAXS and Raman spectroscopy, combined with automated sampling and complementary physicochemical analyses. This collaboration will provide advanced training in the correlation between polymerisation, self-assembly mechanisms, nanoparticle structure, and function. This position is located within an area subject to the French Protection of Scientific and Technical Potential (PPST) regulations. Consequently, in accordance with French legislation, the successful candidate's appointment is subject to authorization by the competent authority of the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research (MESR). The challenge. Precision nanomedicine demands nanocarriers that combine targeting, controlled release, multimodal payloads and real-time imaging in a single platform. Integrating all these functions into robust, scalable polymeric systems remains an unsolved challenge, which limits combination therapies against cancer, inflammatory diseases and complex infections. The approach. This PhD will develop a new generation of theranostic polymer vesicles using Polymerisation-Induced Self-Assembly (PISA), a one-pot process that unifies polymer synthesis, self-assembly and drug encapsulation. The vesicles will be engineered to: encapsulate active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs); carry targeting ligands; release their payload on demand in response to pH, temperature or reactive oxygen species; integrate fluorescent probes for in vitro and in vivo tracking. The scientific breakthrough. The project aims to understand how nanoparticles form and how drugs become compartmentalised during PISA. It will exploit the FastNano Liquid platform, which monitors nanoparticle formation in real time by SAXS and Raman spectroscopy. Automated sampling will feed complementary SEC, NMR and HPLC analyses, linking polymerisation kinetics, macromolecular architecture, morphology and encapsulation. The data-driven acceleration. All experimental data will feed a comprehensive database, analysed with statistical learning and Bayesian optimisation. This closed-loop framework will predict optimal PISA formulations and drastically reduce experimental screening. What you will gain. Multidisciplinary training in polymer chemistry, nanomedicine, advanced characterization, synchrotron science, automation and AI for materials discovery. You will establish quantitative process-structure-property relationships for polymer nanomedicines. Framework. Funded by the PEPR DIADEM programme (pepr-diadem.fr). Degree awarded by Université Paris-Est Créteil. description: 205 Application Deadline: December 3, 2026, 11:59 PM (NYC EST time) Applications are now open for the 2027 MCW Global’s Young Leaders Fellowship. The Young Leaders Fellowship Program is a one-of-a-kind leadership opportunity open to all young people between 18 – 26 from all over the world who wish to address community projects in the areas of education, health, and economic security. The year-long Fellowship prepares young people to become leaders of change in their communities through leadership development, global citizenship, self-awareness, and vision planning. The Fellowship Program aims to mobilize young people with the skills and resources needed to create and implement vision plans in the areas of education, health, and economic security. MCW Global’s Young Leaders Fellowship begins with the Community Needs Assessment – A one-month community needs mapping that prepares young people, between the ages of 18-26, from around the world to understand their local communities better. After the community needs assessment, Young Leaders participate in a 10-day intensive in-person training program that helps them become leaders of positive change in their communities. After the in-person training program, participants return to their communities to spend ten months developing their action plans with virtual support from alumni mentors. Eligibility Requirements Young Leaders Must: Demonstrate commitment to their community Identify an issue in their community in the areas of education, health, or economic security Demonstrate a strong motivation to create positive change and an interest in social projects, while expressing your most authentic and original thoughts. Original ideas and genuine reflections will be valued more than AI-generated responses. Be between the ages of 18 – 26 at the start of the program (June 1, 2027) Be fluent in written and spoken English Commit to doing the Community Needs Assessment in June, attending the 10-day in-person program in July, and spending the following year aiming to execute their community project Have access to email and the internet to allow for consistent communication with the MCW Global Team and Young Leaders Fellowship alumni-mentor for the duration of the year-long program Adhere to Young Leaders Fellowship graduation guidelines (to be provided upon acceptance to the program) Be eligible for appropriate visa and travel documentation Program Phases The program is based on three phases: Virtual | Community Needs Assessment: 1 Month The Fellowship begins with an intensive community mapping and needs assessment . Young Leaders will be provided with the tools and knowledge to assess their community. This phase is implemented prior to starting the in-person training, as it will give the young leaders a better understanding of the community’s needs. In-Person | Vision Planning & Project Development: 10 Days Participants come to the Fellowship with an idea of a community issue they want to address. Vision planning is the process of transforming passion into a concrete, tangible plan for change. Through the in-person training program , which includes diverse speakers, workshops, events, and facilitated group work, participants can put their local issues into a larger global context while understanding why they are uniquely positioned to change their community. Participants will also determine which tools and skills can be applied to an actionable plan. Virtual | Project Implementation & Alumni Mentorship 10 Months To further develop and execute their actionable plans, Young Leaders are paired with alumni mentors, who will guide them in the in-person program toward creating an actionable plan. These mentors have gone through the Fellowship program and successfully graduated from it. During the year, alumni mentors support participants by facilitating quarterly “hangouts” and ongoing remote communication. Alumni mentors undergo customized training prior to the start of the program to support team building and cultural competency among the diverse group of Young Leaders. Application Timeline November 5, 2026: Young Leaders Fellowship Application Opens December 3, 2026: Young Leaders Fellowship Application Closes December 21, 2026: First-round Decisions Sent Out; Shortlisted Candidates Notified; Second-Round Application Opens January 8, 2027: Second-Round Application Closes February 3 – 16, 2027: Interviews with Alumni February 23, 2027: Acceptances Sent Out March 2, 2027: Confirmation of Acceptance March 16, 2027: Confirmation of U.S. Visa Interview Date and Deposit by Mentees June – July 2027: Community Needs Assessment July 20 – 29, 2027: In-Person Training Program – Young Leaders Fellowship July 2027 – July 2028: The Entire Young Leaders Fellowship Duration For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the MCW Global’s Young Leaders Fellowship

description: TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution. The Dresden Center for Nanoanalysis (DCN) offers a position as Research Associate (m/f/x) (subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L) starting March 1, 2027 or as soon as possible. The position comprises 75% of the fulltime weekly hours and is limited to a period of 36 months . The period of employment is governed by the Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). The position offers the chance to obtain further academic qualification (usually PhD). Altermagnets are a new class of magnetic materials, and their properties depend strongly on crystal structure. This project studies how atomic defects and strain affect the formation of magnetic domains and domain walls in altermagnetic single crystals such as MnTe and Fe2O3. The work combines advanced electron microscopy with magnetic imaging techniques. Within the SPP 2558 “Unconventional Magnetism: Beyond the S-Wave Magnetism Paradigm” and in strong collaboration with the group of Prof. Claire Donnelly (ETH Zürich), the successful candidate will help build a comprehensive picture of how structure and magnetism interact across different length. Tasks: acquire and analyze aberration-corrected HR-(S)TEM images and determine local chemical compositions using EDS and EELS perform large-field-of-view strain measurements with 4D-STEM and correlate strain and defect maps with XMCD imaging develop and apply STEM-EMCD and vortex-EMCD techniques and apply them to altermagnets collaborate with a PhD student of Prof. Claire Donnelly (Co-PI, responsible for XMCD) publish and present results in peer-reviewed journals and at (inter)national conferences Requirements: a very good university degree (e. g. Master) in physics (preferred), materials science, nanotechnology, or a related field a profound background in solid state physics in general, and of crystal structures, crystalline defects, magnetism and the mechanics of materials, including stress, strain, and deformation in particular experience with transmission electron microscopy or another advanced characterization method strong analytical and quantitative skills, and an interest in computational data analysis (e.g., Python) good written and spoken English Desirable: experience with electron microscopy of magnetic materials, EMCD, or electron holography familiarity with magnetism, particularly antiferromagnetism or altermagnetism experience with electron-diffraction-based strain analysis interest in simulation of electron scattering We offer: access to aberration-corrected TEM and advanced electron microscopy facilities supervision and training in state-of-the-art techniques the opportunity for engaging and independent work within a flat hierarchy, in an open-minded team and supportive atmosphere flexible arrangements for work hours to support a good work-life balance 30 days of vacation per year (based on a 5-day workweek) extensive opportunities for professional development and continuing education health care and sports programs offered by TUD a discounted job ticket (also available as a Deutschlandticket) participation in the supplementary pension scheme for employees in the public sector via VBL (Federal and State Government Employees Retirement Fund) TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The university is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment. Application: Please submit your detailed application with the usual documents by January 4, 2027 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de by sending it as a single pdf file to recruiting-dcn@tu-dresden.de or to: TU Dresden, Dresden Center for Nanoanalysis, Dr. Darius Pohl, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany. Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed. TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance. Reference to data protection: Your data protection rights, the purpose for which your data will be processed, as well as further information about data protection is available to you on the website: https://tu-dresden.de/tu-dresden/arbeiten-an-der-tud/stellenangebote/Datenschutzhinweis?set_language=en
