description: 7 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Maastricht University (UM) Research Field Engineering » Systems engineering Engineering » Biomedical engineering Psychological sciences » Behavioural sciences Psychological sciences » Cognitive science Computer science » Programming Computer science » Cybernetics Researcher Profile Recognised Researcher (R2) Application Deadline 4 Dec 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Welcome to Maastricht University! Are you excited about developing AI methods that can make sense of complex human signals? Do you have a strong interest in machine learning, multimodal data, (neuro)physiological sensing, and adaptive systems? Are you fascinated by building sophisticated predictive models, but equally interested in understanding the mechanisms and human processes behind them? Then this postdoctoral position may be the one for you. Postdoctoral Researcher in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence – BISS at Maastricht University. Our goal: Develop advanced multimodal AI methods that transform (neuro)physiological, behavioral, and interaction data into reliable indicators of user state, enabling adaptive and personalized VR training. Your colleagues: A collaborative and interdisciplinary team at BISS, where researchers from across Maastricht University work together to apply artificial intelligence and data science to societal and technological challenges. We are looking for a postdoctoral fellow with a strong academic interest in data science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and multimodal human sensing. The successful candidate will work on the three-year VR-STRESS project. VR-STRESS is a cross-border research and innovation project aimed at developing an adaptive virtual reality system for medical training. The project investigates how (neuro)physiological, behavioral, and interaction data can be used to infer a user's cognitive and emotional state, and how these estimates can be translated into real-time adaptations of a virtual training environment. A central component of the project is the development of an integrated system that combines multiple non-invasive sensing modalities and transforms raw data into meaningful indicators of stress, cognitive load, attention, fatigue, emotional state, and performance. A key scientific challenge is to combine heterogeneous physiological, neurophysiological, and behavioral signals into robust and interpretable models that work across individuals and changing conditions. What you do You will take a leading role in the data science and artificial intelligence component of the VR-STRESS project. You will develop methods for processing, integrating, and interpreting multimodal physiological and behavioral data collected in controlled studies in which participants are exposed to different levels of stress, cognitive demand, and task complexity. Using signal processing, machine learning, and multimodal data-fusion techniques, you will investigate how patterns across different measurement channels can be used to estimate relevant aspects of user state. A central scientific question is not only how accurately these states can be predicted, but also what the models can tell us about the signals and mechanisms underlying them. You will therefore study model interpretability, robustness, individual variability, and generalizability, and validate model outputs against subjective self-reports, experimental manipulations, behavioral measures, and objective performance indicators. You will also contribute to the development of real-time or near-real-time methods that connect inferred user states to adaptive mechanisms in the VR environment. These mechanisms may, for example, dynamically adjust the intensity of stressors, task complexity, or the presentation of supportive information. Your work will focus on: developing signal-processing, machine-learning, and multimodal data-fusion methods for heterogeneous human-sensing data; building and evaluating robust and interpretable models of cognitive, emotional, and physiological user states; translating these models into real-time or near-real-time algorithms for adaptive VR applications; collaborating closely with experimental psychologists, cognitive scientists, engineers, and VR developers, and disseminating results through scientific publications and conferences. What you bring We are interested in your expertise, scientific curiosity, and potential. You hold, or are close to completing, a PhD in data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer science, computational cognitive science, biomedical engineering, cognitive science, mathematical psychology, or a related field. You have experience developing and evaluating machine-learning, statistical, or signal-processing methods for complex datasets, and you are comfortable working with different scientific programming environments. You are interested in combining multiple data streams, including (neuro)physiological, behavioral, and interaction signals. Experience with time-series analysis, physiological signal processing, sensor fusion, deep learning, representation learning, or related approaches is particularly welcome. We are looking for someone who enjoys building sophisticated models, but who also wants to understand why they work, what information they use, and how they relate to underlying psychological and physiological processes. An interest in virtual reality, adaptive systems, human-computer interaction, brain-computer interfaces, or physiological computing is therefore highly relevant. We are particularly interested in candidates who: combine strong technical and quantitative skills with scientific curiosity about human cognition and physiology; are proactive and independent, while enjoying interdisciplinary collaboration; have a research track record appropriate to career stage and the ambition to publish in relevant scientific outlets; communicate fluently in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Dutch is welcome, but not required. At BISS, you will work in an environment where artificial intelligence and data science are developed in close connection with societal and human questions. The VR-STRESS project therefore offers an opportunity not only to develop advanced AI methods, but also to investigate how these methods can contribute to intelligent systems that respond meaningfully to the people using them. What we offer At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer: An employment contract for a period of 36 months with a scope of 1.0 FTE. A gross monthly salary between €4925,00 and €6682,00 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus. 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours. Flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home. Freedom and space to shape your work independently and develop your ideas. A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with. A solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities. An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe. Faculty of Science and Engineering At the Faculty of Science and Engineering (FSE), we focus on themes such as circularity and sustainability, future farming, digitisation and (scientific) instrument development. FSE's leading projects, like the Einstein Telescope Pathfinder, are sure to grab anyone's attention. The faculty is a vibrant hub of education and research in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) and Liberal Arts and Sciences (LAS). At FSE, over 450 staff members and 3700 students gather to explore e exciting interdisciplinary research and educational programmes. Feel welcome, be part of our team and put your brilliant mind to work! FSE at the Brightlands Campuses Maastricht, Sittard-Geleen, Heerlen, and Venlo, the home of four creative Brightlands campuses, are bustling with 30,000 entrepreneurs, researchers, and students working diligently to solve global challenges. The Faculty of Science and Engineering is active on all four Brightlands campuses, and this is where our impact reaches its peak. To give you an idea of what is happening at each campus: Sittard-Geleen is home to the largest chemical site in the Euregion, while Venlo is a large hub for agri-food innovation. Maastricht is the site of the Health Campus, and Heerlen is the place to be for Smart Services. Brightlands Institute for Smart Society (BISS) At Brightlands Institute for Smart Society (BISS), Maastricht University scientists work on innovative and responsible solutions to data challenges. All disciplines and faculties collaborate in applying data science and technology to solve real life societal and business needs. BISS was set up by Maastricht University, the Province of Limburg and APG. BISS is located on the Brightlands Smart Services Campus in Heerlen, the Netherlands. BISS’ mission is to empower people and organisations through the socially responsible application of digital technologies. We focus on privacy preserving technologies, on value creation from data, and on human-technology interaction. BISS is part of Brightlands, an open innovation community in Limburg, The Netherlands with 29,000 innovative entrepreneurs, researchers and students. Every day they work on breakthroughs in the field of sustainability, health and digitization. At Brightlands Smart Services Campus in Heerlen they enable knowledge in the field of data science to lead to new smart digital services that improve the quality of life. Interested? No Offer Description Are you curious about how people navigate uncertainty in healthcare, and how AI is changing the way decisions are made? Do you have a background in the social sciences or humanities? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a postdoctoral position at Uppsala University. The Department of Information Technology holds a leading position in both research and education at all levels. We are currently Uppsala University's third largest department, have around 350 employees, including 120 teachers and 120 PhD students. Approximately 5,000 undergraduate students take one or more courses at the department each year. You can find more information about us on the Department of Information Technology website. At the Division of Systems and Control, we develop both theory and concrete tools to design systems that learn, reason, and act in the real world based on a seamless combination of data, mathematical models, and algorithms. Our research integrates expertise from machine learning, optimization, control theory, and applied mathematics, spanning diverse application domains such as medicine, energy systems, biomedical systems, neuroscience, and safety and security. The Division of Systems and Control enjoys a wide network of strong international collaborators. The position is financed by the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP), and its sister program WASP-HS with a focus on humanity and society. WASP is Sweden’s largest individual research program ever, a major national initiative for strategically motivated basic research, education and faculty recruitment. The program addresses research on artificial intelligence and autonomous systems acting in collaboration with humans, adapting to their environment through sensors, information and knowledge, and forming intelligent systems-of-systems. The vision of WASP is excellent research and competence in artificial intelligence, autonomous systems and software for the benefit of Swedish society and industry. Read more: https://wasp-sweden.org/. WASP-HS fosters novel interdisciplinary knowledge about AI and autonomous systems and their impact on humanity and society. WASP-HS enables cutting-edge research, expertise, and capacity building in the social sciences and humanities. Read more: https://wasp-hs.org/. Project description Every healthcare decision involves uncertainty. AI systems express uncertainty in probabilistic terms, while clinicians, patients and epidemiologists deal with it through judgement, experience and institutional context. What happens when these ways of knowing meet? This joint WASP/WASP-HS project, run by researchers at Uppsala University (Sara Hamis) and Linköping University (Nicolette Lakemond & Gunnar Holmberg), treats uncertainty as a statistical as well as a social phenomenon. It studies how stakeholders interpret uncertainty in human- and AI-generated assessments, and how this shapes their decisions. The project combines surveys, interviews and phenomenological methods to explore how uncertainty is handled in healthcare today, and how AI is changing this. The postdoc will be based in Uppsala. Duties The position is for two years and includes 90% research and 10% departmental duties (typically teaching). Requirements A PhD in the social sciences, humanities, or another field relevant to the project. Examples of relevant fields include business administration, organization and management, industrial engineering and management, sociology, psychology, human–computer interaction, communication, information systems, health services research, and public health. A foreign degree deemed equivalent to a PhD in above mentioned fields is also accepted. The degree needs to be obtained by the time of the decision of employment. Priority will be given to applicants who have completed their degree no more than three years before the deadline for applications. Due to special circumstances, the degree may have been obtained earlier. The three-year period can be extended due to circumstances such as sick leave, parental leave, duties in labour unions, etc. Experience of qualitative research methods, such as surveys, interviews, ethnography or mixed-methods research is required. Solid skills in academic writing and research design are required. Professional proficiency in written and spoken English is required. Additional qualifications Research experience in one or more of the following subjects is meriting (without order of importance): Healthcare or public health. AI and digitalisation in society or organisations. Decision-making under uncertainty. Quantitative methods. Mathematical or statistical modelling. Application The application must include: 1) A one-page cover letter outlining how you meet the required criteria, your motivation for applying to this position, and your expected earliest starting date. 2) A CV. 3) A publication list. 4) 1-3 publications or manuscripts, which may include your PhD thesis. 5) References with contact information (names, emails and telephone number) and, optionally, up to two reference letters. About the employment The employment is a temporary position of 2 years according to central collective agreement. Full time position. Starting date January 15, 2027 or as otherwise agreed. No Offer Description Applications are invited for an exciting opportunity to join the research groups of Professor Rob Kingsley and Professor Evelien Adriaenssens at Quadram Institute Bioscience (QIB), Norwich. We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Postdoctoral Research Scientist to contribute to an innovative research programme developing novel bacteriophage-based approaches to control Salmonella infections in pigs. The Research Opportunity: Antimicrobial resistance represents a major global challenge and bacteriophages (phages) offer considerable potential as alternative antimicrobials. Our research has established a functional genomics approach to enhance antimicrobial activity. You will play a key role in advancing this technology, applying molecular biology and microbiology approaches to engineer improved Salmonella phage-propagation strains and evaluate phage efficacy in a pig infection model. The research will combine bacterial genetics, phage biology, microbiology and host-pathogen interactions to generate findings with significant potential for translation into practical applications. This is an opportunity to contribute to impactful, translational research within a collaborative academic environment, with the expectation that findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications. The role and responsibilities: As a Postdoctoral Research Scientist, you will lead experimental work to develop, characterise and evaluate improved approaches for bacteriophage production and the control of Salmonella infection. Your responsibilities will include: Applying molecular biology and microbiology techniques to investigate bacterial and phage biology. Evaluating the antimicrobial efficacy of bacteriophage preparations in a pig infection model. Assessing Salmonella infection and efficacy of phage intervention. Analysing, interpreting and communicating experimental findings. You will work closely with the supervisory team and wider project partners, contributing to the development of a promising technology with potential applications in animal health and antimicrobial stewardship. Professional development and career opportunities: This position offers an excellent opportunity to develop your scientific expertise within a leading academic research environment, working at the interface of fundamental microbiology and translational research. You will gain expertise in Salmonella and bacteriophage biology, bacterial genetic engineering and host-pathogen interactions. You will also develop transferable skills in scientific communication, collaborative research, project delivery and the translation of research innovations towards commercial application. We place considerable importance on personal and professional development aligned with your individual research interests, career aspirations and project objectives. The ideal candidate: We are looking for a highly motivated and creative scientist with a PhD in microbiology or a related life sciences discipline, together with an interest in bacterial genetics, bacteriophage biology and host-pathogen interactions. Experience in Salmonella genetics, bacteriophage research or host-pathogen interactions would be advantageous but is not essential. Training and support will be provided in relevant techniques and areas of the research programme. Above all, we are seeking an enthusiastic scientist with a genuine passion for research and innovation. Additional information: This is a full-time post for a contract of 24 months. Salary on appointment will be within the range £39,000 to £46,500 per annum depending on qualifications and experience. A starting salary of £40,100 is guaranteed for candidates who can evidence their PhD certificate at appointment; those awaiting confirmation of their PhD award will be appointed at £39,000 until evidence is provided. For further information and details of how to apply, please visit our website https://jobs.quadram.ac.uk or contact the Human Resources team on 01603 450814 or nbi.recruitment@nbi.ac.uk quoting reference 1006242. This role meets the criteria for a visa application, and we encourage all qualified candidates to apply. Please contact the Human Resources Team if you have any questions regarding your application or visa options. We are committed to equity, diversity and inclusion, and welcome applications from all sectors of society. The Institute values of Respect, Innovation, Collaboration and Excellence are at the heart of all we do, and we expect all employees to share and display these values. To support our commitment, we have a range of family, faith and diversity friendly working arrangements to help all staff achieve excellence in their area of work. As a Disability Confident employer, we guarantee to offer an interview to all disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for this vacancy. About the Quadram Institute: The Quadram Institute is an interdisciplinary research institute dedicated to understanding how food and microbes interact to promote health and prevent disease. Its mission is to deliver healthier lives through innovation in gut health, microbiology and food. This is one of Europe’s largest centres of life sciences and home of the John Innes Centre and The Earlham Institute. ( https://quadram.ac.uk/ ). No Offer Description The Brain Signaling and Neurolipids Lab at the Institute for Advanced Chemistry of Catalonia (IQAC-CSIC, Barcelona) is looking for a PhD student with a strong quantitative background and hands-on experience in machine learning. The position is a 3-year predoctoral contract funded by the Spanish National Research Plan (project PID2025-168430NA-I00). Project The project focuses on G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), the receptors neurons use to communicate and the largest family of drug targets in the brain. It addresses how the lipid composition of neuronal membranes, which changes with aging and disease, shapes the way these receptors work. The lab tackles this question with large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. The PhD student will play a key role in bringing AI and machine learning into how these data are analyzed, sampled and interpreted, in collaboration with experimental groups in Europe. The position offers A full-time, 3-year predoctoral contract at IQAC-CSIC, with a gross salary of around EUR 30,000 per year Close supervision and hands-on training at the interface between molecular simulation, membrane biophysics and machine learning Access to supercomputing facilities and datasets to build and test new machine-learning methods Integration into a network of national and international collaborators, with research stays abroad and first-author publications as part of the training plan A stimulating work environment in Barcelona, a lively scientific hub on the Mediterranean with a rich cultural life and an excellent quality of life Requirements A master’s degree (or in the final stage of completing one) in physics, mathematics, chemistry, computer science or a closely related quantitative field An excellent academic record in both the bachelor’s and master’s degrees Demonstrable knowledge of machine learning and deep learning (e.g., through coursework, a master’s thesis or projects), including practical experience training models Strong programming skills in Python and experience with PyTorch or a similar deep-learning framework A solid grounding in statistics, linear algebra or statistical physics Good command of English Experience applying machine learning to scientific or molecular data (e.g., graph neural networks, variational autoencoders, generative or latent-space models) will be considered a strong asset. No Offer Description Criminology sits within the School of Social Sciences, adding complementary interdisciplinarity in legal studies, the Wales Observatory on Human Rights of Children and Young People, the Centre for Social Change, and the collaborative Centre for Criminal Justice and Criminology (CCJC). The CCJC undertakes interdisciplinary empirical research on areas including youth justice policy, drug policies and criminality, policing, sports criminology, sex work, crimes of the powerful, the political economy of crime in the Global South, terrorism and cybercrime. Swansea University also hosts the Administrative Data Research Centre (Wales), which facilitates access to linked, de-identified administrative data in a secure environment. The School of Law is located within the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences providing a unique setting within which to conduct empirical or socio-legal research connecting with law the concerns and methods of social science. Swansea’s School of Law has an active and vibrant research culture including: CCJC; Cyber Threats Research Centre (CYTREC); Institute of International Shipping and Trade Law (IISTL); Observatory on Human Rights and Social Justice; and the Centre for Governance and Human Rights. Previously the School has supported studentships across a wide range of sub-disciplines, including: public and constitutional law; legal education; human rights; disability law; asylum law; tort law; environmental law; European Union law and governance; family law; perceptions of risk in third sector sporting clubs; banking and environmental risk; comparative Welsh/English housing law/policy; and constitutional perspectives on Welsh Devolution. Students will predominately be based at Swansea University, although will be invited to attend WGSSS events at other locations in Wales. Throughout the PhD, all WGSSS students come together for joint workshops, residential courses, and annual conferences. Seminars include those organised by the Welsh Centre for Crime and Social Justice Conference (held at Gregynog, Powys) each year, who also hold residential postgraduate training days. In these, and other events, students work and present alongside established researchers. description: 103 Application Deadline: December 6, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. (CET) Applications are now open for the 2027 taz Panter Foundation Rest & Resilience Fellowship. The taz Panter Foundation offers journalists from countries with restricted press freedom a six-month stay in Berlin for rest, recovery and professional development. Taz Foundation invites two journalists from countries with restricted press and information freedoms to Berlin for a six-month stay. During their time in Berlin, the media professionals can take a break from their daily responsibilities, recover from difficult working conditions, and broaden their personal and professional horizons. At the end of the six months, the fellows return to their home countries with renewed energy and new perspectives to continue their journalistic work. If they wish, participants may withdraw completely from public life. However, the fellowship includes various workshops for professional development and networking, and participation in these is strongly recommended. In addition, the stay in Berlin offers the opportunity to connect with international journalists from around the world, get to know German newsrooms, attend language courses, and—if desired—receive individual psychosocial counseling. Requirements Suitability for the program. Applicants should have a clear idea of how the six-month fellowship in Berlin will positively impact their current work situation. Note: The fellowship is intended to support personal development and, if applicable, career realignment; journalists should be able to return to their home countries with refreshed energy and new perspectiv es Several years of professional experience as a journalist P lease note: Although the work of human rights activists is highly valuable, we are unable to invite individuals who are not professional journalists. A personal risk profile due to journalistic work, or difficult working conditions caused by external risk factors Documented English language skills. Applicants must be able to communicate well in a professional context. A passport valid for at least twelve more months at the time of application (or applicants must be able to renew it independently). A state of health compatible with long-distance travel and a six-month stay abroad, as well as sufficient independence to manage daily life in a foreign environment. Ability and willingness to return to the home country after the fellowship. Please note: Applications from journalists who cannot return to their home country due to the political situation or their personal risk cannot be considered. This is primarily because German authorities do not issue visas without the possibility of return. Benefits Visa and travel costs Furnished apartment in Berlin Travel health insurance for the six-month stay in Berlin A monthly budget to cover living expenses for each of the six months Psychological support Workshops (e.g., digital security training, stress management) Professional journalistic and/or personal development opportunities APPLICATION DOCUMENTS Your application must include the following documents: The completed and signed application form, including: A curriculum vitae (CV) A motivation letter (1 page) explaining why you are applying for the Rest & Resilience Fellowship If you are unable to register and complete the form, please contact us at: [email protected] Application Timeline Application deadline: December 6, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. (CET) Planned fellowship period in Berlin: May 1 – October 31, 2027 For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the taz Panter Foundation Rest & Resilience Fellowship

No Offer Description Duration: 1 year Starting date: January / February 2027 Research environment The successful candidate will join the Adrenal and Gonadal Pathophysiology team led by Pr Nathalie Rives, within Inserm research unit U1239, located on the Science and Technology campus of Mont-Saint-Aignan, near Rouen (Normandy, France). The postdoctoral researcher will benefit from a stimulating multidisciplinary research environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and technological platforms at the Institute for Research and Innovation in Biomedicine, as well as through national research collaborations. Research project Within the framework of the France 2030 research programme “Women's and Couples' Health”, our team, a member of the Infertil-SaFe consortium, is offering a one-year postdoctoral position. Our team has internationally recognized expertise in fertility preservation and restoration. The research project aims to investigate the molecular and metabolic changes associated with prepubertal testicular development, with a particular focus on the first wave of spermatogenesis. The recruited postdoctoral researcher will be responsible for characterizing the steroidome and metabolome of mouse prepubertal testicular tissue, both in vivo during the first wave of spermatogenesis and in vitro using organotypic cultures. Comparative analyses of these two experimental models will provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying testicular cell maturation and the onset of puberty. Beyond its fundamental scientific objectives, this project may contribute to the optimization of in vitro spermatogenesis protocols. Ultimately, this research could help advance the development of innovative fertility restoration strategies for boys undergoing gonadotoxic cancer treatments. description: The International Max Planck Research School for Biology and Computation (IMPRS-BAC) is now recruiting doctoral candidates for a start in 2027. We seek exceptional graduates from around the globe and are delighted to offer them the ideal environment for advancing their scientific careers. The IMPRS-BAC graduate program provides interdisciplinary training for doctoral candidates at the intersection of molecular life sciences and computational sciences. This program offers comprehensive perspectives and mentorship in both experimental and computational fields, catering to graduates in molecular biology, biochemistry, mathematics, bioinformatics, and related disciplines. If you possess a strong understanding of genome science and a passion for areas such as epigenetics, developmental biology, gene regulation, RNA biology, protein biochemistry, stem cells, bioinformatics, sequence analysis, mathematics, statistics, molecular evolution, or biophysics, and wish to work at the Max Planck Institute for Molecular Genetics or Freie Universität Berlin, this doctoral program is your ideal pathway! The IMPRS-BAC is a collaboration between Freie Universität Berlin (Department of Biology, Chemistry, Pharmacy; Department of Mathematics and Computer Science) and Max Planck Institute for Molecular Genetics . You have: an above-average master's or comparable degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, mathematics, bioinformatics or any related areas, awarded by September 2027; some experience with computational or biological research; knowledge in biology or computation with a willingness to gain the other; very good written and spoken English; a project proposal that aligns with the research interests of our recruiting faculty . We offer: cutting-edge research in biology and computation, with possible specializations in genomic and molecular biology techniques as well as in algorithms, statistics and artificial intelligence for molecular genetics; 3 years funding to work on your doctoral project; a degree from the Freie Universität Berlin; excellent structured supervision through a thesis advisory committee ; a diverse community to exchange ideas with; a flexible and challenging curriculum of scientific courses and transferable skills; an international graduate program in one of Europe's most exciting cities; financial support to learn German. Timeline: Apply by the 7th of December 2026 ( 18:00 CET ) via our application portal . Long-listed candidates are invited for online interviews between the 15th and 18th of February 2027. Short-listed candidates are invited to Berlin for interviews between the 15th and 17th of March 2027. Successful candidates start their doctorate between May and November 2027. Check our website for more information. Application: Fill out the online application form by the 7th of December 2026 (18:00 CET) . Check our website and FAQ for more information. Contact: Dr. Anne-Dominique Gindrat ( imprs-bac@molgen.mpg.de ) We are looking forward to your application!

description: 3 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company University of Amsterdam (UvA) Research Field Physics » Mathematical physics Physics » Statistical physics Computer science » Programming Computer science » Informatics Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 8 Dec 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? No Offer Description Are you interested in understanding the dynamics of deep learning using general mathematical principles, such as symmetry and universality? AMLab is hiring multiple PhD students to work with Dr. Nabil Iqbal on a project supported by the Simons Foundation grant Symmetries and their breaking in deep learning. Join Us! Artificial neural networks models are made out of many individually simple constituents which assemble together into emergent entities with remarkable capabilities, including the ability to converse, reason, and accomplish difficult tasks. How can stacks of matrices and non-linearities accomplish such amazing feats? The task of developing a theoretical framework for this emergence – and to then use this understanding to construct more robust, efficient, controllable, and generally better machine learning models – is currently a focus of extremely intense study. Philosophically similar problems involving the emergence of non-trivial collective behavior from simple microscopic ingredients have been studied for decades in the neighbouring field of physics. In this project, you will take inspiration from those ideas – and in particular the general unifying principle of symmetry – to tackle these difficult problems. This is what you will do You will work to understand the dynamics of modern neural architectures in a mathematically principled manner, and further you will use this understanding to build new deep learning architectures. Your project will involve a tight feedback loop between theory and experiment. Some concrete questions include: Symmetry breaking in deep learning : a central problem in deep learning is the coherent propagation of information through many layers, and the integration of information across space and time to perform a computation. Nature solves this problem in various ways, which often include the spontaneous breaking of symmetries, a topic which lies at the heart of our understanding of the phases of matter in the natural world. Recent work has shown that some of the same principles can be applied to deep learning. Can we exploit these ideas to construct new physically-inspired neural network architectures for efficient computation? Generative models and non-reciprocal thermodynamics : despite their amazing empirical successes, the fundamental principles underlying the operation of generative models remains somewhat unclear. Is there a theory for how generative models such as diffusion models and autoregressive text generation generalize from their training set? Can simple dynamic principles constrain the creation of structure in such a generative model? Can we obtain insights into the process of generalization from fundamental principles in statistical physics and use these insights to build new kinds of generative models? Your precise projects will be chosen in cooperation with the PI (Nabil Iqbal) to reflect mutual interests, and you will work together with other students and postdocs in a new group within AMLab that will study deep learning from a physical point of view. Tasks and responsibilities: Conducting independent theoretical research, including development of novel algorithms and mathematical study of the dynamics of deep learning Conducting independent empirical research, including coding, training and evaluating deep learning models on a on a high-performance computing cluster. Presenting research results at international conferences, workshops, and journals. Completing a PhD thesis within the appointed duration of four years Assisting in teaching activities, such as teaching labs and tutorials or supervising bachelors and master students. What we ask of you You have an MSc in artificial intelligence, computer science, physics, mathematics, or a related field. You have strong mathematical skills and are comfortable with building mathematical models of complex phenomena. You have a working knowledge of machine learning, including modern deep learning architectures such as transformers. You have sufficient programming skills in Python or related languages. Familiarity with scientific libraries (e.g. NumPy/SciPy, PyTorch or JAX) is preferred. You are interested in interdisciplinary research, crossing AI/Machine Learning, computer science, mathematics, and physics You are fluent in the English language, both in speaking and writing. You are willing to take a light education task, as teaching assistant and in supervising Bachelor’s and Master’s students in their thesis research work. Familiarity with physics ideas such as spontaneous symmetry breaking is preferred but not required. We are looking for candidates who are excited by the idea of crossing disciplinary boundaries and welcome nontraditional backgrounds or preparation. If you are unsure whether you qualify we encourage you to contact Nabil at n.iqbal@uva.nl . The start date is flexible (but no later than Fall 2027) and there are multiple positions available. This is what we offer you A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is flexible but could be as soon as possible. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3,204 to € 4,051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD Candidate is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable. Curious about our extensive secondary benefits package? Read more about our benefits. You will work in this team The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain. You will be part of the Amsterdam Machine Learning Lab (AMLab). AMLab conducts research in machine learning, artificial intelligence, and its applications to large scale data domains in science and industry. This includes the development of deep generative models, methods for approximate inference, probabilistic programming, Bayesian deep learning, causal inference, reinforcement learning, graph neural networks, and geometric deep learning. You will be part of a new group founded by Nabil Iqbal working at the intersection of deep learning and physics. Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam. If you feel the profile fits you, and you are interested in the job, we look forward to receiving your application. You can apply online via the red button. We accept applications until and including 8 December. Applications should include the following information (all files besides your cv should be submitted in one single pdf file): a detailed CV including the months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience; a letter of motivation, including a description of what makes you a fit for the position a list of publications; a complete record of your Bachelor and Master courses, included grades, and explanation of the grading system; the names and email addresses of two references who can provide letters of recommendation. A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure. (for details: national knowledge security guidelines ) Only complete applications received within the response period via the link below will be considered. If you have any questions or do you require additional information? Please contact: Nabil Iqbal, Associate Professor, n.iqbal@uva.nl Where to apply Website https://www.academictransfer.com/en/jobs/365221/multiple-phd-positions-in-symme… Requirements Additional Information Website for additional job details https://www.academictransfer.com/365221/ Work Location(s) Number of offers available 2 Company/Institute UvA Country Netherlands City Amsterdam Postal Code 1098XH Street Science Park 904 Contact City Amsterdam Website http://www.uva.nl/ Street Spui 21 Postal Code 1012 WX STATUS: EXPIRED Apply now Share this page

No Offer Description Subject description AI-based protein design for generating programmable protein–semiconductor two-dimensional metamaterials. The focus of the project is to utilize de novo designed proteins as nanoscale construction systems for semiconductor materials. The research combines AI-driven protein design, protein self-assembly, semiconductor nanotechnology, and solid-state physics to develop new approaches to semiconductor nanofabrication. Rather than relying on conventional top-down fabrication, the project aims to use designed proteins to organize semiconductor materials into precisely defined periodic structures with control approaching the molecular scale. The work may include AI-based protein design, experimental protein expression and validation, protein self-assembly, semiconductor synthesis, high-throughput screening, and structural, optical, and electrical characterization of the resulting hybrid materials. Our lab is committed to translating fundamental discoveries into technologies with real-world impact. Protein-programmed semiconductor assembly could enable applications extending beyond the initial project, including metasurfaces and metalenses, optical materials, sensors, nanoelectronics, photonics, and new forms of biologically manufactured functional materials. The lab’s first spinout company is already funded and operational, with additional translational opportunities under development. Postdoctoral researchers are actively encouraged to identify and pursue new scientific directions, applications, and potential spinouts emerging from their work. This provides a unique environment for researchers interested in careers in academia tackling ambitious fundamental research problems, or in technology development and entrepreneurship. We value creativity, community spirit, dedication, and the pursuit of unconventional ideas with the potential to make a meaningful impact on future technologies. For more information : saragovi.science All early-stage researchers recruited into the WISE program will be a part of the WISE Research School https://wise-materials.org/research-school/ an ambitious nationwide program of seminars, courses, research visits, and other activities to promote a strong multi-disciplinary and international network between PhD students, postdocs, researchers, and industry. Work duties The main duties involved in a post-doctoral posistion is to conduct research. Teaching may also be included, but up to no more than 20% of working hours. The position shall include the opportunity for three weeks of training in higher education teaching and learning. Research within AI-based protein design, protein self-assembly, and protein–semiconductor hybrid materials. Development and implementation of computational pipelines for the de novo design of proteins and protein-based self-assembling systems. Experimental production, characterization, and optimization of de novo designed proteins and protein assemblies. Development and implementation of high-throughput experimental approaches for screening and characterization of designed protein systems and hybrid protein–semiconductor systems. Development and characterization of protein–semiconductor two-dimensional materials and nanoscale assemblies. Integration of designed protein assemblies with a variety of substrates and supporting membranes to enable the fabrication and characterization of two-dimensional protein–semiconductor materials. Structural, optical, and functional characterization of designed protein–semiconductor systems. Teaching in the first, second, and third cycles of studies. Supervision of degree projects and doctoral students Actively seeking external research funding. Collaboration with researchers from different scientific disciplines and with external partners, including industry. Administration related to the work duties listed above. Qualification requirements Appointment to a post-doctoral position requires that the applicant has a PhD, or an international degree deemed equivalent to a PhD, within the subject of the position, completed no more than three years before the date of employment decision. Under special circumstances, the doctoral degree can have been completed earlier. Additional requirements: Very good oral and written proficiency in English. A doctoral degree, or equivalent research experience, in a field relevant to the position, such as protein design, computational bioinformatics, hybrid materials or a closely related field. Assessment criteria and other qualifications This is a career development position primarily focused on research. No Offer Description National Institute of Research and Innovation (NIRI), Riga, Latvia Payment : 22 EUR gross per hour Duration: 24 months (full-time) Application Deadline: December 11, 2026 About the Position The National Institute of Research and Innovation (NIRI) in Riga, Latvia, invites applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher specializing in metagenomics, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and microbial ecology to join the One Health Informatics Group under the EchoHEALTH ERA Chair project. We are looking for a motivated researcher with a strong background in microbial genomics, metagenomics, or computational biology who is interested in investigating the diversity, evolution, and dissemination of antimicrobial resistance across human, animal, and environmental ecosystems. The successful candidate will work with high-throughput sequencing datasets, including shotgun metagenomics and bacterial whole-genome sequencing, to investigate microbial communities, antimicrobial resistance genes, mobile genetic elements, and their ecological and evolutionary relationships. The position offers opportunities to develop independent research ideas, contribute to international collaborations, publish scientific findings, and participate in multidisciplinary One Health research. Research Focus The research will explore the distribution, diversity, and potential transmission of antimicrobial resistance across interconnected ecosystems. Key research areas include: Metagenomics and resistome profiling: Characterization of microbial communities and antimicrobial resistance genes in complex biological and environmental samples. Genome-resolved metagenomics: Assembly, binning, and characterization of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). Microbial genomics: Whole-genome assembly, annotation, comparative genomics, and genomic epidemiology. Long-read and hybrid sequencing: Integration of short- and long-read sequencing data for microbial genome reconstruction. Mobile genetic elements: Investigation of plasmids, integrons, and other genetic elements involved in horizontal gene transfer. One Health surveillance: Integration of genomic and environmental data to investigate AMR across livestock, wastewater, and human-associated microbiomes. Computational method development: Development and application of reproducible bioinformatics workflows for large-scale genomic and metagenomic datasets. Key Responsibilities The successful candidate will: Conduct independent and collaborative research in microbial genomics, metagenomics, and antimicrobial resistance. Analyze high-throughput sequencing datasets using computational and statistical approaches. Perform microbial genome assembly, annotation, comparative genomics, and genome-resolved metagenomic analyses. Investigate antimicrobial resistance genes, mobile genetic elements, and microbial community dynamics. Develop, implement, and maintain reproducible bioinformatics pipelines. Integrate genomic, ecological, and environmental metadata to address One Health research questions. Prepare scientific manuscripts, present research findings at international conferences, and contribute to project deliverables. Collaborate with interdisciplinary research teams and contribute to mentoring PhD students and junior researchers. Required Qualifications Applicants should meet the following requirements: A PhD in bioinformatics, microbiology, genomics, computational biology, environmental science, veterinary science, agricultural science, or a closely related discipline. Candidates expecting to complete their PhD before the employment start date may also be considered, subject to institutional eligibility requirements. Demonstrated research experience in microbial genomics, metagenomics, or closely related computational analyses. Practical experience with Linux/Unix environments and bioinformatics tools. Programming or scripting experience using Python, R, Bash, or similar languages. Familiarity with high-throughput sequencing data analysis, genome assembly, annotation, or microbial community profiling. Ability to conduct research independently and collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams. Good scientific communication and academic writing skills. Excellent written and spoken English. Desirable Qualifications Experience in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage: Shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved metagenomics. Metagenome assembly, binning, and MAG reconstruction. Antimicrobial resistance gene detection and resistome characterization. Plasmid analysis, mobile genetic elements, and horizontal gene transfer. Long-read sequencing technologies, including Oxford Nanopore or PacBio. Hybrid genome assembly using short- and long-read sequencing data. Bioinformatics workflow development using Nextflow or Snakemake. High-performance computing (HPC) environments. Statistical analysis of microbial communities and integration of multi-omics datasets. Environmental microbiology, wastewater surveillance, or One Health research. Applicants are not expected to have expertise in all the areas listed above. We particularly encourage applications from researchers with strong computational skills who are interested in expanding their expertise in AMR genomics and One Health research. What We Offer A full-time postdoctoral research position within the EchoHEALTH ERA Chair project. Opportunities to conduct research at the intersection of microbial genomics, bioinformatics, and One Health. Access to sequencing infrastructure, computational resources, and high-performance computing facilities. Opportunities to publish in international peer-reviewed journals and present research at scientific conferences. Collaboration with researchers across microbiology, genomics, veterinary science, environmental science, and computational biology. Opportunities to develop independent research directions and contribute to competitive research proposals. A supportive, international, and interdisciplinary research environment. Salary and employment conditions in accordance with institutional policies and applicable Latvian regulations. Application Procedure Interested candidates should submit the following documents in English: Curriculum Vitae (CV) An academic CV, preferably in Europass format, including: Educational qualifications and research appointments. Technical expertise and relevant bioinformatics skills. Research projects and scientific publications. Conference presentations, awards, and other relevant academic achievements. Motivation Letter (maximum 2 pages) The letter should briefly describe: Your research background and relevant technical expertise. Your experience in metagenomics, microbial genomics, bioinformatics, or related fields. Your research interests and motivation for joining the EchoHEALTH project. How your expertise could contribute to the proposed research activities. Please email your application to anda.baumane@niri.lv with the subject line: EchoHEALTH – Postdoctoral Researcher Application Applications may be reviewed as they are received. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted regarding the next stages of the selection process. Recruitment Committee: Dr. Alvis Brazma – ERA Chair Holder, NIRI Prof. Jānis Kloviņš – Project Manager, NIRI Dr. Robin B. Guevarra – Senior Researcher, NIRI Dr. Zane Kalnina – Senior Researcher, NIRI Dr. Ilze Elbere – Senior Researcher, NIRI Elīna Zeltkalne-Ratniece – Human Resources, NIRI Where to apply E-mail anda.baumane@niri.lv Requirements Research Field Biological sciences Education Level PhD or equivalent Languages ENGLISH Additional Information Additional comments About NIRI and EchoHEALTH The EchoHEALTH project aims to strengthen One Health informatics research by integrating bioinformatics, genomics, and data science into the study of human, animal, and environmental health. Through interdisciplinary collaboration and the application of advanced omics technologies, the project seeks to improve understanding of microbial ecosystems and antimicrobial resistance and contribute to integrated surveillance and preventive health strategies. The successful candidate will join the One Health Informatics Group in Riga, Latvia, and contribute to the development of genomic and computational approaches for One Health research. No Offer Description The Netherlands is one of the leading countries in quantum technology with QuTech at its heart. Join our team as an Embedded Software Engineer at our research centre and help us shape the quantum future. Job description As an Embedded Software Engineer at QuTech, you will be part of the Open Access Team within the Quantum Internet Division. The team works closely with research groups, engineers, and support staff, as well as with research and engineering teams across Europe through the Quantum Internet Alliance (QIA), a partnership of more than 50 organisations working together to build a quantum internet in Europe. The Open Access Team is working to develop shared Open access infrastructure for quantum internet research and development. The goal is to provide tools and facilities that help researchers, technology developers, and end users accelerate progress across Europe. One example is QI-Lab, a quantum hardware emulation platform recently developed at QuTech that enables hardware-in-the-loop quantum network experiments using a desktop. Our goal is to release QI-Lab as an open-source experimentation platform that can be used by the wider quantum internet community. In this role you will work closely with researchers and engineers to develop, maintain and improve the platform and make it usable for a wider community. On a daily basis your responsibilities will be: Develop new features for our quantum hardware emulation platforms and maintain and improve the existing codebase. Work on the embedded parts of the stack, including RTOS programming and integration on platforms with real-time constraints, adapting the design as new research challenges arise. Integrate and control lab instruments and FPGA-based hardware from software, and debug issues at the hardware/software boundary. Prepare QI-Lab for open-source release: packaging, versioning, automated testing and handling contributions from outside QuTech. Write documentation, examples and onboarding material, and support researchers at QuTech and QIA partners using the platform. Work with experimentalists and fellow engineers to design and run experiments that demonstrate hardware/software integration and the functionality of the stack. Collaborate with engineering and research teams at QIA partner organizations across Europe, including occasional on-site visits. Job Requirements We are looking for a motivated junior to mid-level Embedded Software Engineer, ideally with around two years of relevant experience and a master's degree in Embedded Systems, Computer Science, or a related field. We would be particularly interested in candidates who have: Experience developing software in C/C++ and Python. Familiarity with low-level software (e.g. peripheral firmware, serial communication) and with development on Linux. Ability to explain technical choices clearly to physicists, engineers and external users, in English. Enjoyment of working in multidisciplinary teams across organizations. If you are eager to further develop these skills, we would be happy to support your growth. Nice to have: Experience with RTOSs, SoCs, or FPGA development (VHDL/Verilog) or FPGA-based instruments. Experience controlling lab or test equipment from software (e.g. SCPI/VISA, vendor SDKs, custom protocols). Comfort with oscilloscopes, logic analysers and similar debugging tools. Experience with open-source projects, technical documentation, or CI pipelines. Familiarity with Agile ways of working. Interest in physics experiments; exposure to quantum technology or optics is a plus but not required. We look forward to receiving applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to creating an inclusive environment that celebrates diversity. We believe in the power of an inclusive organizational culture and think it is important that everyone can be themselves. Whether it concerns age, gender, religion, sexual orientation, cultural background: everyone is welcome! TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. QuTech At QuTech, we work on radically new technologies with world-changing potential. Our mission: to develop scalable prototypes of a quantum computer and a quantum internet by integrating world-class research and groundbreaking innovation. Through excellence, relevance, and leadership, we cultivate a vibrant quantum technology ecosystem. Together, we are creating the quantum future, because we believe that quantum technologies can be a game changer in many societal and economic sectors, including health, agriculture and safety. Conditions of employment As an Embedded Software Engineer, you will initially be offered a one-year contract with TU Delft, with the possibility of extension. You will work in a dynamic, international, and inclusive environment, where you will have ample opportunities to learn, develop your skills, and grow professionally. A salary based on Scale 10 of the CAO for Dutch Universities with a salary between €3,706 - €5,760 gross per month based on a fulltime contract (38 hours) 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. An excellent pension scheme via the ABP. The possibility to compile an individual employment package every year. Discount on health insurance. Flexible working week. Every year, 232 leave hours (at 38 hours). You can also sell or buy additional leave hours via the individual choice budget. Plenty of opportunities for education, training, and courses. Additional information For questions concerning the procedure please contact our recruitment team at QuTech at recruitment-qutech@tudelft.nl . Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 10 December 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: CV Motivational letter You can address your application to Nico Seidler. Please note: To protect your personal data, we only accept applications submitted via the ‘Apply’ button advertised under the vacancies on our website. Applications and additional information sent by email or through other channels, including unsolicited applications, will not be considered or responded to. This also applies to open applications. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services. No Offer Description Are you ready to establish your own research group and pursue ambitious questions in experimental protein biochemistry? Join Uppsala University and SciLifeLab to develop an independent research programme in a collaborative, internationally leading scientific environment. We are now looking for an Assistant Professor (SciLifeLab Fellow) with scientific originality and the potential to establish an internationally competitive research programme in experimental protein biochemistry. The position has a strong research focus and offers considerable freedom to develop an independent research direction that broadens and strengthens the existing research environment. Biochemistry is a core area at the Department of Chemistry for Life Sciences and a central part of the Faculty of Science and Technology’s life science profile. Our workplace at the Biomedical Centre (BMC) offers an excellent environment for experimental protein biochemistry, with modern laboratories and access to advanced infrastructure for protein production and characterization, structural biology, biophysical analysis and cell-based assays. Through Uppsala University and SciLifeLab, there is also access to world-class national technology platforms in proteomics, genomics, imaging, bioinformatics and data-driven life science. These resources provide excellent opportunities to conduct and develop innovative experimental protein biochemistry and integrate mechanistic studies with advanced experimental and computational approaches. The recruitment is part of Uppsala University's tenure-track career system. The successful candidate will receive a substantial start-up package comparable in scale to an ERC Starting Grant, providing the resources to establish an independent research group and develop an independent research programme. The position offers a clear pathway towards a long-term academic career, with the opportunity for promotion to a permanent position as Senior Lecturer (Associate Professor) following a successful evaluation. You will join a highly collaborative and internationally strong Biochemistry programme that seeks to uncover how protein sequence, structure, dynamics and interactions give rise to biochemical activity and cellular function. The programme has established strengths in large-scale interaction discovery, quantitative characterization of molecular interactions and in time-resolved studies of protein structural dynamics. We welcome applicants with a background in experimental protein biochemistry, including areas such as structural biology, protein dynamics and intrinsically disordered proteins, molecular recognition, enzymology, protein design, directed evolution, and synthetic biology. We particularly encourage original research programmes that develop or apply innovative experimental approaches to understand, predict, or design protein function. Scientific excellence, originality, and potential for future development are central to this recruitment. You can read more about research and education at the Department of Chemistry for Life Sciences and the Biochemistry programme . The position is affiliated with the Science for Life Laboratory (SciLifeLab). SciLifeLab is a national center for leading edge technological infrastructures that supports large-scale data and hypothesis-driven research in the field of molecular biosciences. SciLifeLab ( www.scilifelab.se ) operates nationally, engaging all major Universities of Sweden including the four founding universities: Karolinska Institutet, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm University and Uppsala University. SciLifeLab brings together researchers across traditional boundaries and promotes collaborations with industry, healthcare, public research organizations and international partners. As a SciLifeLab Fellow, the recruited researcher will be part of the dynamic SciLifeLab community both locally in Uppsala and in Sweden at large. For information about the SciLifeLab fellow program, see https://www.scilifelab.se/research/#fellows . SciLifeLab Fellows are also part of a broad national network of future academic leaders within SciLifeLab and Wallenberg’s national program for data-driven life science (DDLS fellows) and the fellow programs at the Wallenberg Centers for Molecular Medicine (WCMM fellows), within the network Program for Academic leaders in Life Science, PALS, see https://www.palsnetwork.se . Subject area The subject area is Experimental Protein Biochemistry. It encompasses experimental approaches to understanding how protein sequence, structure, dynamics and interactions determine biochemical activity and cellular function, and to use this understanding to predict or engineer protein function. Particularly relevant are research programmes that use or develop innovative experimental approaches to investigate protein function, from atomic structure and molecular mechanisms to biological function. We particularly welcome research programmes that employ or develop innovative experimental approaches to investigate protein sequence, structure and function, spanning atomic-resolution studies and molecular mechanisms to biological processes. Of particular interest are research directions that open new avenues in experimental and predictive protein science, for example through time-resolved, quantitative, or systematic studies of protein structure, dynamics, and function, or by integrating experimental methods with AI-assisted modelling and/or the design of proteins with desired properties and functions. The subject area is intentionally broad, and we welcome applicants from across experimental protein biochemistry, without preference for a particular protein class, biological system or methodology. Scientific excellence, originality and future potential will guide the selection. Duties : You will work with: research. Research includes establishing and leading an independent research group, publishing research of high quality, presenting results internationally. Actively applying for and securing external grants. teaching. Teaching includes responsibility for courses, course administration and supervision of doctoral students in Swedish and English. If you are initially unable to teach in Swedish, Swedish-language training aimed at achieving this proficiency will be included in your duties. administration. Participate in the general academic duties of the Department of Chemistry for Life Sciences. This includes serving on committees, taking on responsibilities beyond your own research and teaching assignments, contributing to the evaluation and development of teaching and research activities, working collaboratively with colleagues, and providing support and constructive feedback to colleagues. keeping up to date in your subject area and following developments in society that are relevant to your work at Uppsala University. to contribute to a constructive and collegial working environment. In choosing between eligible candidates, emphasis will primarily be given to both research and teaching expertise, with particular weight to research expertise. In addition, attention will be given to management and collaboration expertise. Qualifications required You must have: a PhD in biochemistry, biophysics, molecular life science, or a closely related field. description: 6 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company NTNU Norwegian University of Science and Technology Department Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management Research Field Engineering » Electrical engineering Economics » Economic policy Engineering » Other Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Positions PhD Positions Application Deadline 11 Dec 2026 - 23:59 (Europe/Oslo) Country Norway Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Full-time Hours Per Week 37,5 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme?
