No Offer Description This is NTNU NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim. At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world. You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here. About the position We invite applications for a 3-year PhD Candidate position on the future role of hydrogen and hydrogen products in industrial decarbonization. The position is based at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management , located at NTNU’s campus in Trondheim. The mission of Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management (IØT) is to carry out education, research, and innovation activities at an international level at the intersection between technology/natural sciences and business economics, management, and HSE. The department’s activities aim to contribute to sustainable value creation within technology-based areas in industry, business, and the public sector in Norway About the position Electrification is widely promoted as a key pathway to industrial decarbonization. At the same time, hydrogen and carbon capture and storage (CCS) are increasingly recognized as important solutions for sectors where direct electrification may be difficult or uneconomic. This has led to a growing debate about the future role of "electrons versus molecules" in a net-zero economy. Most existing studies assume that today's industrial structure remains largely unchanged and focus on how current industries can reduce emissions. However, deep decarbonization may fundamentally reshape industrial production, value chains, competitiveness, and the location of energy-intensive activities. As a result, future hydrogen demand may depend as much on industrial transformation as on technological choices. This PhD project will investigate how alternative pathways toward a zero-emission industrial sector affect the future demand for hydrogen and the development of hydrogen value chains. The research will analyze the interplay between electrification, hydrogen, and CCS, while explicitly accounting for potential changes in industrial structures and production systems. The project addresses research questions like: How will future hydrogen demand vary across alternative industrial decarbonization pathways? Which industrial sectors are likely to rely on electrification, hydrogen, or CCS to achieve net-zero emissions? How might industrial transformation affect hydrogen production, transport, storage, and trade? What level of hydrogen deployment is required to justify dedicated hydrogen infrastructure and markets? How can Europe and Norway prepare for different industrial and energy-system transition pathways? The successful candidate will develop and analyze future scenarios for industrial transformation, hydrogen demand, and infrastructure development. The project will contribute to the scientific and policy debate on how competitive zero-emission industries can emerge under different transition strategies. Research environment The PhD candidate will join a multidisciplinary research environment at the intersection of energy economics, industrial economics, operations research, and energy systems analysis. The position is affiliated with FME HYDROGENi, the Norwegian Research and Innovation Centre for Hydrogen and Ammonia. The centre brings together 46 research and industry partners to develop the knowledge, technologies, and solutions needed to support a sustainable hydrogen economy and contribute to Norway's ambitions for climate neutrality and industrial transformation. FME HYDROGENi conducts research across the hydrogen value chain, including hydrogen production, transport and storage, industrial and maritime applications, safety, and the broader role of hydrogen in future energy systems. The centre is funded by the Research Council of Norway through the Centres for Environment-friendly Energy Research (FME) programme and operates during the period 2022-2030 The PhD candidate will be hosted at the Managerial Economics, Finance and Operations Research (BEDØK) group at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management. The group is one of Norway’s leading academic environments in operations research, logistics, optimization, and quantitative decision support. The candidate will work in close collaboration with researchers from NTNU’s Department of Computer Science and Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Your role in the project The PhD candidate will: Conduct original scientific research on hydrogen and industrial decarbonization pathways. Develop and analyze scenarios for industrial transformation and climate neutrality. Assess the future role of electrification, hydrogen, and CCS across industrial sectors. Quantify hydrogen demand and infrastructure requirements under alternative transition pathways. Publish research results in leading international journals and conferences. Collaborate with academic, industry, and public-sector partners. Complete the required coursework as part of the PhD programme. Contribute to dissemination and communication of research findings. Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Qualification requirements Applicants must hold a master’s degree in a relevant field with strong academic results (B or better according to NTNU’s grading scale). Relevant academic backgrounds include: Operations research or optimization Energy systems Energy Economics Engineering disciplines with strong quantitative and analytical content Or other closely related disciplines. Applicants must demonstrate strong analytical and quantitative skills. The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Desired qualifications The following qualifications will be considered an advantage: Experience with energy system modelling, scenario analysis, or techno-economic analysis. Knowledge of hydrogen technologies, industrial decarbonization, or climate policy. Experience with quantitative modelling and data analysis. Programming skills in Python, Julia, R, GAMS, or similar tools. Interest in interdisciplinary research at the interface of technology, economics, and policy. Applicants in the final phase of their master’s studies are encouraged to apply. Personal characteristics We are looking for a candidate who: Is intellectually curious and motivated to conduct high-quality research Has strong analytical and problem-solving skills Works independently and in a structured manner Has excellent communication and collaboration skills Thrives in an interdisciplinary research environment. Is interested in research with relevance for industry, policy, and society. Emphasis will be placed on scientific quality, research potential, and personal suitability. We offer An exciting and international academic environment with opportunities for competence development Close collaboration with leading researchers in energy systems modelling, optimization, and something else Opportunities to engage with industry partners and public sector stakeholders Participation in research addressing key challenges of the green transition. Opportunities for international research stays and conference participation. An open and inclusive workplace with engaged colleagues Favorable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund Employee benefits Good loan, insurance, and pension schemes in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) Working at NTNU Information about working and living in Norway can be found at the following link: https://www.workinnorway.no/en/Home Diversity Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful . We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. Salary and conditions In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. The period of employment is 3 years. The position is connected to the PhD program at the Faculty of Economics and Management, and the faculty will be your employer. Appointment to a PhD position requires that you are admitted to the PhD programme in Industrial Economics and Technology Management within three months of employment, and that you participate in an organized PhD programme during the employment period. Trondheim is the workplace. For necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act , and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed. Any statutory leave will be added to the employment period. As an employee at NTNU, it is important to stay updated on professional and organizational changes and adapt to these. About the application Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information we have at the application deadline. Therefore, ensure that your application clearly demonstrates how your skills and experiences meet the criteria described above. The application must contain the following: Motivation letter – The motivation letter must clearly state how the candidate meets the qualification requirements. Research plan (maximum one page) – Applicants should provide a brief research plan describing how they would approach one or more of the research questions outlined in the description of the position. The plan should reflect the applicant’s research interests and provide an outline of how they envision contributing to the project objectives. CV , diplomas, and certificates Scientific works, including the master thesis. Names and contact information of at least two potential references If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both bachelor's and master's education, in addition to other higher education. Description of the documentation required can be found here . Please note that diploma Supplement is required to attach for European Master Diplomas outside Norway. Chinese applicants are required to provide confirmation of Master Diploma from China Credentials Verification (CHSI) . If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir) , please attach this as well. In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential for research will also count in the assessment of the candidates. NTNU is committed to following the evaluation criteria for research quality according to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment – DORA and the commitments in CoARA (responsible research assessment and recognition of a broader range of academic contributions in line with NTNU's societal mission). Incomplete applications will not be considered. General information A public applicant list with names, ages, job titles, and municipalities of residence will be prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to reserve yourself from being included on the public applicant list, this must be justified. The assessment will be made in accordance with applicable laws. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted. Trondheim is a modern European city with a rich cultural scene. Trondheim is Norway's technology capital with a population of over 200,000. The Norwegian welfare state, including healthcare, schools, kindergartens, and general equality, is probably the best of its kind in the world. Professional subsidized childcare is readily available. Furthermore, Trondheim offers excellent educational opportunities (including international schools) and opportunities to enjoy nature, culture, and family life, with low crime rates and clean air quality. Questions about the position can be directed to Professor Asgeir Tomasgard (asgeir.tomasgard @ntnu.no) or Professor Anne Neumann ( anne.neumann@ntnu.no ). If you have any questions regarding the employment process, please contact HR Advisor Oddny Lyngvær at oddny.lyngvar@ntnu.no . No Offer Description The research at the Division of Atomic Physics is centered on different applications of optics and lasers, including atomic and molecular physics with ultrashort light pulses, high-intensity laser-plasma physics, quantum information, and biophotonics. The Division operates the High-Power Laser Facility, including several advanced femtosecond laser systems and collaborate with several free electron laser facilities. It is a central part of a major interdisciplinary research environment within the Lund University, the Lund Laser Centre, LLC. The division is also heavily involved in undergraduate education, especially within the Photonics programme. Work duties At the division, research is performed on the generation and application of extremely short light pulses, in the attosecond and extreme ultraviolet range. The activities span from ultrafast laser technology and extreme nonlinear optics to studies of the electron dynamics in atoms and molecules as well as more complex systems using attosecond light pulses. The division of Atomic Physics is now looking for one PhD student for the project described below. The project is funded through a Marie Sklodowska-Curie doctoral network: Quantum information science and ultrafast nonlinear control at the attosecond timescale – QU-ATTO This means that the positions come with some additional constraints and possibilities. The candidates recruited for these positions cannot have worked in Sweden for the last 5 years to be eligible. The positions come with a training network in Europe together with 15 PhD students in different countries. The project focuses on using a technique for the tomographic reconstruction of entangled states in photoionization. The goal is to improve the technique that has been developed in Lund for the reconstruction of the density matrix of photoelectron originating from the absorption of ultrashort XUV pulses by atoms and molecules. The main duties of doctoral students are to devote themselves to their research studies which includes participating in research projects and third cycle courses. The work duties can also include teaching and other departmental duties (no more than 20%). Admission requirements A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if he or she: has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. A person meets the specific admission requirements for third-cycle studies in Physics if he or she has: at least 30 second-cycle credits of relevance to the subject, of which at least 15 credits shall comprise a second-cycle degree project, or an MSc in engineering physics or an associated field, or a Master’s degree in physics or an associated field. Equivalent knowledge acquired through corresponding programmes will be assessed individually. In order to enable interdisciplinary initiatives and important specialisations in certain areas, students with qualifications in subjects other than Physics may be considered for admission. Finally, the student must be judged to have the potential to complete the programme. Additional requirements: Very good oral and written proficiency in English. The student should have a background in optics/photonics and/or atomic physics/quantum mechanics. Other assessment criteria Experience in some of the following areas is a qualification for all the projects: Femtosecond lasers and ultrafast optics Quantum optics High-order harmonic generation and attosecond physics Photoelectron and photoion spectroscopy Data analysis, vacuum technique, and mechanical design Basis of assessment Selection to postgraduate studies is based on the expected ability to perform well in the studies. The evaluation of the ability to perform well is based primarily on the results of studies at the basic and advanced levels, in particular: Knowledge and skills relevant to the thesis project and the subject of the study. An assessment of ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems. Written and oral communication skills Other experience relevant to postgraduate studies, such as professional experience. Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant, through his or her experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme. Terms of employment Only those admitted to third cycle studies may be appointed to a doctoral studentship. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. A doctoral studentship is a fixed-term employment of a maximum of 5 years (including 20% departmental duties). Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§. Instructions on how to apply Applications may be written in English or Swedish and include a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the position and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background. The application must also contain a CV, degree certificate or equivalent, and other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.). description: 61 Application Deadline: December 13, 2026 Applications are now open for the Applications are now open for the East Africa Biodesign Fellowship 2027–2028 , a 10-month professional training programme designed to equip African innovators with the skills to develop practical health technologies that address unmet healthcare needs across the continent. The fellowship brings together professionals from medicine, engineering and entrepreneurship to identify challenges within healthcare systems, design innovative solutions and explore how those solutions can reach patients. The programme is particularly relevant to individuals interested in medical technology, healthcare innovation and improving access to quality healthcare in underserved communities. The East Africa Biodesign (EAB) Fellowship is a collaboration between the University of Global Health Equity (UGHE), the University of Rwanda, Kenyatta University and Stanford Mussallem Center for Biodesign. Established in 2024, the programme applies Stanford’s Biodesign innovation approach to healthcare challenges in East Africa. Its central objective is to train local innovators to develop appropriate, accessible and sustainable health technologies based on the actual needs of patients and healthcare providers. Requirements The fellowship is intended for individuals with professional or academic backgrounds relevant to health technology innovation. These include: Medicine and other clinical health professions Biomedical, electrical, mechanical and other engineering disciplines Healthcare and health sciences Business and entrepreneurship Other relevant fields connected to medical technology and healthcare innovation Benefits The East Africa Biodesign Fellowship runs for 10 months and is a full-time professional development programme. No Offer Description Climate change is affecting ecosystems, species, populations and individuals worldwide. This project will link unique long-term individual tracking data with remote sensing products and explore the dependence of waterfowl on small to intermediate water bodies throughout the year, focussing on the availability of freshwater as a key requirement for survival and reproduction. Freshwater availability is a key determinant of life on earth, yet climate change is rapidly altering hydrological systems worldwide. Migratory waterbirds are particularly sensitive to these changes because they depend on water bodies at multiple sites along their flyway. While the role of waterbodies in shaping spring migration of waterbirds is relatively well understood, its importance during breeding, autumn migration and winter periods remains largely unexplored. The aim of this project is to fill this gap and quantify how changes in freshwater availability influence movements throughout the annual cycle, identifying feedbacks between hydrological conditions and waterbird behaviour. The greater white-fronted goose (Anser albifrons) , one of the most abundant goose species wintering in the Netherlands, will serve as a model species. The project builds on a unique long-term dataset comprising GPS tracks of more than 200 individuals collected since 2013 and which is continuously expanding. The following research questions are central to this project: How do greater white-fronted geese adjust their movement decisions in relation to snow cover and freshwater availability in their Arctic summer ranges? Which water bodies do greater white-fronted geese use for resting during autumn migration and how is this influenced by water availability and breeding success? What is the effect of yearly temperature changes on freshwater roost availability and the movement of greater white-fronted geese during winter? You will curate and analyse GPS tracking data, integrate them with remotely sensed environmental datasets, and develop statistical models to understand the ecological processes underlying the year-round movements of geese. You will also participate in BSc and MSc teaching activities. Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time. description: 165 Application Deadline: December 14, 2026 at 3:59 PM Applications are now open for the 2027 African Wildlife Foundation (AWF) Geospatial Leaders Fellowship. The AWF Geospatial Leaders Fellowship is a ten-month Pan-African programme that brings together mid-level conservation GIS professionals from NGOs, government agencies, research institutions and community-based organisations who are passionate about using spatial data to protect Africa’s wildlife and wild lands. Eligibility To be eligible for the AWF Geospatial Leaders Fellowship, you must: Be a national of, and currently working in, one of the following eleven countries: Cameroon, Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Tanzania, Tunisia or Uganda Have at least two years of hands-on GIS experience in conservation, natural resource management or a related field. Be currently employed or attached to an organisation (NGO, government agency, research institution, private sector or community-based organisation) t hat will host your capstone project, and provide a letter of support from your employer confirming your full participation. Be able to commit to ten months of consistent engagement, including virtual sessions, self-paced learning, mentorship check-ins and a capstone project. Be available to travel to Nairobi, Kenya for the in-person workshop on 13th -20th June 2027 Benefits • Practical training in modern GIS tools, data management, field data collection, real-time GIS, imagery and spatial analysis. • Expert coaching and mentorship to strengthen your technical and leadership skills. • Support to develop a map, model, dashboard or decision tool addressing a conservation priority within your organization. • Connections with a Pan-African network of conservation and geospatial practitioners. Programme Format and Support The fellowship combines virtual sessions, an in-person workshop in Nairobi, applied project work and mentoring. Expect approximately four hours per week, varying by module and project requirements. Funding covers programme-related travel and local transport, accommodation during workshops and required placements, and an internet connectivity stipend. How to Apply Submit your CV, an employer recommendation letter and academic transcripts/certificates. A portfolio or sample GIS work is optional. description: 120 Application Deadline: December 15th, 2026 at 12:00 PM (CET). Applications are now open for the 2027 Reporters Without Borders (RSF) Berlin Fellowship. The RSF Fellowship Program is designed to provide a safe space for journalists: Fellows will be able to take time off from their daily obligations and recover from their difficult working conditions, whilst learning new skills to better protect themselves by taking part in comprehensive safety trainings program on digital security. The RSF BERLIN FELLOWSHIP PROGRAM is funded by the Berlin Senate Department for Economic Affairs, Energy and Public Enterprises , as well as the generous support of Reporters without Borders Germany’s members and donors. Program Details A comprehensive, hands-on training program in digital security, including individual risk assessments and mentoring in risk mitigation strategies. Workshops on safety and resilience-building for journalists covering sensitive issues. Peer-to-peer exchange with colleagues from different regions and professional backgrounds. Insights into the activities of Reporters Without Borders, a human rights organisation active around the world. Networking opportunities with German media professionals and newsrooms. Opportunities to meet with relevant stakeholders in German civil society and policy fields. Holistic support for individual psychosocial needs. The fellowship aims to empower journalists to promote digital self-defence among their colleagues and networks of media professionals. After completing the fellowship, participants are expected to conduct at least one workshop or training session in their country of residence. Requirements The RSF Fellowship is open to working journalists with at least three years’ professional experience. This includes both full-time staff and freelancers working in any type of medium. We actively promote diversity and encourage applicants from a range of backgrounds to apply NB The RSF Fellowship is open to applicants from any country who are at significant risk due to their journalistic work. However, applicants must be able to demonstrate that they could return to their country of residence at the end of the fellowship period for visa application purposes. RSF can only support journalists working in independent media; those working in government or politically affiliated media workers will not be considered. Applicants working as investigative journalists on topics related to human rights, such as climate change, corruption, labour rights or migration, will be given positive consideration in the selection process. Expectations include: Fellows are expected to openly discuss their experiences and challenges as working journalists with a group of peers from diverse backgrounds. They should also share the knowledge they acquire during the programme with their colleagues back home. After completing the fellowship, participants are expected to return to their home region or country of residence (including third countries of permanent residence). The program will be conducted entirely in English, so fluency in speaking, reading and writing English is required in order to participate fully. Benefits RSF will cover: Visa and travel expenses Assistance with all visa-related matters A furnished studio apartment in Berlin for the duration of the fellowship A monthly stipend Travel and health insurance Public transportation costs within Germany Travel to networking events and/or journalism conferences A co-working space in a Berlin media hub Touristic and social activities Application Requirements To apply, candidates will be asked to address the following: Their experiences of threats or persecution, and how these relate directly to their journalistic activity. Concrete ideas demonstrating how the fellowship will positively impact their current work situation. They should also describe the type of digital threats they encounter and explain how digital security training would impact their personal safety, as well as that of their colleagues and sources. How to Apply If you match the eligibility criteria outlined above, you can apply for the RSF Fellowship Program until December 15th, 2026. Please register and fill out the online application form and upload the required documents here .Please be prepared to submit the following: A completed online application form A scan of your passport CV Contact information for two professional references For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the Reporters Without Borders (RSF) Berlin Fellowship

description: The Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology is one of the leading centres for research in social anthropology. Common to all research projects at the institute is the comparative analysis of social change; it is primarily in this domain that its researchers contribute to anthropological theory, though many programmes also have applied significance and political topicality. The Department ‘Anthropology of Politics and Governance’ is offering a position for Doctoral Student (m/f/d) as a part of the “Weathering Life” research group (starting as early as the 1st of March 2027) Background The Department ‘Anthropology of Politics and Governance’ is looking for a doctoral student to join the Max Planck Research Group “Weathering Life”. The group hosts research projects that differently investigate how the weather, and extreme weather phenomena in particular, are experienced, narrativized and rendered governable across the earth’s hemispheres. The group posits the notion that a rise in unpredictable weather phenomena across the world are producing novel ways in which people are building, maintaining or even attempting to cease relationships to the weather: what it clubs together as practices of weathering. The overarching questions that animate the research group are: (a) amidst a shift in global climatic conditions, what are our relationship to the weather today and (b) what do we understand the weather to be? Interested applicants are required to propose a research project that aligns with the broader research agenda set by the group, including methodological plans for long-term fieldwork. We are open to projects that identify places in Europe, Africa, North America and South Asia as field sites, and will prioritise projects where the applicant is able to demonstrate their motivation and capacity to carry out fieldwork in those sites. Tasks and Profile The primary task of the PhD student will be to develop, write and submit a PhD dissertation on a subject of relevance to this project. This should include a substantial period of ethnographic field research. Additionally, the PhD student will also be an important member who will contribute to the group’s planning, writing and reading agenda. The candidate should meet the following prerequisites: excellent master’s degree in social anthropology, human geography, science and technology studies (STS), sociology or a closely related discipline (required) experience with qualitative ethnographic methods (required) proficiency in written and spoken English (required) topical expertise in climate change, climate technologies and weather systems (desired) experience of working in interdisciplinary contexts (desired) Our Offer The PhD position is awarded for three years, with the possibility of an extension of 12 months (pending a positive evaluation). Employment will be on a full-time, contractual basis, with sufficient additional funding for fieldwork. The workplace is Halle (Saale), a dynamic, historical town in central Germany (Sachsen-Anhalt) that is home to the renowned Martin Luther University and numerous scientific institutions. The MPI offers a job ticket, company health management, and childcare services in cooperation with local day-care centres. The successful candidate will be integrated into the Institute’s International Max Planck Research School “Global Multiplicities” ( https://www.imprs-gm.mpg.de ), which offers comprehensive structured doctoral training and scientific exchange with doctoral students from our partner universities (MLU, Leipzig University and FAU). The Max Planck Society is committed to raising the proportion of women in science; we thus explicitly encourage applications from female researchers. Individuals with disabilities will be given priority, assuming equal qualifications. Contact Please submit your application electronically by 15 December 2026 following the link for vacancies on our homepage (under ‘Career’), or by going directly to the online application form using the link below. Signed cover letter explaining your interest in, and suitability for, the position Curriculum vitae including a list of publications Three-page proposal for a dissertation project, including details about methodology, and a possible timeline Writing sample (e.g., a publication or chapter from master’s thesis) Copies of all relevant degree certificates and academic transcripts from both the bachelor’s and master’s level Informal enquiries concerning the positions may be directed to Rishabh Raghavan ( raghavan@eth.mpg.de ). If you have any questions about the application, please contact: Human resources management Nadine Wagenbrett ( wagenbrett@eth.mpg.de ) We look forward to receiving your completed online application under: https://recruitingapp-5034.de.umantis.com/Vacancies/530/FurtherApplication/Apply/2 Further information on the research agenda of the Max Planck Institute is available on our website: https://www.eth.mpg.de

description: 7 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company University of Amsterdam (UvA) Research Field Engineering » Materials engineering Engineering » Chemical engineering Chemistry » Reaction mechanisms and dynamics Chemistry » Computational chemistry Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 15 Dec 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? No Offer Description Are you fascinated by how electrochemical processes unfold at the nanoscale, and do you want to use advanced computer simulations to help drive the clean energy transition? Are you eager to develop and apply quantum chemical and machine-learning methods to model complex solid-liquid interfaces? Then join the Computational Chemistry Group at the University of Amsterdam! Join our team! The Computational Chemistry Group at the Van 't Hoff Institute for Molecular Sciences (HIMS) is looking for a motivated PhD candidate in Computational Nano-Electrochemistry. Controlling electrochemical reactions at the nanoscale is essential for next-generation energy conversion and storage technologies, such as green hydrogen production, CO2 electroreduction, and advanced batteries. In this project, you will bridge the gap between fundamental atomistic physics and real-world electrocatalysis by modeling electric double layers, charge transfer, and catalytic reactivity under operating conditions. You will work in an international, collaborative team of theoretical and computational chemists at Amsterdam Science Park, closely interacting with experimental partners within the Advanced Nano-electrochemistry Institute of the Netherlands (ANION consortium) e.g. AMOLF, University of Twente etc. This is what you are going to do Develop and apply multi-scale simulation workflows, combining Density Functional Theory (DFT), ab initio molecular dynamics, and machine learning interatomic potentials, to model electrochemical interfaces at the nanoscale. Investigate reaction mechanisms, solvent dynamics, and electric double-layer effects in nano-confined electrochemical systems. Collaborate closely with experimental electrochemists and catalysis researchers to validate theoretical models and guide material design. Publish your research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present your work at national and international scientific conferences. Complete a PhD thesis within four years and assist in teaching undergraduate and master’s chemistry courses and supervising student projects. This is what we ask of you You hold (or are about to obtain) a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Chemistry, Physics, Computational Science, Materials Science, or Chemical Engineering. You have a solid background in quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, machine-learning or atomistic simulations (such as DFT, molecular dynamics, or scientific programming in Python/Linux or C++). When tackling complex scientific problems, you take initiative, think critically, and enjoy exploring creative solutions. You communicate your ideas clearly in English, both in writing and in discussions with colleagues from diverse scientific backgrounds. You enjoy working collaboratively in an international team and actively share code, methods, and insights with fellow group members. This is what we offer you You will work in a supportive, open, and well-equipped research environment with access to national and local high-performance computing (HPC) facilities, regular group seminars, and hands-on mentorship tailored to your academic and career growth. A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is ultimately January 2027 (or early 2027) however, for exceptional candidates this is negotiable. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and ranges between €3,204 (1st year) to €4,051 (last year), scale P. This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile Promovendus is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities is applicable. Besides the salary and a vibrant and challenging environment at Science Park we offer you multiple fringe benefits: 232 holiday hours per year (based on fulltime) and extra holidays between Christmas and 1 January; multiple courses to follow from our Teaching and Learning Centre; multiple courses on topics such as leadership for academic staff; multiple courses on topics such as time management, handling stress and an online learning platform with 100+ different courses; 7 weeks birth leave (partner leave) with 100% salary; partly paid parental leave; the possibility to set up a workplace at home; a pension at ABP for which UvA pays two third part of the contribution ; the possibility to follow courses to learn Dutch; Are you curious to read more about our extensive package of secondary employment benefits, take a look here. This is where you will work You will be embedded in the Computational Chemistry Group at HIMS, an interactive team of faculty, postdocs, PhD candidates, and master’s students developing and applying novel simulation methodologies for complex molecular and material systems. Our group culture is collaborative, and curiosity-driven, with weekly group meetings and strong ties to national research networks. The Van 't Hoff Institute for Molecular Sciences (HIMS) is one of eight institutes of the University of Amsterdam (UvA) Faculty of Science . HIMS performs internationally recognized chemistry and molecular research, curiosity driven as well as application driven. This is done in close cooperation with the chemical, flavor & food, medical and high-tech industries. Research is organized into four themes: Analytical Chemistry , Computational Chemistry , Synthesis & Catalysis and Molecular Photonics . The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain. If you recognize yourself in the profile and are interested in the position, we look forward to receiving your motivation letter and CV. You can respond via the red button up to and including 15th December 2026 . description: 12 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company Leiden University Research Field Engineering » Materials engineering Engineering » Simulation engineering Chemistry » Physical chemistry Chemistry » Computational chemistry Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 15 Dec 2026 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Key responsibilities The response of internal and emergent functions to chemical or structural modification of molecular constituents is often very non-linear - sometimes even disruptive - and remains poorly understood, rendering the design of soft electronic materials with precise properties across different (correlated) scales a significant challenge. On the computational side, there is a historic separation between methods and scientific communities dealing with electronic function and with materials. In particular, quantum/function and classical modelling/materials differ in so many aspects that the community has thus far completely failed to bridge quantum and classical in a practical multi-scale approach. Here, we plan to benefit from the unique expertise available in our group with molecular optimisation, (hybrid) modelling at the quantum, atomistic and mesoscopic level, and with visual workflows for FAIR simulation. In particular, the candidate will extend an existing rational design strategy framework for coarse-grained molecular optimisation named EvoMD into a nested version for structure and function design across multiple scales. In this PhD project, we will focus on two aspects, namely:1) Retaining protein functions like proton pumping upon embedding in a designer mixed lipid/polymer membrane: how does the protein conformational sampling (and thus function) respond to embedding in a structured matrix and vice versa? 2) Evaluating quantum sensitivity: can we mitigate issues of sensitivity at the smallest scale in optimisation schemes? The PhD candidate will have the opportunity to work at the forefront of software development, multiscale simulation, machine learning for multi-objective optimisation, and workflow automation. This project is part of a larger effort to develop schemes for the automated simulation of transition-metal containing molecules across the QM/classical boundary, for instance focussing on WALP-based metallopeptide insertion into lipid membranes for the purpose of charge transfer like in natural photosynthesis. Funding for other aspects of this development is currently actively sought. The PhD candidate will be placed in the Leiden Institute of Chemistry research group of Agur Sevink, which is part of the Metals in Catalysis, Biomimetics & Inorganic Materials (MCBIM) group, providing a direct link to experimental research. We are looking for an enthusiastic, motivated and friendly PhD candidate with a multi-disciplinary background that is eager to collaborate, learn and try new things. The philosophy of the group is to select tools (simulation methodology) for a given challenge, not to seek challenges for a given tool. The visual workflow development is carried out in collaboration with dr. Xinmeng Li of BoundaryComputing (Salpa, salpa.app). Selection Criteria Highly qualified and motivated graduates holding a master’s degree (or equivalent) in physical chemistry, physics, or related areas, with excellent grades. Experience with data-driven methods and optimization. Experience in modern simulation techniques at the quantum, atomistic and coarse-grained scale. No distinct preference for simulation techniques at either the quantum or classical domain, since they will be both equally important for the project. Good communication skills and good to excellent proficiency in English. A keen interest in carrying out research at the frontier of chemistry, physics and biology in a multidisciplinary environment. Our organisation The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is very diverse, ranging from mathematics, information science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The research activities are organised in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelor’s and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2.200 staff and almost 4,200 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together. The chemistry and life science research in the Leiden Institute of Chemistry (LIC) is organized around two major research areas: ‘Chemical Biology’ and ‘Energy & Sustainability’. The institute’s research themes illustrate the central position of chemistry between biology, medicine and physics. The various research topics carried out within these themes are ideal for executing interdisciplinary research. The project will officially start on 1 January 2027. The project addresses emerging challenges in power conversion, advanced control, and power distribution systems for future human space exploration missions. The academic beneficiaries include Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM, Spain), Universiteit Twente (UT, The Netherlands), Universidad de Oviedo (UNIOVI, Spain), KU Leuven (KU Leuven, Belgium), Université de Mons (UMONS, Belgium), Ghent University (UGent, Belgium), Università degli Studi di Padova (UNIPD, Italy), and Universidad Miguel Hernández de Elche (UMH, Spain). (Leonardo, Italy), IMEC (Belgium), Thales Alenia Space Belgium (TAS-B, Belgium), OHB System AG (OHB, Germany), and CRISA-AIRBUS (Spain), creating a unique research and training environment that combines academic excellence with industrial and space-sector expertise. No Offer Description Of the rocky bodies in the Solar System, we know that volcanic activity is ongoing on Earth, on Io (a satellite of Jupiter), and on Venus. Could Mars be the fourth one? The ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) spacecraft has two spectrometer suites, ACS and NOMAD, which detect trace gases along vertical atmospheric profiles via occultation sounding. One of the objectives of the TGO mission has been to determine whether this technique can reveal the presence of gases of volcanic origin in the atmosphere, from which active volcanism would be inferred. Since 2019, at the beginning of the aphelion season ACS measurements have detected hydrogen chloride (HCl) molecules in the lower atmosphere, with a concentration increasing toward the surface above the large rift system of Alba Mons, one of the giant volcanoes of Mars. These detections are hardly explained by atmospheric chemistry. In a paper in press (Trokhimovskiy et al., 2026, Science Advances) we argue that volcanic seeping provides the most plausible explanation for these HCl detections. The latest ground deformation occurred less than 1 million years ago, generating fissures that provide potential pathways for volcanic gases to reach the atmosphere. The EXOMHYCL project of the National Science Centre (NCN) of Poland investigates the geological conditions making possible such HCl seepage on Mars. We announce an open competition for the position: Postdoctoral Researcher (F/M), DK.110.K.7.2026.WR The successful candidate will participate to the EXOMHYCL project, under the guidance of Daniel Mège (project PI, Space Research Centre PAS, and TGO Interdisciplinary Scientist) and Vincent Chevrier (Arkansas Center for Space and Planetary Sciences, University of Arkansas). The work will aim at determining how HCl degassed from magmas interact with an ice-rich subsurface before escaping to the atmosphere, thus enabling us to propose a robust seepage mechanism. description: TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution. At the “Friedrich List” Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences, the Chair of Traffic and Transportation Psychology offers a full-time project position as Research Associate / PhD Student (m/f/x) within the MSCA Doctoral Network STEP-UP (the salary is calculated according to MSCA regulation) starting May 1, 2027 . The position is limited to 48 months (max. until 08/2031). The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz – WissZeitVG). About STEP-UP: STEP-UP is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network investigating pedestrian behavior and mobility in urban environments. Its research focuses on three areas: individual and interpersonal aspects of pedestrian behavior, environmental and infrastructural barriers to walking, and interactions between pedestrians and other road users. The aim is to improve the understanding of pedestrian mobility and support the development of safer and more inclusive urban public spaces. STEP-UP brings together academic and non-academic partners to train 10 PhD students through an international Joint Doctorate program. The candidates benefit from joint supervision by researchers at partner institutions, an integrated doctoral training program, and opportunities for interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral collaboration, including research secondments at partner organizations. In addition to specialized scientific knowledge, they develop transferable skills in areas such as research communication and dissemination. The program prepares them for careers in research and other fields related to transport and urban development. About the Individual Research Project (IRP 5): Road lighting plays a crucial role in how road infrastructure and its surroundings are perceived at night. Effective road lighting design must consider not only objective visibility conditions but also their subjective evaluation. Adequate lighting should enhance both the actual visibility and the subjective sense of safety. However, current research reveals significant gaps in our understanding – both in defining the psychological components of perceived safety and in identifying the critical lighting conditions that influence it. The objective of this IRP is to investigate the defining criteria of perceived safety and its relationship to objective visibility conditions resulting from road lighting characteristics. The project will consider both aspects across diverse demographic groups (e.g., young adults, women, and the elderly) in comparison to middle-aged male pedestrians, and under various lighting scenarios. To achieve this, the research is structured around three sub-objectives: (1) Design and conduct studies to gather subjective data on perceived safety, including focus group interviews and on-site surveys combined with lighting measurements; (2) Develop and implement VR or screen-based experiments, systematically varying objective lighting conditions in controlled environments to collect related subjective responses; (3) Identify and quantify the key factors influencing pedestrians’ perceived safety at night, using methods such as clustering, data integration, and modelling, and drawing on expertise from both lighting engineering and traffic psychology. This IRP is co-supervised by Lund University (Sweden). The PhD student will be enrolled both at TUD and Lund University, and will receive two PhD degrees upon completion of the program. The IRP includes a 12-month secondment to Lund to conduct an observational study. Requirements: above-average university degree (MSc or equivalent) in psychology, human factors, or a related field a basic understanding of outdoor lighting and its technical characteristics would be an advantage solid understanding of empirical research methods and statistical analysis ability to work efficiently and independently in a diverse, interdisciplinary and multicultural environment ability to work both in a team and independently ability to solve complex problems while adhering to strict deadlines proactive attitude excellent written and verbal communication skills in English to make full use of the network's training opportunities willingness to travel, as secondments and project events are part of the program eligibility for enrolment in a PhD program at TUD and Lund University (see TUD requirements and Lund requirements ) knowledge of the host institution's language will be considered an asset in the selection process Applicants can be of any nationality. Candidates may apply prior to obtaining their master’s degree, but cannot receive an employment contract before having obtained the master’s degree. description: TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution. At the “ Friedrich List” Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences, the Chair of Traffic and Transportation Psychology offers a full-time project position as Research Associate / PhD Student (m/f/x) within the MSCA Doctoral Network STEP-UP (the salary is calculated according to MSCA regulation) starting May 1, 2027 . The position is limited to 48 months (max. until 08/2031). The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz – WissZeitVG). About STEP-UP: STEP-UP is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network investigating pedestrian behavior and mobility in urban environments. Its research focuses on three areas: individual and interpersonal aspects of pedestrian behavior, environmental and infrastructural barriers to walking, and interactions between pedestrians and other road users. The aim is to improve the understanding of pedestrian mobility and support the development of safer and more inclusive urban public spaces. STEP-UP brings together academic and non-academic partners to train 10 PhD students through an international Joint Doctorate program. The candidates benefit from joint supervision by researchers at partner institutions, an integrated doctoral training program, and opportunities for interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral collaboration, including research secondments at partner organizations. In addition to specialized scientific knowledge, they develop transferable skills in areas such as research communication and dissemination. The program prepares them for careers in research and other fields related to transport and urban development. About the Individual Research Project (IRP 9): Independent mobility is a key milestone in children's personal development. Active participation in road traffic as pedestrians plays a particularly central role during childhood. The transition from accompanied to independent mobility is essential and is considered a critical component of health promotion, social participation, and inclusion. At the core of this transition is the development of cognitive abilities that enable children to perceive their environment purposefully, process relevant information, and respond appropriately to diverse traffic situations. These abilities are especially crucial when crossing the street, where the successful coordination of perception, decision-making, and action is vital. Children must be able to assess the overall situation, recognize potential hazards early, and make sound decisions. In addition, they must often evaluate the approach of an oncoming vehicle and judge whether the available gap is sufficient for a safe crossing. The objective of this proposed research is to analyze how the age-related development of key cognitive abilities influences children’s perception, information processing, and decision-making in street-crossing situations. While previous studies have addressed aspects such as hazard perception or gap acceptance, there is currently no systematic, evidence-based overview of the development of traffic-relevant competencies and their impact on children's ability to safely navigate road environments – particularly when crossing streets. A deeper understanding of these relationships will support the development of targeted measures to promote the safe and independent participation of children in pedestrian traffic. The project is structured around the following sub-objectives: (1) Examine the perception and processing of traffic information, specifically identifying which visual (and auditory) cues children of different age groups attend to during various phases of street crossing. This will involve VR-based eye-tracking analyses in simulated traffic environments.; (2) Investigate information processing and executive functioning, focusing on the strategies children use to assess traffic situations and make crossing decisions (including their knowledge, mental models of speed–distance relationships, and risk assessment). This will include both survey-based assessments and an experiment designed to examine the age-related development of knowledge, perception, and risk evaluation, and how these relate to successful street-crossing behavior. This IRP is co-supervised by the University of Leeds (UK). The PhD student will be enrolled both at TUD and University of Leeds, and will receive two PhD degrees upon completion of the program. The IRP includes an 18-month secondment to Leeds to conduct VR experiments. No Offer Description The Department of Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics at Umeå University is offering a postdoctoral scholarship within the project “Saturation in graphs and hypergraphs”. The scholarship is full-time for two years with a starting date n o later than October 1, 2027. The deadline for application is December 21, 2026. Extremal Combinatorics and Mathematics in Umeå The postdoctoral scholar will be an integral part of the Discrete Mathematics group here at Umeå. Discrete mathematics is one of the six main research areas in the Department, alongside Geometry, Computational mathematics, Mathematical statistics, Analysis & Modelling, and Mathematical foundations of Artificial Intelligence. The Discrete Mathematics group has nine permanent members whose research interests span a wide swathe of modern combinatorics. The group runs a weekly seminar and enjoys a frequent flow of research visitors. Areas of expertise include extremal combinatorics, discrete probability, combinatorial optimisation, discrete geometry, and computational combinatorics. Beyond Maryam Sharifzadeh, who will be the main supervisor, there are good opportunities for collaboration with other group members with research interests in extremal and probabilistic combinatorics, namely Victor Falgas-Ravry, Klas Markström and István Tomon. More information about Discrete Mathematics in Umeå may be found at: https://www.umu.se/en/research/groups/discrete-mathematics/ Project description Within the project, the scholarship recipient will have the opportunity to work on problems in extremal and probabilistic combinatorics. More specifically, the project will explore saturation and weak saturation functions for various combinatorial objects. The first part will focus on graphs, while the second will investigate possible connections to hypergraphs and other combinatorial structures. There will also be flexibility to explore related questions in combinatorics. This postdoctoral scholarship is financed and administrated by the Kempe Foundation (JCSMK261-0055). The tax-free scholarship will be 750,000 SEK for two years, meaning 375,000 SEK per year. Qualifications To qualify as a postdoctoral scholarship holder, the postdoctoral fellow is required to have completed a doctoral degree or a foreign degree deemed equivalent to a doctoral degree. These qualification requirements must be fulfilled no later than at the time of the decision about scholarship recipient. Priority should be given to candidates who completed their doctoral degree, according to what is stipulated in the paragraph above, no later than three years prior. If there are special reasons, candidates who completed their doctoral degree prior to that may also be eligible. Special reasons include absence due to illness, parental leave, appointments of trust in trade union organizations, military service, or similar circumstances, as well as clinical practice or other forms of appointment/assignment relevant to the subject area. The doctoral degree should be within the field of Discrete mathematics. You should have a strong background in combinatorics and basic knowledge of probability theory. Documented experience in extremal and probabilistic combinatorics will be deemed highly meritorious. Excellent and rigorous knowledge of mathematics, as well as the ability to express yourself clearly and fluently in English, both in writing and speech, are required. Good interpersonal skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively are also essential. Application The application should include: Cover letter (maximum 2 pages) describing your mathematical background and research areas, tools and techniques in discrete mathematics and more specifically extremal combinatorics that you are familiar with. You may also briefly describe your current research, Curriculum Vitae (CV) including a list of publications and preprints, Verified copies of doctoral degree or documentation that clarifies when the degree will be obtained, Verified copies of other diplomas, list of completed academic courses and grades, Copies of relevant work such as PhD theses or research articles that you have authored or co-authored, Other documents that the applicant wishes to include, Contact information for two reference persons (phone number, email address, mail address, affiliation, and the capacity in which they know you). The application should be written in English (preferably) or Swedish, and attached documents should be in Word or PDF format. The application should be registered via Umeå University’s e-recruitment system Varbi and submitted by the deadline 21 December 2026. Umeå University strives to offer an equal environment where open dialogue between people with different backgrounds and perspectives lay the foundation for learning, creativity and development. We welcome people with different backgrounds and experiences to apply for this scholarship, and especially encourage female applicants. Further information Further details are provided by Maryam Sharifzadeh: maryam.sharifzadeh@umu.se More information about the department: https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-mathematics-and-mathematical-statistics/ We look forward to receiving your application! The West African Health Organisation ( WAHO ), in collaboration with the Association Galien Africa ( AGA ), is offering 36 public health scholarships covering all training and research costs: 12 PhD and 24 Master’s. The scholarships support young health professionals and researchers from the 12 member states of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) who wish to pursue postgraduate education and research in public health. Implemented in collaboration with the Galien Africa Association, the programme aims to strengthen public health systems, promote community health and develop highly qualified professionals capable of addressing the region’s healthcare challenges. description: This PhD project relates with ongoing research projects in the area of renewable energy powered membrane processes, in particular solar-powered electrodialysis at IAMT. The removal of inorganic contaminants such as nitrate, arsenic, selenium, uranium and fluoride is a key priority. This project will explore the adaptation of the system to fluctuations in solar energy that results in a non-steady state operation. The project will include i) operation of novel continuous electrodialysis system with fluctuating energy, ii) examination of water contaminants in brackish water treatment, iii) evaluation of results in comparison to established nanofiltration and reverse osmosis processes, iv) national and international field work. There are many aspects of this project, that require in-depth research and development, including; Feasibility studies on contaminant removal in a solar powered electrodialysis process Establishment of the most suitable energy management scenario in collaboration with the renewable energy colleagues at IMT Elucidation of the dominant separation mechanisms, to achieve both fundamental understanding and optimized process performance The PhD project will be predominantly experimental and will begin with an identification of a set of research questions based on a detailed literature survey. A research proposal is required for the application stage with a timetable for a four-year research project. Execution of the research plan through conducting of experiments, sample and data analysis and write-up of results for scientific publication are part of the PhD process – a journey to become an independent researcher! Throughout the project, there will be multiple opportunities for cooperation with internal and external partners, supervision of Master students, giving oral presentations at conferences, writing high-impact journal articles, as well as sharing your knowledge via (a minimal amount of) teaching. Career development through many team activities is an opportunity to attain leadership skills and prepare for exciting professional opportunities in industry or academia. description: This PhD project builds on ongoing research projects in the area of photocatalytic membranes at IAMT. Current work will be expanded to (select) novel materials and membrane preparation methods for photocatalytic membrane development. The project will focus on i) photocatalyst selection, looking beyond the most commonly used materials, ii) exploring options of catalyst deposition and coating, iii) investigation of system design from small-scale to potentially pilot scale, and iv) application to micropollutant removal. Modelling aspects are open to exploration at molecular and process scale. There are many aspects of this project, that require in-depth research and development, including: Can a photocatalytic membrane fully degrade contaminants and how can full degradation be verified? What are the most suitable photocatalytic material characteristics for micropollutant degradation in water and what are selection criteria / tools? What are the mechanisms behind membrane photocatalysis and how can these be quantified? description: 56 Application Deadline: December 31, 2026 . Applications are now open for the 2027/2028 Yale Council on African Studies Visiting African Scholars Fellowship. The Council on African Studies at the Whitney and Betty MacMillan Center for International and Area Studies at Yale University invites applications for its Visiting African Scholars Fellowship Program for the 2027-2028 academic year . This opportunity is open to academics holding full-time positions in African universities and is designed to promote first-rate Africa-focused research and teaching at Yale and on the continent. The successful candidates will teach one course on an African topic in any humanities or social science field in either the fall or spring semester while developing a research project. The recipients will also deliver a public lecture to the Yale community and participate in the intellectual and social life of the Council and the MacMillan Center. The fellowship comes with a generous stipend and research support, including access to Yale’s excellent library and other resources. Qualifications The Visiting African Scholars will be expected to be in full-time residence during the academic year beginning August 1, 2027 . Applicants should be mid-career or senior scholars, having earned a PhD at least 7 years ago and currently holding a full-time academic position at an African university. Application Process Applicants should apply through Interfolio and must include the following: Cover letter, including current e-mail address and name of Yale faculty member you would want to work with and why. This PhD is in collaboration with Politecnico di Torino (POLITO) where the PhD degree will be awarded. Transportation accounts for approximately one-third of global energy-related carbon dioxide emissions and is undergoing a profound transition towards electric mobility and renewable energy integration. Ultra-fast charging technology is critical for providing charging convenience comparable to conventional refuelling and for accelerating the widespread adoption of electric vehicles. The aim of TRAIN-FAST is to educate the next generation of leading scientists and engineers who will advance ultra-fast charging technology within the broader electric-mobility ecosystem. The programme adopts an interdisciplinary approach, combining advanced engineering, data science, techno-economic analysis, and socio-behavioural research to address complex cross-sector challenges. As part of this project, you will have the opportunity to conduct pioneering research at the forefront of battery and charging technology. Please refer to the TRAIN-FAST project website ( https://train-fast.dtu.dk/ ) for further information about the project and the PhD opportunities available at the other recruiting organisations. Responsibilities and qualifications The PhD researcher will focus on the following activities: Develop a multi-scale and multi-physics simulation workflow to accelerate battery material screening and cell design capturing coupled electro-chemical, thermal, and mechanical degradation. Employ a combination of ML (Machine Learning) and MOR (Model Order Reduction) techniques to efficiently approximate coupled multi-physics partial differential equations across high-dimensional parameter spaces. These activities will be carried out in close collaboration with the other PhD candidates within the TRAIN-FAST network and with strong support from the industrial partners. You should have a passion for research in industrial context and a background in modeling and simulation in multi-physics domains (especially in electro-chemistry and mechanical). You will become part of a multidisciplinary innovation team located in Leuven (Belgium) with a focus on energy topics such as batteries, hydrogen, and covering several application fields from automotive to aerospace. We combine these innovation themes with numerical methods such as MOR and ML in close collaboration with academia. Investigate and derive degradation-related phenomena for specific battery chemistries. Yes Offer Description We are looking for a postdoctoral researcher specialising in quantum foundations and algebraic methods to join the INFRES department at Télécom Paris. The position is hosted by Quriosity, a joint Inria and Télécom Paris team within the LTCI laboratory and the Computer Science and Networks department (INFRES). Based in Palaiseau on the Saclay plateau, the team benefits from an active research environment in quantum information and quantum foundations. The position is part of the PIQ project “New algebraic tools for causal decompositions of quantum processes”, led by Augustin Vanrietvelde. This recruitment covers phase 1 of the project, for 18 months. The project investigates the causal decomposition conjecture: every unitary channel should admit a decomposition whose connections faithfully reflect its causal structure. The aim is to develop algebraic and syntactic tools to investigate open cases, construct decompositions or identify obstructions. The research is exploratory; partial results and limitations of the methods will be documented. Your main responsibilities will include : Conduct research on causal decompositions of quantum processes within phase 1 of the PIQ project. Supervise and mentor student projects and internships. Contribute to the scientific visibility of Télécom Paris, the Institut Mines-Télécom and the Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Job requirements You must hold a PhD or equivalent in physics, mathematics, computer science or a discipline relevant to the project, obtained no later than the date you take up the post. You must possess a solid understanding of quantum foundations, particularly quantum causality, or advanced algebraic methods, as well as strong mathematical reasoning, proof-writing and critical analysis skills. You must be able to conduct theoretical research independently, be capable of writing rigorous scientific papers and have a command of scientific English, both written and spoken. Knowledge of operator algebras, quantum information and diagrammatic formalisms is desirable. Experience in symbolic or numerical computation applied to theoretical problems, as well as in supervising students, would be an advantage. Finally, you must demonstrate good team spirit, the ability to engage in dialogue and synthesise ideas, as well as strong writing and teaching skills. Why join us? You'll be working in a fast-growing, pleasant, green and accessible environment (especially for people with disabilities) just 20 km from Paris (RER B and C suburban train lines, close to major roads).
