description: 99 Application Deadline: January 5, 2027 Applications are now open for the 2027/2028 NED Reagan-Fascell Democracy Fellows Program. Named in honor of NED’s principal founders, former president Ronald Reagan and the late congressman Dante Fascell (D-Fl.), the Reagan-Fascell Democracy Fellows Program is a federally funded, international exchange program that offers democracy activists, journalists, civil society leaders, and scholars from around the world the opportunity to spend five months in residence at the National Endowment for Democracy (NED), in Washington, D.C., in order to undertake independent research on democracy in a particular country or region. The program offers five-month fellowships for practitioners to improve strategies and techniques for building democracy abroad and five-month fellowships for scholars to conduct original research for publication. While in residence, fellows reflect on their experiences; engage with counterparts; conduct research and writing; consider best practices and lessons learned; and develop professional relationships within a global network of democracy advocates. Fellows are expected to complete a written or audiovisual product relating to their proposed research project. The fellowship culminates in a formal presentation in which fellows typically focus on their research project or another topic relating to the state of democracy in their country. The program serves as NED’s “ Democracy Accelerator ,” an initiative that brings together a focused group of fellows—key civic leaders, tech innovators, practitioners, and scholars focused on defining challenges to democracy—to incubate new ideas and initiatives on the cutting edge of the global fight for freedom. Eligibility Requirements Under the Democracy Accelerator framework, a select number of fellows are chosen based on their track record working to build democracy and their potential to advance democratic learning at a strategic and practical level. By bringing together a carefully curated cohort, we create an optimal environment for in-depth collaboration and innovation that reverberates across the NED family. This approach entails investing in fewer, higher-potential individuals and working toward fellowship outcomes that are suited to a new environment. All applicants should: -Demonstrate proficiency in the English language -Propose a project focusing on the political, social, economic, legal or cultural aspects of democratic development -Be available to work in residence at the International Forum for Democratic Studies in Washington, D.C. during the 5 month fellowship period. No other fellowships or jobs may be held at this time. Applicants on the practitioner track should: -Have substantial practical experience working to promote democracy or human rights in their country of origin or interest -Be mid-career professionals Applicants on the scholarly track should: -Possess a doctorate (a Ph.D., or academic equivalent) at the time of application -Have a proven record of publications in their field -Have developed a detailed research outline for their fellowship project Please note: Former Reagan-Fascell fellows are not eligible for repeat fellowships. Financial Support: Each fellow receives a monthly stipend for living expenses, plus basic health insurance and roundtrip travel to and from Washington, D.C., at the beginning and end of the fellowship period. Fellowship payments are calculated to cover cost of a short-term, furnished rental apartment, plus “cost of living” for food, local transportation, and other necessities. Fellows are provided with a fully equipped office, plus a limited budget for long-distance phone calls and professional travel within the United States. Please note that fellows who wish to bring family members with them to Washington, D.C., will be expected to cover the costs of their dependents’ roundtrip travel and stay within the United States. Research Support: Program staff work with several fellows to provide critical support in a variety of ways: consulting with fellows on the shape and direction of their projects, providing research, written, and editorial support on issues relating to the theory and practice of democracy, facilitating outreach, aiding in the preparation and follow-up of fellows’ public presentations, and providing other assistance as necessary. How to Apply In order to apply for the Reagan-Fascell Democracy Fellowship you must first create an account through the online portal . For detailed instructions on how to create an account , Once you have set up an account, the application process requires you to submit: 1. Applicant information 2. Project proposal for the practitioner or the scholarly fellowship track 3. Letters of recommendation 4. Resume/CV and Biography Please submit all application materials in English. Application Timeline: The application deadline for the 2027-2028 Reagan-Fascell Democracy Fellows Program is January 5, 2027 , with letters of recommendation due by no later than January 12, 2027 . For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the NED Reagan-Fascell Democracy Fellows Program

The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship program is a tool developed by the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs to assist French institutions of higher education in attracting the best foreign students to Master’s and Doctoral/Phd degree programs. It trains future foreign decision-makers from the private and public sectors in priority areas of study. Areas of Study The two main disciplinary fields for the France Excellence Eiffel scholarships cover the following seven areas of study for the Master’s and Doctorate elements: For Science and Technology Biology and Health Ecological Transition Mathematics and Digital Engineering Sciences For Humanities and Social Sciences History, French language and civilization Law and political science Economics and management Levels of Study French higher education institutions who submit candidates to the France Excellence Eiffel program agree to enroll them: in courses leading to a master’s degree in an engineering program in a joint doctoral program (joint supervision of dissertation and/or dual degree), in partnership with a partner institution abroad. Duration of the scholarship Master’s level a maximum of 12 months when enrolling in an M2 a maximum of 24 months when enrolling in an M1 a maximum of 36 months for the completion of an engineering degree Doctorate level The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship is awarded for a period of maximum 12 to 36 months starting on September 1 of the year the scholarship is awarded. No Offer Description We are excited to announce a funded Ph.D. position within a research project “Constraint-based Analysis in Mechanics” (CVUT Starting Grant 2026 led by Ivan Gudoshnikov, Ph.D.). This is an opportunity to participate in novel research with a heavy focus on connecting mathematical theory to applications in mechanics. The project focuses on the modeling of irreversible processes in materials (plasticity, fracture, damage) by the tools of convex analysis, sweeping process, vector hysteresis, variational and quasi-variational inequalities. They allow to properly describe one-sided constraints that represent mechanical properties of deformable bodies. From the numerical point of view, these methods are related to constrained optimization and complementarity problems. The goals of the project extend beyond proving the existence of a solution, and include analysis of problems, coming from specific mechanical models, limiting behavior analysis (shakedown theory), applications of optimal control methods for sweeping processes, and topological analysis in the spirit of Hodge decomposition. To represent the spatial structure, we work in the setting of Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) for continuous bodies, as well as in the setting of discrete networks of springs ( the so-called Lattice Spring Models). Where to apply E-mail ivan.gudoshnikov@fsv.cvut.cz Requirements Research Field Mathematics » Applied mathematics Education Level Master Degree or equivalent Research Field Engineering » Civil engineering Education Level Master Degree or equivalent Languages ENGLISH Level Excellent Additional Information Benefits Participation in an ambitious interdisciplinary research project on the intersection of mechanics and mathematics, hosted at a globally renown institution. An informal and inclusive international working environment at the Department of Mechanics , Faculty of Civil Engineering . Office facilities located on the Czech Technical University in Prague’s Dejvice campus . Prague regularly ranks among the top five European cities to live in (cf. Time Out Magazine index for 2021). Full social and health insurance. 30 days of paid annual leave. Children’s corner , kindergarten , and elementary school operated by the Czech Technical University in Prague. Additional benefits such as subsidized meals, yearly benefits supporting recreational and sports activities, as well as health care programs. Relocation assistance via the EURAXESS Czech Republic office. Eligibility criteria a recent MSc degree in mathematics, applied mathematics, mechanical or civil engineering, or a similar discipline, mathematical background at least up to the level of real analysis, functional analysis and PDEs, or an engineering background in continuum mechanics (elasticity, plasticity, fracture mechanics etc.), a positive attitude towards mathematical modeling and mechanics involving nonsmooth processes, speaking, reading and writing in English. Additionally, knowledge of the following topics is relevant to the project and, while not required, would give a head-start: constrained optimization, convex analysis, variational inequalities, sweeping process, complementarity problems, linear-algerbaic aspects of graph theory (see Bapat, “Graphs and matrices”), discrete exterior calculus, de Rham-type Hilbert complexes. Programming skills with Python/NumPy or C++ are welcome, but they are not crucial for this position. Suitable candidates will be asked to participate in an informal online interview. For a chosen candidate it will be necessary it will be necessary to follow the formal admission procedure to a Ph.D. study program “Mathematics in Civil Engineering” on the topic “Modeling of Irreversible Mechanical Processes”. The admission process and necessary documents are described in details here . The deadline of the admission procedure is January 6, 2027. description: 183 Application Deadline: January 9, 2027. Applications are now open for the 2027/2028 Knight Science Journalism Academic-Year Fellowship. Every year, the Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT offers academic-year fellowships to 10 science journalists from around the globe, giving them an opportunity to explore science, technology, and the craft of journalism; to concentrate on a specialty in science; and to learn at some of the top research universities in the world. Program Details The fellowship program is divided between activities arranged by the Knight Science Journalism staff and self-directed activities. Seminars : Fellows’ time in Cambridge is enriched by regular seminars from top researchers and media professionals. Field Trips: KSJ organizes several trips each year to locations of special interest to science and technology writers. Past destinations have included the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and the Marine Biological Laboratory in Woods Hole, MA, the Jackson Laboratory in Bar Harbor, ME, and the Harvard Forest in Petersham, MA. Skill-Focused Workshops: The number of storytelling channels open to journalists is multiplying, and we want our Fellows to return to the workforce with more technical skills than they had coming in. Each year we include a few skills-based workshops. Past workshops have centered around narrative writing, data journalism, and using AI. Course of Study: Fellows audit courses at MIT, Harvard, and other colleges and universities in the area. As long as fellows include one science course each semester, they have immense flexibility in choosing the suite of courses they wish to attend. Professors of these classes must approve the fellows’ request to audit. Eligibility Requirements To be eligible for a KSJ Fellowship, applicants must meet the following criteria: Be full-time journalists, whether on staff or freelance. Part-time journalists are not eligible. Have at least three consecutive years of experience covering science, health, technology, or the environment. Be reporters, writers, editors, producers, illustrators, filmmakers, photojournalists, or book authors. This includes work for newspapers, magazines, television, radio, and digital media. Be able to secure a visa to reside in the U.S. during the fellowship year (typically a J-1 visa). Citizens of countries where the U.S. has suspended the issuance of visas should wait to apply to KSJ until after such restrictions are lifted. Those holding citizenship and a passport from an additional country with no restrictions may apply with that citizenship. Benefits A stipend of $87,500 paid out over 9.5 months A $5,000 travel and housing stipend paid near the start of the fellowship Health insurance for each fellow and accompanying family members A childcare subsidy of $500-$750 per month for fellows who qualify Access to free and subsidized public transportation and free and discounted access to museums and other programs Fellows Expectations If applicants are selected to participate in the KSJ Fellowship at MIT, they must meet the following expectations: Reside full-time in the Boston/Cambridge area for the MIT academic year, which runs from mid-August to May. Produce a well-thought-out research project during the academic year that effectively leverages local resources. Attend field trips, seminars, and required training sessions arranged by the Knight Science Journalism Fellowship Program. Develop a course of study that includes at least one science course per semester. Refrain from outside paid professional work during the Fellowship, unless written permission has been granted by the director. For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the Knight Science Journalism Academic-Year Fellowship

description: 22 Application Deadline: January 15, 2027. Applications are now open for the 2027/2028 Leadership & Advocacy for Women in Africa (LAWA) Fellowship Program. The Leadership & Advocacy for Women in Africa (LAWA) Fellowship Program was founded in 1993 at the Georgetown University Law Center in Washington, DC, to train women’s human rights lawyers from Africa who are committed to returning home to their countries to advance the status of women and girls throughout their careers. The entire LAWA Fellowship Program is approximately 14 months long – from July of the first year through late August of the following year. The LAWA Program starts with the Foundations of American Law , followed by a thesis writing course. From late August to May, the LAWA Fellows earn a Master of Laws (LL.M.) degree at Georgetown, with an emphasis on international women’s human rights, and complete a major graduate thesis. Fellows are also welcome to apply for a specialized LL.M. or certificate program . Fellows also participate in professional development seminars and networking events with recent U.S. law school graduates who are working in the field of women’s rights. After graduation, the LAWA Fellows have the option to complete an internship, but not every Fellow finds an appropriate internship placement or is selected by an organization to intern. Benefits The LAWA Program helps defray costs for candidates who otherwise could not afford an LL.M. degree and provides additional professional development training. The LAWA Fellowship provides the tuition for the mandatory summer courses and for the Master of Laws (LL.M.) degree from the Georgetown University Law Center. On-campus housing is provided for the first three weeks of the summer program. The program also covers books and health insurance for the duration. Fellows are also reimbursed up to $600 for miscellaneous medical expenses. Total required for visa, including tuition, living expenses, books and insurance (estimated for the 2026-2027 school year; presume that this amount will increase for the 2027-2028 school year) $141,119 Covered by the LAWA Program and Scholarship Tuition for Summer Experience and the school year $95,066 Books and Health Insurance for Summer Experience and the school year $6,214 Housing for the first three weeks of Summer Experience $1,630 Misc. medical expenses $600 Total support provided by the LAWA Program $103,510 Remainder of living expenses which applicant must show to qualify for visa (excludes additional funding required for post-graduate OPT/summer internship) $37,609 Requirements Candidates who are awarded a LAWA Fellowship must be prepared to cover the costs of all additional expenses (such as visas, travel, housing, utilities, food, clothing, etc.). description: 3 Nov 2026 Job Information Organisation/Company University of Amsterdam (UvA) Research Field Environmental science » Ecology Environmental science » Global change Computer science » Informatics Researcher Profile First Stage Researcher (R1) Application Deadline 15 Jan 2027 - 22:59 (UTC) Country Netherlands Type of Contract Temporary Job Status Not Applicable Hours Per Week 38.0 Is the job funded through the EU Research Framework Programme? Not funded by a EU programme Is the Job related to staff position within a Research Infrastructure? No Offer Description Curious how foundation models can accelerate environmental science, and how they reach their answers? Join Us! Foundation models are changing how science is done. To truly help scientists, they must work with real scientific data, and we must understand how they reach their answers. That is the challenge you will take on. We are looking for two PhD candidates (four years each) to make AI both useful and understandable for science. You will join a collaborative team at the University of Amsterdam, led by Prof. Evangelos Kanoulas and Dr. Ana Lucic, and work closely with AI researchers and environmental scientists across Europe in the Horizon Europe project EVELYN. Together, we will turn cutting-edge AI into tools that help researchers understand and reduce environmental pollution. This is what you will do Position 1: Fine-tuning and retrieval for multimodal foundation models in science Foundation models change how science is done: one model, pre-trained on broad data, can be adapted to many specialised tasks. Scientific tasks rarely look like a chat, though. Scientists need detection maps from satellite imagery, fast approximations of expensive simulations, gap-filled sensor records and ranked candidate explanations, each backed by evidence. In this position you develop and evaluate methods that adapt multimodal foundation models to such tasks and ground their predictions in retrieved data and knowledge. You work with real EVELYN use cases (air quality, PFAS, microplastics, soil and water contamination, satellite detection of oil spills and plastic) and with the environmental scientists who will use the models. You will be part of the Information Retrieval Lab (IRLab) at the Informatics Institute. What are you going to do? We are looking for an enthusiastic and creative individual who is interested in: Developing parameter-efficient methods that adapt foundation models to scientific tasks with diverse outputs, from segmentation maps to simulation fields and time series. Developing automatic methods that decide where and how to adapt a model within a compute budget, for image, atmospheric and time-series models. Developing retrieval-augmented models that use past observations, simulations and scientific literature to improve and justify their predictions. Designing evaluation frameworks that compare foundation models fairly against strong specialist baselines and test whether outputs are supported by evidence. Working with environmental scientists to turn their questions into machine learning tasks. Publishing and presenting your findings at international AI conferences such as ICLR, SIGIR, ACL and EMNLP. The exact topics and the work plan are defined together with the selected candidate. Position 2: Mechanistic interpretability of machine learning models As machine learning (ML) models gain influence on everyday life, it becomes increasingly important to understand how they work internally. Mechanistic interpretability is an emerging subfield of ML that reverse-engineers how modern deep learning architectures make predictions. In this position you focus on developing and evaluating post-hoc interpretability techniques, which explain predictions of models that have already been trained. You will be part of the Institute for Logic, Language and Computation (ILLC) and the Informatics Institute. What are you going to do? You conduct independent research on mechanistic interpretability. The field is young, so there is substantial room to contribute. The work can address various types of AI models (e.g., transformers, GNNs) and various applications, from social network analysis to molecular simulation: as long as the data contains ground-truth explanations, we can evaluate the methods we propose. We are looking for an enthusiastic and creative individual who is interested in: Developing novel techniques for understanding how information flows through deep neural networks. Developing evaluation frameworks for assessing the correctness of mechanistic interpretability techniques. Connecting empirical findings about model behaviour to theoretical frameworks about computation. Contributing to making AI systems more interpretable, reliable and safe. Publishing and presenting your findings at international AI conferences such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, FAccT, AAAI, ACL and EMNLP. The exact topics and the work plan are defined together with the selected candidate. What we ask of you For both positions: MSc in artificial intelligence, computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics, or a related discipline Demonstrable background in machine learning Excellent software engineering skills in Python Fluent in English, both written and spoken This is what we offer you A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3,204 to € 4,051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD Candidate is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable. Curious about our extensive secondary benefits package? Read about all our benefits. You will work in this team The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain. The Informatics Institute (IvI) of the Faculty of Science performs curiosity-driven and use-inspired fundamental research in five themes: Artificial Intelligence; Computational Science; Data Science; People, Society & Technology; and Systems & Networking. IvI is home to the Amsterdam unit of ELLIS , together with VU Amsterdam and CWI, and to ICAI , the Dutch network of AI labs that connects knowledge institutes with industry, government and societal partners. Position 1 is embedded in the Information Retrieval Lab (IRLab) , which works on search engines, recommender systems and conversational assistants, with data-driven methods across text, images and structured data. It was founded in 2020 out of the ILPS group and has researchers from over 15 countries. description: 68 Application Deadline: 20 January 2027 Applications are now open for the 2027 International Journalists‘ Programmes (IJP) Southern-African Journalists’ Fellowship Programme . The Southern African-German Journalists’ Programme is a multiyear effort to foster a deeper understanding between Germany and Africa as a whole. It has been offered in response to concerns about an increasing political and cultural detachment between Africa and Europe. The bursary is intended to enable young journalists to gain valuable insights into the political, economical, cultural and social fabric of the host country. The bursary is named in honour of former Federal President Horst Köhler, whose exemplary dedication to German-African relations has left a lasting impact. President Horst Köhler was a passionate advocate for Africa, both during his time in office and beyond, championing a cultural shift in Africa policy that acknowledged historical transformations and the continent’s global significance. Every year, the International Journalists‘ Programmes (IJP) offer a bursary to up to five young Southern African journalists (SADC Member States: Angola, Botswana, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe + Kenya) and up to five young German journalists. For two months, the Southern African delegates will have the opportunity to work in Germany. They will be integrated into the day‐to‐day operations of their host newsroom while researching stories for their home media. All candidates must have a strong command of the English language. German language skills are an advantage but not mandatory. The Southern African Bursary is a multi-year initiative designed to foster mutual understanding and strengthen relations between Africa and Germany. It enables young journalists to gain valuable insights into the political, economic, cultural, and social fabric of the host country. The Southern African-German Journalists’ Programme begins with an introductory conference for all delegates in Berlin, allowing participants from Southern Africa to familiarize themselves with the host country. Upon their return, fellows are required to submit a multi-page report on their experience as well as copies of their published work. Application Requirements All journalists from Southern Africa (SADC Member States + Kenya) between the ages of 25 and 40 who regularly work for a media organisation are eligible to apply. Benefits Southern African delegates receive a fixed bursary of €3,500. This is expected to cover most of their travel, accommodation, and living expenses. No further payments will be provided, and delegates are expected to cover any additional costs using their own funds. Payment for work carried out for host media outlets is not envisaged. Application Document Application Documents: A comprehensive CV (including a passport photograph) detailing your education, work experience, and language skills in English and German (enclose relevant certificates, e.g. Goethe-Institut or TOEFL, if available) An 800-word essay addressing the following topics: o Why would you like to work in Germany? o What are the three research topics you plan to pursue during the fellowship? o What role do you expect to play at your home media in the future? o How do you plan to spend the bursary? Work samples: Two representative articles written by you. TV and radio journalists should submit scripts and/or online links. Reference: A journalistic reference from your editor-in-chief or head of department is required (freelancers may submit a reference from a senior journalist). The letter must also explicitly guarantee a leave of absence for the duration of the programme. For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the International Journalists‘ Programmes (IJP) Southern-African Journalists’ Fellowship Programme

description: 45 Application Deadline: 22 January 2027 . Applications are now open for the 2027/2028 Centre for Research in the Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences (CRASSH) at the University of Cambridge Visiting Fellowships. The Centre for Research in the Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences (CRASSH) at the University of Cambridge is inviting applications for funded Visiting Fellowships for scholars from the Global South. The purpose of these Fellowships is to provide opportunities for scholars working at higher education institutions in the Global South to exchange ideas with other researchers based at CRASSH and elsewhere in the University of Cambridge and to draw benefit from access to the University’s collections and resources. It is hoped that these visits will lead on to future collaborations and exchanges. Eligibility criteria Applicants must be currently employed at a higher education institution or a research institute located in the Global South, on at least a 50% contract, and working primarily within the arts, humanities, or social sciences. For the purposes of this Fellowship scheme, ‘Global South’ is defined as those countries that are included in the OECD’s list of countries receiving Official Development Assistance . Applicants should have been awarded a PhD at least five years before the date of application. Applicants must have a level of spoken English that will allow them to engage actively in discussion on topics of academic interest. Requirements This is a residential fellowship: scholars should be resident in Cambridge for the full term (nine weeks). Up to one week during the term may be spent elsewhere, by prior arrangement, for research, family or other personal reasons. A subsistence allowance will not be payable for time spent outside of the UK for non-academic reasons during the Fellowship. Fellows will be expected to take part in Research Practice seminar at CRASSH during the term. All Fellows selected under this scheme will be asked to work together to design an event related to the theme of this call, to take place during the term they are resident in Cambridge, and to present their own research at this event. Some of this preparatory work will take place online before the start of the Fellowship. Applicants must undertake to confirm their dates of travel at least five months before arrival in Cambridge and to apply for a visa (where required) at least four months before the start of their Fellowship. Successful applicants will need to confirm that they have taken out travel insurance (at their own cost). A successful applicant wishing to bring one or more dependants with them should inform CRASSH before the official letter of invitation is issued. We are able to include dependants in the letter of invitation, but applicants should be aware that we are not able to cover any additional costs involved in bringing dependants to Cambridge. Single accommodation will be provided as standard; it may be possible to book double accommodation for a Fellow who wishes to bring a partner, but availability is not guaranteed and the additional cost would be charged to the Fellow. We regret that we are not able to book accommodation for Fellows with children, which is more challenging to find in Cambridge. If Fellows choose to book family accommodation separately, CRASSH will make a contribution that equals the cost of the single accommodation we would have provided. Benefits Visiting Fellows will receive return (economy fare) travel from the scholar’s home institution, in accordance with the University’s travel policy. CRASSH will also cover the cost of a visa, if required. CRASSH will also book and cover the cost of single ensuite accommodation will be provided at Wolfson College . Wolfson College will waive its usual membership fee and provide free access to the college library, gym, and social spaces, as well as participation in activities open to college members. Fellows may take meals in the college Dining Hall at their own expense. As this scheme is open to scholars already employed at a higher education institution, it is assumed that most everyday expenses will be met through their salary; however, a subsistence allowance of £175 per week is provided to help with the costs of food and local travel, which may be higher in the UK than in the applicant’s country of residence. Each Visiting Fellow will have desk space and computer access at CRASSH, along with full access to the University’s libraries, collections, and academic events hosted by CRASSH and other University institutions. The in-person Fellowship must be held for a minimum of nine weeks, and may be extended to twelve weeks if the Fellow wishes. It will be followed by a nine-month digital Fellowship, providing continued access to the University’s online events and resources. Application procedure Applications must be submitted via the online application system by the deadline indicated. Register or log in to your application on the right-hand side of this page. The following documents are required: A cover letter, explaining why you would like to be considered for a Fellowship at CRASSH. A curriculum vitae – please use the template supplied. Applications with CVs in alternative formats will be considered ineligible. A copy of your phD certificate , confirming that your PhD has been formally awarded and clearly showing the date of award. A letter of support from your Head of Department (or equivalent), confirming that leave of absence will be granted by your institution for the full period of the Fellowship. A sample of written work – please upload a short text (e.g. a journal article or book chapter) you have already published on a topic relevant to your research proposal. A research proposal – please outline in up to 1500 words the research project you propose to undertake during your Fellowship at CRASSH. Your proposal should clearly identify a central research problem or question and explain the original contribution your project seeks to make to existing knowledge or understanding. We are particularly interested in how your project emerges from your previous work, and how it builds on or challenges existing scholarship. Please explain the specific sources, materials, evidence or cases you intend to investigate, the approach you will take, and how these will enable you to address your research questions. Your proposal should also explain what part of the project you would aim to complete during the Fellowship. We are looking for proposals that demonstrate independent intellectual judgement, a well-developed understanding of the research problem, and a clear rationale for the choices underpinning the project. We value precision, originality and critical engagement over broad claims about the significance or novelty of the proposed research. For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the Centre for Research in the Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences (CRASSH) at the University of Cambridge Visiting Fellowships

No Offer Description The position A PhD Student position in gender studies is available in the Centre for Women’s and Gender Research (SKK) at the Department of Philosophy (IFF) , Faculty of Humanities, Social Sciences and Education (HSL) , UiT The Arctic University of Norway. The position is linked to the research initiative Gender, AI and Technological Engagements (GATE): Towards Informed Futures led by Ania Malinowska . The successful candidate will develop and carry out an original doctoral research project within GATE’s thematic framework, leading to a PhD degree. The candidate will participate in the research environment at SKK and contribute to interdisciplinary exchange on gender, artificial intelligence, technological change, and social life. The workplace is campus Tromsø. The duration is three years with possibility for one additional year upon completion of the doctoral thesis in time. Shortlisted candidates should expect to be called for interview by April. Desired starting date in August 2027. The objective of the position is to complete research training to the level of a doctoral degree. Admission to the PhD programme is a prerequisite for employment, and the programme period starts on commencement of the position. The PhD fellow position is for a period of three years and full time studies with the possibility of an extension of the appointment period . If the doctoral dissertation is submitted for appraisal within 3 years or within 3.5 years, the PhD candidate is qualified for a completion grant for either 12 or 6 months. The completion grant should be used to further qualification measures such as courses in teaching in higher education, lecturing and other relevant work at the faculty. More information about the completion grant scheme can be found here . Supervision and research environment The proposed main supervisor is Associate Professor Ania Malinowska, a cultural theorist and researcher working across technology, affect, gender and culture. Her research combines cultural and gender-informed theory with media archaeology, qualitative inquiry and art-based experimentation. She is the author of Love in Contemporary Technoculture (Cambridge University Press) and Cutting Up Books: A Writing Method in Critical Thinking (Intellect), and co-inventor of Hypnotic AI, a patented AI-based research and art system investigating affective human–technology relations. Formal supervision arrangements will be confirmed under UiT’s doctoral regulations . The project / The position’s field of research Gender, AI and Technological Engagements (GATE) brings gender studies into dialogue with science and technology studies (STS), critical AI studies, affect theory and digital humanities. It investigates how understandings of gender inform the design, use and governance of intelligent systems, and how these systems, in turn, shape identities, affects, social relations, knowledge, work and participation. The project takes a critical and constructive approach to artificial intelligence. It examines how AI and algorithmic systems can reproduce inequality, exclusion and bias, as well as how gender- informed research can contribute to more inclusive, equitable and socially responsible technological futures. The High North provides an important context for investigating geographical and linguistic biases in technological systems and for developing approaches informed by northern and Arctic experiences and histories of technology. Applicants are expected to propose a focused, feasible doctoral project addressing one or more of the following research directions: Gendered assumptions, representation and bias in AI systems, datasets, platforms and interfaces; Gender identities and expectations in interactions with AI agents, robots, avatars and digital assistants; Affect, trust, intimacy, care and relationships in human–machine encounters; Algorithmic feedback loops, data exclusion and the production of gendered knowledge; Gendered transformations of labour, automation, expertise and social reproduction; Gender-informed, qualitative, digital, historical, experimental or art-based methods for researching intelligent technologies; Gender-informed technological design, foresight, governance and emancipatory possibilities; AI and technological futures in the High North, including minority languages, Indigenous contexts and geographical inequalities. Project description should formulate a clear research question, situate it in relevant gender-theoretical scholarship, identify appropriate methods and empirical material, address research ethics, and provide a realistic plan for completion within the appointment period. Proposals may be theoretical, empirical or practice-based, provided they demonstrate a rigorous gender-theoretical and/or methodological contribution. Depending on the doctoral project, research may involve qualitative fieldwork, media archaeology, analysis of digital systems, or experimental encounters with technological objects. Opportunities for practice-based experimentation may include engagement with intelligent systems and research hardware such as Hypnotic AI, where relevant and feasible. Access to equipment, laboratory facilities and any particular system is subject to agreement and availability. The fellow is expected to present research at academic events, participate in the centre’s scholarly activities, and publish or otherwise disseminate findings in appropriate scholarly formats, including open access where possible. The project description shall not exceed 8-10 pages, literature references included. Template for project description can be found here . No Offer Description PhD position, MSCA-DN funding Atomic gases (hot atoms) provide powerful and elegant tools for fundamental physics and for quantum sensing of electromagnetic fields. The SAI group at USPN has developed unique precision spectroscopic techniques to probe hot atomic vapors at nanometric distances from surfaces, enabling experimental tests of thermal effects in Casimir–Polder (CP) interactions, a long-elusive prediction of QED [1,2]. Extending these approaches to molecular physics is a fascinating prospect. Molecules possess a rich internal structure and ultra-narrow transitions, offering new opportunities for fundamental physics studies. The SAI group has recently extended its nanoscale spectroscopy techniques to molecular gases, pioneering precision spectroscopy in molecular thin cells [3,4]. The use of molecular rovibrational transitions opens new perspectives for photonic platforms that have traditionally relied on dielectric materials such as glass or silicon nitride. In particular, operation in the near- and mid-infrared enables the use of silicon for thin-cell (nanocell) fabrication and the development of more complex nanophotonic structures, particularly well suited for QED experiments. A major objective of this PhD project will be the fabrication of nanocells for precision measurements of molecule–surface interactions. Such interactions are of fundamental importance in physical chemistry and have attracted considerable theoretical interest because the complex geometry of molecules can give rise to anisotropic Casimir–Polder interactions. These interactions will be investigated through precision spectroscopy of acetylene or HF molecules confined in silicon nanocells. Our unique approach will directly probe differences in the surface interaction between molecular quantum states with different orientations of their rotational angular momentum relative to the surface. This platform could subsequently be extended by integrating more complex silicon nanostructures. A further objective will be to interface acetylene, which exhibits rovibrational transitions at telecommunication wavelengths, with high-Q silicon nanocavities [5]. Coupling these two systems could provide access to molecular cavity-QED studies. Moreover, the strong confinement of electromagnetic fields within cavity gaps, on the scale of only a few nanometers, could enable molecular spectroscopy at unprecedented distances from surfaces, giving access to CP interactions in the extreme near field. Objectives/tasks 1. Fabrication of nanocells filled with molecular gases (acetylene or HF). 2. Spectroscopic probing of molecular gases confined within 100 nm gaps, and precision measurements of the Casimir-Polder interaction. 3. Theoretical modeling of Casimir-Polder, molecule-surface interactions. 4. Coupling of acetylene gases with high-Q silicon nanocavities. References 1. A. Laliotis, T. P. de Silans, I. Maurin, M. Ducloy, and D. Bloch, “Casimir–Polder interactions in the presence of thermally excited surface modes,” Nat. Commun. 5, 4364 (2014). 2. J. C. de Aquino Carvalho, I. Maurin, P. Chaves de Souza Segundo, A. Laliotis, et al., “Revealing Some Disagreements between a Casimir-Polder Sensor and Predictions from Far-Field Emittance,” Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 143801 (2023). 3. J. Lukusa Mudiayi, I. Maurin, T. Mashimo, J. C. de Aquino Carvalho, D. Bloch, S. K. Tokunaga, B. Darquié, and A. Laliotis, “Linear Probing of Molecules at Micrometric Distances from a Surface with Sub-Doppler Frequency Resolution,” Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 043201 (2021). 4. G. G. Arellano, J. C. de Aquino Carvalho, H. Mouhanna, E. Butery, T. Billeton, F. Du-Burck, B. Darquié, I. Maurin, and A. Laliotis, “Probing molecules in gas cells of subwavelength thickness,” Nat. Commun. 15, 1862 (2024). 5. A. N. Babar, T. A. S. Weis, K. Tsoukalas, S. Kadkhodazadeh, G. Arregui, B. Vosoughi Lahijani, and S. description: 149 Application Deadline: 1 FEBRUARY 2027 Applications are now open for the 2027 St. Gallen Symposium Global Ideas Competition . Compete in the Global Ideas Competition and qualify for an all-expenses-covered participation as a Leader of Tomorrow in the world’s premier opportunity for cross-generational debates: The St. Gallen Symposium. As a Leader of Tomorrow, you’ll join a unique global community that extends far beyond the Symposium. Be inspired by world-renowned speakers, challenge your perspectives, and contribute to the conversations shaping tomorrow. Submission Type The Solution Brief is the core of your submission. In no more than 1,000 words, across four sections, you identify a real problem, back it with evidence, propose a partnership that could solve it, and show how it would work. It’s assessed anonymously, the strength of your argument and evidence is what counts, not who wrote it. The Video Explainer is your second submission. Imagine you run into your dream speaker at the Symposium and pitch them your idea — you have three minutes. Topic Question What could we solve, if we could agree? Cooperation increasingly comes with terms, and those terms determine what gets built and what is left undone. They also govern the clock: what was once a decision is now a negotiation. Somewhere, a solvable problem remains unsolved because the parties cannot agree. Identify such a problem and propose a novel arrangement that would make solving it more effective . Eligibility Enrolled in a graduate or postgraduate programme (master level or higher) in any field of study at a regular university Born in 1997 or later Requirements Form: Solution Brief (max. 1000 words using our template) + 3-minute Video-Explainer Individuality: Individual work expected, no group work allowed. The solution brief must be written exclusively for this contest . The idea must be the author’s own. Citation: All sources must be cited and referred to the respective part in the essay. All contributions will be tested for plagiarism . Any auxiliary aids (AI, proofreading, layout/graphics services, writing and translation programs, etc.) are to be listed. All auxiliary aids and resources used must be fully and correctly cited. Failure to acknowledge or reference any aid will result in disqualification . Transparency and academic integrity are mandatory. description: 105 Application Deadline: 5 February 2027. Applications are now open for the 2027/2028 International Court of Justice (ICJ) Judicial Fellowship Programme. The Judicial Fellowship Programme, formerly known as the University Traineeship Programme, was established in 1999 to enable recent law graduates to gain professional experience by working for the International Court of Justice. The programme aims to deepen participants’ understanding of public international law in practice and of the Court’s procedures by involving them directly in the activities of the Court. Judicial Fellows work on a full-time basis under the supervision of a Member of the Court, alongside the Member’s primary legal assistant. Fellows can expect to conduct research and draft memorandums on questions of law or fact relating to cases pending before the Court, attend hearings and sittings, and perform any other duties that may be assigned to them by their respective judges. The duration of the fellowship is approximately ten months, from early September to June of the following year. The Court selects up to 16 participants each year, nominated by universities across the world. Eligibility criteria and selection of candidates In making its selection, the Court seeks candidates of diverse nationalities. To be eligible, candidates should be 31 years old or younger at the start of their fellowship. This requirement may be waived only in special circumstances. Candidates must have achieved excellent results in their legal studies and demonstrate an interest in public international law through their studies, publications and/or work experience. Candidates must have an excellent oral and written command of at least one of the two official languages of the Court (English and French); a working knowledge of the other language is considered an asset. Only universities can nominate candidates. The Court does not accept applications from individuals. While it is possible to nominate a single candidate, the Court encourages universities to propose more than one nominee. Nomination Requirements An online pre-screening questionnaire must be completed by the nominating university, which must also designate an authorized focal point through whom all application materials will be submitted. Following completion of the questionnaire, the focal point will receive a confirmation email containing further application instructions, the ICJ personal history form and the candidate profile summary table. The following six documents must be submitted for each candidate via the email address of the university’s focal point, in the order below: Official letter of nomination from the university ICJ personal history form Letters of reference Official academic records Writing sample Candidate profile summary table For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) Judicial Fellowship Programme

description: 26 Application Deadline: 15 February 2027 Applications are now open for the 2027 Iso Lomso Fellowships. The Fellowship words ‘iso lomso’ originate from isiXhosa, the translation of which is ‘the eye of tomorrow’ and connotes seeing into the future, working towards the future, preparing for the future, and laying foundations for tomorrow. Launched in 2017, the fellowship has evolved to be one of the most prestigious and highly competitive early-to-mid-level career programmes on the continent. Scholars selected for this Fellowship are considered as part of the highly regarded emerging researchers in their field. At Institutional level, the fellowship aims to significantly contribute to the efforts of universities and research institutions on the African continent in addressing the gap that exists between completion of the PhD and becoming an established scholar rooted in Africa. Requirements The fellowship Call is thus open to African scholars who have obtained a doctoral degree within the preceding seven years, have completed a post-doctoral Fellowship or equivalent post-PhD programme and hold an academic position at a university or research institution anywhere in Africa. All disciplines are considered. Eligibility criteria Applicants must be: a national of any African country; have an affiliation at a research or higher education institution in an African country, and continue to do so for the foreseeable future; have obtained a doctoral degree from any recognised higher education institution (worldwide) within the preceding eight years from 1 January of the fellowship Call year; have completed a post-doctoral Fellowship or conducted an equivalent post-PhD research programme; not more than 42 years of age on 1 January of the fellowship Call year; in a position to commence a first period of residency at STIAS within the first year from date of fellowship commencement. Applicants from non-Anglophone African countries may conduct their research in the language of preference; however, the application documents must be completed in English. Programme Details Iso Lomso Fellowships provide a three-year affiliation with STIAS. The aim is to facilitate and support emerging researchers towards becoming established scholars in their fields. This is achieved by enabling the Iso Lomso Fellows to develop and conduct a long-term research programme of their preference. The main means of support is STIAS residencies. Residential periods will be agreed mutually between the Fellow, their home institution and STIAS, and may vary between ten weeks and five months per residency with a total of ten months residency time supported over the three years. A first period of residency is to be taken up at STIAS, followed by one or two further residencies at STIAS or abroad. Benefits While in residence at STIAS Fellows receive regular STIAS Fellow support which includes: an economy return airt ticket or on-road return reimbursement for SA-based Fellows (where applicable); accommodation preferably within walking distance from the Institute; individual office equipped with a PC, monitor, and connected to a pool printer; a monthly stipend for daily living costs; access to the Stellenbosch University library (including electronic resources) and a high-speed internet connection; participation in the regular STIAS Fellows programme, including daily lunch, weekly Fellows’ seminars, STIAS public lectures and social events; a childcare subsidy for Fellows accompanied by young children while in residence. During the three-year Fellowship period, Fellows may apply for a range of research sponsorship interventions. These are considered in a flexible manner to ensure that each fit the individual Iso Lomso Fellow’s academic career goal and optimally into the Institute’s research programme. The research sponsorship interventions may include: a residency at a partner Institute for Advanced Study or relevant research institution beyond their home institution country (this will form part of the ten months’ residency allocation; the Fellow’s preferences for potential host institutions will be considered); funding to attend up to two academic conferences or research training events (covering travel, accommodation and participation fees); limited project funding for key interventions in their research programme; the possibility of hosting a workshop at STIAS or at their home institution as a means of strengthening the Fellow’s scholarly network and research impact. For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the Iso Lomso Fellowships

description: 30 Application Deadline: 15 February 2027 . Applications are now open for the 2027 African Research Universities Alliance (ARUA) Early Career Research Fellowship Programme. The African Research Universities Alliance (ARUA), with support from the Mastercard Foundation, invites applications for the third cohort of its Early Career Research Fellowship Programme. The programme will support forty (40) early-career African researchers to undertake six-month research fellowships at institutions hosting or affiliated with ARUA’s thirteen (13) Centres of Excellence (CoEs) and twenty-two (22) Africa–Europe Clusters of Research Excellence (CoREs). The fellowships will commence in May/June 2027 , depending on the readiness of successful applicants, and will run for six months, ending in October or November 2027, respectively. The programme aims to strengthen the research capacity, productivity, and global competitiveness of early-career African researchers by providing opportunities to undertake focused research, collaborate with experienced researchers, and benefit from structured mentorship at ARUA CoEs and CoREs. Through these engagements, Fellows are expected to generate high-quality research outputs, strengthen research networks, and contribute to knowledge generation and solutions to Africa’s development challenges. Requirements Applicants must be African nationals, hold a PhD in a relevant discipline and be 35 years or younger at the time of application, except where an age-limit exemption is granted under section 4 (b). At least 70% of the fellowships will be awarded to women. Selection Criteria – Applicants must meet the following eligibility and selection criteria: a) Nationality and academic qualifications: Applicants must be African nationals holding a PhD in a discipline or sub-discipline relevant to the thematic focus of the selected ARUA Centre of Excellence (CoE) or Africa–Europe Cluster of Research Excellence (CoRE). Age requirement: Applicants must be 35 years of age or younger at the time of application. Age-limit exemption may be considered for female candidates older than 35 years at the time of application, subject to the ARUA ECR Fellowship Age-Limit Exemption Criteria. Applicants seeking an exemption should review the criteria before applying. Institutional affiliation: Applicants should be young faculty members or researchers at an ARUA member university. Eligible candidates from non-ARUA universities may also apply. Postdoctoral fellows: Female postdoctoral fellows may be considered in limited cases. Research excellence and potential: Applicants should demonstrate a highly competitive research track record relevant to the fellowship opportunity, with the potential and commitment to develop a strong international research reputation. Availability and institutional commitment: Applicants must be available to undertake a six-month residential fellowship away from their home institution and be able to return to their home institution upon completion of the fellowship. Research readiness and alignment: Applicants must be engaged in an ongoing research project aligned with the thematic focus of the selected CoE or CoRE and have readily available data to enable them to fulfil the research roles and responsibilities outlined in Section 3. Gender equity: Eligible women are strongly encouraged to apply. At least 70% of the fellowships will be awarded to female candidates, in line with the Mastercard Foundation’s commitment to advancing opportunities for young African women researchers. Benefits Successful applicants will be contracted by ARUA for a period of six (6) months. The fellowship will provide a monthly stipend of US$2,000, a modest accommodation allowance, and travel support covering a return air ticket to the host institution. No additional relocation expenses will be provided. No Offer Description Applications are invited for 15 fully funded Doctoral Candidate positions within INSIGHT, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe. INSIGHT will train a new generation of researchers in optical integrated sensing and communication, aiming towards compatibility by design, by combining expertise in optical communications, distributed fibre sensing, photonic integration, frequency combs, structured light, digital signal processing, machine learning, network optimisation and industrial sensing applications. Each Doctoral Candidate will undertake an individual research project within a coordinated international and intersectoral 36-month programme. The programme includes advanced scientific training, transferable-skills development, secondments at academic and industrial partners, joint workshops and network meetings, international conferences, and training in research integrity, open science, innovation, communication, entrepreneurship and intellectual property. The selected candidates will be employed by the relevant INSIGHT recruiting beneficiaries and enrolled in a doctoral programme at the designated degree-awarding institution, subject to its admission requirements. Available Projects/Positions: DC1 – Optimal amplification schemes for transmission and sensing coexistence This project will develop hybrid optical amplification strategies to allow high-capacity communication and distributed fibre sensing to share long-haul and metropolitan networks. The planned research combines modelling and experimental validation to balance reach, capacity and sensitivity in optical communication and sensing. Recruiting host: CSIC Location: Madrid, Spain PhD institution: Universidad de Alcalá DC2 – Noise-tolerant distributed optical fibre sensing architectures for long-haul sensing This project will create noise-tolerant distributed acoustic sensing architectures for long-haul fibres shared with telecommunications traffic. The project will use wideband and multi-wavelength probes, optical frequency combs, modelling and signal processing to improve robustness and compatibility with telecom infrastructure. Recruiting host: CSIC Location: Madrid, Spain PhD institution: Universidad de Alcalá DC3 – Low-frequency distributed acoustic sensing for infrastructure and environmental monitoring This project will extend distributed acoustic sensing towards ultra-low-frequency and long-term measurements without losing fast dynamic performance. Applications include environmental monitoring, early warning in natural catastrophes, power-cable thermometry, infrastructure health and the observation of slow geophysical processes. Recruiting host: CSIC Location: Madrid, Spain PhD institution: Universidad de Alcalá DC4 – Co-designed optical waveforms and physical-layer architectures for O-ISAC This project will focus on the design of the next generation of optical communication systems that can simultaneously transmit data and sense the physical environment of optical fibers. Develop and experimentally validate innovative optical waveforms and PHY architectures for high-capacity, distributed fiber sensing, combining photonics, signal processing, and AI-enabled sensing. Recruiting host: Politecnico di Torino Location: Torino, Italy PhD institution: Politecnico di Torino DC5 – Network-level coexistence, optimisation and deployment strategies This project will investigate how optical sensing and high-capacity WDM communication can safely coexist in real telecom networks, from metro to long-haul systems. Develop network-level models, optimization and control strategies, and validate ISAC technologies through experiments on real operator fiber infrastructures Recruiting host: Politecnico di Torino Location: Torino, Italy PhD institution: Politecnico di Torino DC6 – Application of agile optical frequency combs in Optical Integrated Sensing and Communications The overarching goal of this project is to investigate a sub/system-level framework for the generation, characterization and optimization of agile optical frequency combs (OFCs) to be employed in O-ISAC systems. This will entail the validation (numerical and experimental) of reconfigurable multi-carrier signals for high-capacity transmission and high-resolution fiber sensing. Recruiting host: Dublin City University Location: Dublin, Ireland PhD institution: Dublin City University DC7 – Photonic integrated circuit-based frequency-comb sensing in short-reach networks The primary objective in this project is to investigate the constraints imposed on PIC based OFCs employed as a transmitter/ad-hoc interrogator in cost sensitive short reach communications systems. This will entail designing and fabricating a PIC to be utilized in existing short reach optical infrastructure to monitor structural health, temperature fluctuations, and acoustic vibrations without degrading the communication throughput. Recruiting host: Dublin City University Location: Dublin, Ireland PhD institution: Dublin City University DC8 – Structured-Light Fiber System for Simultaneous High-Speed Communication and Distributed Sensing This doctoral project will develop a fibre-based system that uses structured light, such as vortex and cylindrical vector beams, for simultaneous high-speed communication and distributed sensing. The work combines laser development, mode-selective amplification and experimental validation over a 5 km fibre link Recruiting host: Tampere University Location: Tampere, Finland PhD institution: Tampere University DC9 – AI-Driven Reconstruction of Complex Multimode Optical Fields for Advanced Photonic Sensing This doctoral project will develop a physics-aware machine-learning framework to reconstruct and interpret complex spatio-spectral optical fields in multimode fibers. The work combines digital holography, numerical propagation modelling and AI-based inversion to enable more sensitive and higher-resolution fiber sensing of environmental changes such as strain, bending and temperature Recruiting host: Tampere University Location: Tampere, Finland PhD institution: Tampere University DC10 – Impact of noise on optical fibre sensing systems based on Rayleigh backscattering This project will focus on the theoretical, numerical, and experimental investigation of the impact of various noise sources on optical fibre sensing systems based on Rayleigh backscattering. Novel mathematical and modelling frameworks based on first principles will be developed and experimentally validated Recruiting host: Technical University of Denmark Location: Kongens Lyngby, Denmark PhD institution: Technical University of Denmark DC11 – Quantum-noise-limited signal demodulation This project will develop AI-assisted digital signal processing algorithms for highly sensitive estimation of strain, temperature, and pressure from Rayleigh-backscattered signals. The ultimate goal is to achieve record sensing sensitivity and push the performance of optical fibre sensing towards the fundamental quantum limit Recruiting host: Technical University of Denmark Location: Kongens Lyngby, Denmark PhD institution: Technical University of Denmark DC12 – DAS and DTSS compatibility with communication links This doctoral project will investigate how distributed acoustic, temperature and strain sensing can coexist with high-capacity optical communication systems in live telecom networks. description: 437 Application Deadline: 28 February 2027 Applications are now open for the 2027 ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship. According to an agreement between the Alliance of International Science Organizations (ANSO), the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and The World Academy of Sciences (TWAS/UNESCO) for the advancement of science in developing countries, up to 40 students/scholars from developing countries will be sponsored to study in China for doctoral degrees for up to 4 years. The ANSO-CAS Scholarship (formerly the ANSO Scholarship for Young Talents ) was launched in 2019 to nurture outstanding young scientists from across the globe. Each year, the scholarship provides support for 100–200 master’s candidates and 300 PhD candidates to pursue full-time postgraduate studies at the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS), and institutes of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). A dedicated sub-category under this program is the ANSO‑CAS‑TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship. Each year, TWAS/UNESCO selects up to 40 PhD candidates from developing countries for this sub- category, among whom 10 awards are prioritized for candidates undertaking climate-related research. Consistent with TWAS/UNESCO’s strategic priorities, preferential consideration will be given to applicants from Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and female applicants. ELIGIBILITY FOR THE ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PHD SCHOLARSHIP: Applicants must: Eligible applicants should NOT hold Chinese citizenship; Eligible applicants must be nationals of eligible developing countries in the South ( Developing Countries in the South | TWAS) Eligible applicants should be proficient in English or Chinese; For PhD program applicants: you should be born after 1 st January 1992 (inclusive); Eligible applicants should meet the admission criteria for international students of USTC/UCAS; Eligible applicants should NOT take up other assignments during the period of his/her scholarship. If the applicant is currently pursuing a doctoral degree at any university/institution in China, s/he will NOT be eligible for the PhD program of this scholarship. Otherwise, s/he will be disqualified from admission and the situation will be reported to the current university/institution You are NOT allowed to apply for the ANSO Scholarship in both USTC and UCAS simultaneously, otherwise you will be disqualified from admission. COVERAGE PhD program Tuition waiver 2. Monthly stipend:6,000 or 7,000 CNY/month (depending on whether the awardee has passed the qualification test arranged by the University), up to 48 months 3. Health insurance 4. Application fee waiver 5. International travel allowance from awardee’s home country to China (one trip per awarded candidate) 6. One-time visa For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship

description: 420 Application Deadline: February 28, 2027. Applications are now open for the 2027 SADC Media Awards Competition. The Secretariat of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) is pleased to announce the launch of the 2027 SADC Media Awards competition in four categories, namely Photo, Print, Television and Radio Journalism. Established in 1996, the SADC Media Awards recognise outstanding media work that contributes to disseminating information on SADC and promoting greater public understanding of the regional integration agenda. The Awards seek to recognise journalists who demonstrate excellence, originality, accuracy, depth of research and impact in reporting on SADC and matters relating to regional cooperation and integration. The Awards further recognise the important role of the media in informing citizens about SADC programmes, policies, initiatives and achievements, while providing a platform for journalists to bring regional issues closer to communities across the SADC region. Through quality and impactful journalism, media practitioners contribute to strengthening communication, awareness and visibility of SADC and promoting greater citizen engagement in the regional integration process. Prize The first prize winner in each of the four categories will receive US$2,500, while the runner-up in each category will receive US$1,000. The SADC Media Awards are open to journalists from all SADC Member States. The winners of the 2027 SADC Media Awards will be announced during the Opening Ceremony of the 47th SADC Summit of Heads of State and Government, to be held in the Republic of Zambia. Requirements Entries are invited from the following categories: i) Print Journalism: comprising features/articles published in newspapers, newsletters, websites, magazines. Print Journalism submissions should have a minimum of 100 (one hundred words and a maximum of 2000 (two thousand) words. ii) Radio Journalism: comprising broadcast material. Radio Journalism broadcast material should have a minimum duration of 1 (one) minute and a maximum of 30 (thirty) minutes. All broadcast material should be submitted on a CD or USB. The entries should be accompanied by electronic transcript in word format for translation purposes. iii)Television Journalism: comprising televised material. Broadcast material should have a minimum duration of 1 (one) minute and a maximum of forty-five (45) minutes. All broadcast material should be submitted on a CD or USB. The entries should be accompanied by electronic transcript in word format for translation purposes. iv) Photojournalism: comprising published pictures with a caption. Photographic entries should have one (1) photo, or a pictorial spread of not more than twenty (20) photos published in one issue/edition. Each entry must be accompanied by an original newspaper in which photo (s) were published. f) All entries must be submitted to the National Adjudication Committee not later than February 28, 2027. For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the SADC Media Awards Competition

description: EPSRC CDT in Quantum Information Science and Technologies 4 year PhDs at the EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Quantum Information Science and Technologies (2027) The University of Sussex, in partnership with the University of Bristol, has launched the new EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Quantum Information Science and Technologies (QIST) funded via the UK Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC). This programme provides unique cross-disciplinary training in experimental and theoretical quantum information and quantum technologies, and specialised training in entrepreneurship, project management, collaborative working, responsible research and innovation (RRI), science policy, and communication skills. What you get We offer 4-year fully funded PhD studentships which includes tuition fees, stipends (tax free) and a generous research budget. Stipend rates will differ for home and international students, with international students receiving the standard UKRI rate (for the 2026/27 academic year, this is currently £21,805) enhanced by £1000 for 4 years. Home students starting their studies in September 2027 will receive the standard UKRI rate, plus the UK Government’s TechExpert funding, taking their payments to a maximum of £30,000 per year. Type of award 4 year PhD scholarship PhD project Whether you're an engineer with an interest in quantum computing, a physicist with a passion for practical technologies or a mathematician with an aptitude for experimental work, this programme is the next step to a successful career in quantum technologies. Our EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Quantum Information Science and Technologies (QIST) welcomes candidates with backgrounds in mathematics, engineering, computer science, chemistry or the physical sciences. This programme is the next step to a successful career in quantum technologies, whether you are: a computer scientist with interest in developing quantum algorithms a chemist intrigued by the modelling power of quantum simulators a mathematician with a passion for quantum computing a physicist excited to implement practical technologies an engineer inspired to deploy a quantum-enabled communications network Our programme: Our four-year programme has been designed by leading academics and industry partners and includes a broad range of taught modules at Sussex and at Bristol in year one leading to a three year research project phase. Postgraduate researchers at Sussex and Bristol will benefit from: Guided and self-inspired learning with a broad range of PhD research projects available Experience of practical application as well as a sound theoretical understanding of quantum physics Developing complementary skills – such as commercialisation and science communication – necessary for academic and industrial excellence Access to an international network of world-class academic and industrial collaborators Week long industry trip to visit companies and research labs working in the quantum field, we have visited the USA for the last 3 years Financial support for academic and industrial secondments Opportunity and funding to attend international and national conferences A cohort approach to learning, enabling students to learn from each other in a rapidly evolving field Access to a broad technology base and state-of-the-art facilities at Sussex and Bristol Our Master Class: We will offer a Microwave Trapped-Ion Quantum Computing Master Class at the University of Sussex. The masterclass will be led by a software engineer formerly working at Google (Joe Swainston) and two talented quantum computing researchers (one with focus on quantum gates (Chris Knapp) and the other focussing on electronics engineering for quantum computing (Pedro Taylor Burdett)). The Master class will be open for our doctoral students based at Sussex. Students will receive training in critical skills for microwave trapped-ion quantum computing and the control of quantum technology experiments using ArtiQ, all during the first year of the CDT. This will give students authentic and hands-on training towards the development of practical quantum computers and other quantum technologies based on trapped ions. Eligibility Applicants should have at least an upper-second class undergraduate degree in a relevant subject such as Physics, Mathematics or Engineering (or equivalent qualification). Scholarships are available for both UK and International candidates. Candidates for whom English is not their first language will require an IELTS score of 6.5 overall, with not less than 6.0 in any section - English language requirements Applications are particularly welcomed from candidates with protected characteristics – e.g., from Black and other ethnic minorities and individuals with disabilities who are under-represented in postgraduate research at our institution. Please do draw our attention to any of the above in your application. Please do note the following when submitting an application. AI-generated personal statements do not capture your individual voice, and thus tend to sound generic, which provides little information for those reading your application to consider when deciding whether or not to invite you to interview. We would thus recommend that you write your personal statement in your own words. As a result, we will not penalise statements that contain minor grammatical and syntactical errors. Number of scholarships available Up to 10 per year Deadline 3 May 2027 23:45 How to apply Applications should be submitted as early as possible. The final application deadline will be the 03 May 2027 but applications may close early if all available places have been filled. Late applications will not be considered. We anticipate holding the first round of interviews in January 2027, the deadline for these applications will be the 01 December 2026. The next deadline will be the 01 February 2027 where we anticipate the bulk of applications. Interviews for this round will be in March 27. (Interview dates have not yet been confirmed and these timings are indicative) As the majority of applicants are expected to be interviewed in March 2027, we recommend submitting your application by the February deadline to be considered. Contact us We will be holding an OPEN DAY here at the University of Sussex on Friday the 15th of January , please do register early for this event using this form . We look forward to welcoming you to the event. For further information about the programme at Sussex please contact the QIST-CDT team.
