About the role Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate. We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in New York to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centers are sited, built, and operated. This is not a communications role or a government affairs role, though you will do elements of both. It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbor, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations. You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand. You will travel regularly across New York State, including upstate communities, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data center markets. Key responsibilities Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with town, village, city, and county elected officials and administrators, planning and zoning boards, local industrial development agencies, state agencies, economic development organizations, community groups, civic leaders, labor and building trades organizations, educational institutions, and workforce partners in description: Join the BE-CSS-IDE section and help shape how CERN stores and serves data from the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC). NXCALS, the CERN accelerator archival system, holds many years of data from CERN's particle accelerators: magnet and powering signals, beam instrumentation, cryogenics, and machine protection and post-mortem data. Accelerator operators, equipment experts and beam physicists use it every day to run the machine, diagnose faults and study performance. Your work will focus on the needs of the HL-LHC. You will help keep NXCALS fast, reliable and scalable as particle accelerator data volumes grow and the machine moves toward the High-Luminosity LHC era. You will work on a real production system alongside experienced engineers, with plenty of opportunities to learn and take ownership. Your responsibilities: Contribute to the development of NXCALS core components, focusing on HL-LHC use cases: ingestion pipelines (ETL), metadata services, data compaction, data extraction and APIs. Improve the performance and reliability of data access for LHC operations, machine protection analyses and commissioning activities. Work with accelerator users in the CERN Control Centre and equipment groups to understand their needs and help them build applications and analyses on NXCALS. Help evaluate big-data technologies (such as HDFS, Apache Ozone or ClickHouse) and their fit for future HL-LHC data requirements. Follow modern engineering practices in a team that values code quality, testing and automation. Your profile: Solid experience in Java development; familiarity with the Spring ecosystem is an advantage. Experience with, or strong interest in, big-data technologies such as Hadoop, HDFS, HBase, ClickHouse, Apache Spark or Kafka. Working knowledge of Python; experience with PySpark is a plus. Familiarity with software quality practices, CI/CD and DevOps. Curiosity about particle accelerators and enthusiasm for working with diverse user communities. Skills: Java. Spring ecosystem (advantage). Hadoop, HDFS, HBase, ClickHouse. Apache Spark, Kafka. Python, PySpark (plus). Software quality practices. CI/CD, DevOps. Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language. Eligibility criteria: You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State . You have a professional background in Software Engineering (or a related field) and have either: a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience; or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience. You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before. Job closing date: 06.12.2026 at 23:59 CET. Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum. Working hours: 40 hours per week Job flexibility: Hybrid Target start date: 01-March-2027 Job reference: BE-CSS-IDE-2026-176-GRAP Field of work: Information Technologies Benchmark job: 200020 - Computing Engineer Global Benefits A monthly net stipend of either 6372 or 7004 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree. 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure. Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund. Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances. A relocation package (installation grant and travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances. Possibility to extend your contract up to 36 months. On-the-job and formal training including language classes. Overview of CERN - Discover a world where the impossible is made possible! At CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, we are pushing the frontiers of science and technology. Our groundbreaking work brings together not only physicists but also a diverse range of professionals from engineering, technical, scientific, and administrative fields. Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive. Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. We meet these challenges through the diverse perspectives within our teams, ensuring every contribution is valued and driving our shared sense of inclusion and purpose. Diversity is a core value of CERN since its foundation, and it remains central to our mission and continued success. If you are ready to be part of a dynamic, inclusive community pushing the boundaries of knowledge, CERN is the place where your curiosity and skills can thrive. Be part of our mission to uncover what lies at the heart of the universe! TAKE PART! More information about us, here: careers.cern

description: At CERN , the European Organization for Nuclear Research, physicists and engineers are probing the fundamental structure of the universe. Using the world's largest and most complex scientific instruments, they study the basic constituents of matter - fundamental particles that are made to collide together at close to the speed of light. The process gives physicists clues about how particles interact, and provides insights into the fundamental laws of nature. Introduction The CERN ATLAS Team plays a major role in the construction of the future silicon ATLAS Inner Tracker (ITk). In particular, the final integration of the ITk detector prior to installation in the experiment is a crucial step to validate the full functionality. As an applied physicist or engineer in the CERN-ATL Team, you will join the Tracker section (EP-ATL-TRK) and work closely with personnel from the Detector Technologies Group (EP-DT) on the construction and integration of the ATLAS ITk Pixel System and its integration into the ATLAS ITk. Functions Reception testing of ITk Silicon Pixel Detector elements and testing of multi-module Pixel structures to be integrated into the ITk Pixel Outer Barrel. Testing and verification of integrated ITk Pixel Detector structures and services as well as combined testing with the ITk Strip Detector in the surface integration facility (SR1) at CERN. Deploy and improve software and hardware elements for integration testing and service validation (online, detector control, detector safety) for the Pixel Detector and the combined ITk. Document procedures and results for ITk integration testing and service validation and develop testing procedures for the ITk Detector after installation. Participate hands-on in the ITk Detector integration work in the surface cleanroom as well as the preparation of equipment for the different testing stages. Master's degree or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Applied Physicist or Engineering or a related field. Experience: Proven experience in the construction and integration of silicon pixel detectors for high energy physics experiments. Proven experience in the testing and data analysis of silicon detector systems. Proven experience in silicon detector operation and quality control including the development, installation and commissioning of laboratory infrastructure. Experience in the development of DAQ/online software or detector control systems for silicon detector testing and operation. Demonstrated experience in working in a multi-disciplinary team and international collaboration, including physicists, engineers and technicians involved in work on detector construction. The following experience would be an advantage: Experience on interpreting CAD designs of mechanics components or cooling plant operation. Assembly of sensitive equipment in a clean room environment. Technical competencies: Testing and validation of detector, accelerator and beam line components. Assembly and integration of detectors. Construction, test and installation of electromechanical equipment and systems. Development of application software. Assembly and integration of infrastructure for detectors or experimental facilities. Behavioural competencies: Achieving Results: delivering high quality work on time and fulfilling expectations. Demonstrating Flexibility: adapting quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements. Working in Teams: building and maintaining constructive and effective work relationships. Managing Self: working well autonomously; taking on activities and tasks without prompting. Communicating Effectively: expressing opinions, ideas and suggestions with conviction and in a logical/structured manner; keeping to the point. Language skills: Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French. description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! WHY THIS ROLE Enterprises hand Cohere their most sensitive data and put our models inside workflows they can't afford to get wrong. Securing that means working on problems the industry hasn't settled yet, what authorization means when an agent acts on a user's behalf, how to contain tools that consume untrusted input, and whether tenant boundaries hold when a model can be steered by the data it reads. The established playbooks only take you so far. We're hiring a Senior Product Security Engineer to work these problems alongside the engineers building the products, reviewing architecture and code, threat modeling before implementation, testing what ships, and turning what you learn into defaults other teams inherit. This is a hands-on engineering role, not an advisory one. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Lead security reviews. Review architecture, code, and security-sensitive changes. Identify both individual vulnerabilities and the recurring design patterns behind them. - Secure AI-powered products. Evaluate risks such as prompt injection, unsafe tool use, identity and delegation failures, excessive agency, data exposure, tenant isolation, and sandbox escapes. - Threat model new capabilities. Identify trust boundaries, abuse cases, and high-impact failure modes before implementation. Translate findings into practical, prioritized mitigations. - Perform hands-on testing. Investigate suspected vulnerabilities, develop proofs of concept, assess exploitability and impact, and partner with engineers through remediation. - Build scalable guardrails. Develop secure defaults, approved patterns, reusable controls, review requirements, and automated checks that reduce recurring risks. - Strengthen engineering capability. Pair with engineers, document practical guidance, and help product teams develop durable security expertise. - Influence risk decisions. Explain technical findings, business impact, and remediation options clearly to engineers, product leaders, and executives. YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF - You have strong software engineering fundamentals and can independently understand, test, and contribute fixes to production codebases. - You are proficient in at least one of Python, Go, or TypeScript. - You have led security reviews or threat models for complex production systems and can point to meaningful design or risk improvements that resulted. - You understand common vulnerability classes and their underlying design failures, including injection, authorization flaws, IDOR, SSRF, unsafe deserialization, race conditions, cryptographic misuse, and software supply-chain risks. - You understand modern application architecture, including web applications, APIs, OAuth/OIDC, cloud platforms, containers, Kubernetes, and CI/CD systems. - You can reason rigorously about untrusted input, authorization, isolation, identity, delegation, and data boundaries. Direct experience with agentic AI systems is valuable but not required. - You have driven security improvements involving multiple engineering teams, including situations where influence mattered more than authority. - You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences. NICE TO HAVE - Experience building or operating security tooling such as SAST, DAST, SCA, custom linters, or policy-as-code. - Experience securing multi-tenant SaaS, enterprise software, or systems that process sensitive customer data. - Offensive security experience through penetration testing, red teaming or security research. - Experience operating or participating in a vulnerability disclosure or bug bounty program. - Contributions to open-source security projects, published research, conference talks, or credited vulnerability discoveries. description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our Deployment Engineering team in North America. This isn't a typical management role - we need someone who thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and leads from the front: technically sharp, hands-on, and relentlessly focused on impact. You'll manage a team of Forward Deployed Engineers on the front lines of building agentic solutions with Cohere's North platform, balancing technical excellence with the kind of team leadership that actually moves things forward. You'll be solving complex problems and securely integrating AI into critical sectors such as finance, healthcare, and telecommunications. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Lead and mentor a team of Forward Deployed Engineers focused on building agentic solutions with North in on-premises environments. - Take ownership of customer success from technical implementation through delivery. - Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, and Sales to shape how we deliver AI to enterprises. - Build relationships with technical stakeholders on the customer end. - Foster a culture of continuous improvement and innovation, focusing on bringing agentic solutions to every step of the development process. - Define and implement processes that scale agent development and deployment across multiple client environments WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 8+ years of experience in software engineering - 2+ years of experience managing software engineering teams - Experience managing engineers in a fast-paced, high-growth environment - Hands-on experience building and deploying enterprise software at scale, with focus on agentic applications - High agency - you don't wait for permission to solve problems - A doer mentality - you dig in, get stuff done, and can execute in fast-paced environments - Excellent communication skills in English, with ability to translate technical concepts for both technical and business audiences NICE TO HAVE'S - Experience with AI/ML infrastructure - Background in enterprise security and compliance. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

description: Your work will change lives. Including your own. We are building a future where biology is solvable. The path to new medicines is currently slow and expensive, with high failure rates, leaving millions of patients waiting for new treatment options. Our story is one of innovation: applying AI, vast datasets, and industrial scale to decode biology and accelerate the development of life-changing treatments. Recursion’s Returnship Program Recursion’s Returnship program, sponsored by the Women at Recursion Employee Resource Group, helps professionals who have taken a break of two or more years from the STEM industry return to the workforce. Participants work in a supportive, learning-focused environment with guidance from their teams and mentors. Our program benefits both sides. You’ll own projects that directly advance our mission to radically decode biology and serve patients, and you’ll build experience with new, cutting-edge tools and technology. In turn, Recursion gains access to an underutilized pool of talent in Utah and benefits from the skills and experience you’ve built through your work and life. What you’ll get A dedicated mentor who meets with you weekly Weekly seminars on workplace culture, communication, and technology Support from your team as you re-enter the workforce Our program runs for sixteen weeks, from March 2027 through the end of June 2027. Depending on performance and business needs, it may lead to full-time employment. This position is primarily based at our Salt Lake City, UT headquarters, with some hybrid flexibility. Neuroscience Returnship The Neuroscience (Neuro) team is a diverse, collaborative group working on complex human cell models for drug discovery. This team works on iPSC differentiation techniques, process development for scaled cell production, assay development for cell characterization, and gene editing techniques to deliver data packages that drive decisions about cellular models and compound selection. With a mission of bringing transformative medicines to patients, this high-performing team works together to continually improve our workflows. The Neuro Returner will work alongside, and in support of, R&D scientists. This role will be trained and mentored by a scientist and will interact with other team members outside of Neuro daily, as needed, during the returnship period. You will own a laboratory project focused on developing and validating cell-based assays, performing hands-on cell culture work, and maintaining data and documentation in the team’s systems. You will be the critical bridge between our cutting-edge AI capabilities and the specific needs of Canadian federal departments, provincial agencies, Crown corporations, and defence organizations. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic’s mission is to ensure that the world safely makes the transition through transformative AI. Security is one of the clearest places where that mission plays out: the same capabilities that help attackers move faster can help defenders move faster too, and helping them use those capabilities safely and well is what this team is for. Security teams are among the earliest and most demanding users of frontier AI. They use Claude to review code at scale, find vulnerabilities before attackers do, and work through alert queues their analysts can’t keep up with. Anthropic’s Applied AI organization is building a dedicated Security team to help them do this well, and we are looking for its first leader. You will build this team from zero. You’ll decide which security customers the team serves first, who you hire and in what order, and how the team works with Sales, Applied AI Engineering, and our security, legal, and trust partners. You’ll also stay hands-on with a few of our most important security customers, because what you learn in those accounts becomes the playbook for everyone else. You’ll also set the standard for how security customers use Claude responsibly, including where a person has to review the output before anyone acts on it. What you’ll do Hire, onboard, and develop the first Applied AI Architects on the Security team. Coach senior and early-career architects differently, and give each one clear goals. Decide where the team spends its time: which segments and account types come first, which deals get architect coverage, and how to say no clearly when demand outruns headcount. Partner with security account executives on joint account plans, regular pipeline and forecast reviews, and deals where the customer’s security review sets the close date. Guide customers from discovery through evaluations and proofs of concept with written success criteria. Then take them from one-time code scans to sustained workloads: application security in the development lifecycle, continuous automated penetration testing, alert triage and investigation, and vulnerability and threat intelligence. Work alongside the security ISVs, systems integrators, and managed security providers already in our customers’ accounts. Keep a clear line between what Anthropic delivers and what partners deliver. Bring in Applied AI Engineers and our security, legal, and trust teams when a customer’s build or review needs them. Write the first security playbooks, reference implementations, and evaluation approaches. Bring what you learn back to Product, Engineering, and Research, so Claude becomes more useful and more trustworthy for defenders at the same time. Carry a small number of strategic security accounts yourself, from executive briefings with CISOs to hands-on workshops with their engineers. Have hands-on security depth in at least one area, such as application security, detection and response, offensive security, or vulnerability management, deep enough that practitioners trust your judgment . Application security experience highly preferred. Have used LLMs for real security work, such as code review, vulnerability discovery, triage, or investigation, and can say where they helped and where they failed. Have worked large enterprise security deals end to end, including customer security reviews, in close partnership with sales. Care about making AI both safe and useful for defenders, and can explain security risk and value to a CISO and to the engineers who will run the work, in terms each one cares about. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why This Role? We're seeking an experienced Program Manager to join Cohere's customer-facing Program Management team, with a focus on UK public sector and defence accounts. This is a highly specialised role requiring an individual who understands technical program delivery, the technical complexity of frontier AI models and the unique requirements of government and defence organisations. You will be the critical bridge between our cutting-edge AI capabilities and the specific needs of UK Government and defence organisations. You'll navigate complex procurement processes, stringent security requirements, data sovereignty concerns, and regulatory compliance while ensuring our customers successfully deploy and scale our AI solutions. In this role, you'll collaborate with our Strategic Customer team, Applied ML (AML) Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Platform, Product, and Go-to-Market teams, serving as the technical program lead and trusted advisor for our most sensitive and high-impact government engagements. Location: UK Security Clearance: Active Top Secret clearance preferred; candidates with Active Secret clearance or those who are eligible and willing to obtain clearance will also be considered. What You'll Do Customer Program Leadership: - Own end-to-end technical program delivery for UK public sector and defence customers, from initial deployment through production scaling - Serve as the primary technical program point of contact for government customers, building trusted relationships with departmental CIOs, IT directors, and technical teams - Translate complex government requirements (security, compliance, accessibility, bilingualism, data sovereignty) into actionable engineering plans - Navigate government procurement processes, RFP responses, and contractual technical obligations. Strategic Communication: - Provide clear, timely, and objective communication across Cohere's engineering organisation, customer stakeholders, and government leadership - Translate between AI/ML technical concepts and government-appropriate language for decision-makers who may not have deep technical backgrounds - Present technical roadmaps and status updates to senior government officials and departmental executives - Represent Cohere's technical capabilities in sensitive government and defence contexts. Complex Program Management: - Create and manage project schedules that account for government timelines, security review processes, and ministerial approval cycles - Identify and manage dependencies across government departments, security authorities, cloud service providers, and internal Cohere teams - Navigate risks unique to government deployments: privacy compliance, security authorisations, technical and infrastructure constraints - Drive alignment between product development priorities and specific government requirements. Technical Delivery & Execution: - Ensure on-time delivery of AI solutions that meet government-grade security, privacy, accessibility, and performance standards - Coordinate technical work across multiple teams: model customisation, security hardening, integration with government systems, bilingual support - Establish governance checkpoints appropriate for high-stakes government deployments - Problem-solve complex technical challenges in air-gapped, on-premises, or highly regulated environments. You May Be a Good Fit If: Required Experience: - 6+ years of experience as a customer-facing Technical or Engineering Program Manager in AI/ML consulting, technology transformation, or enterprise software delivery. - Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management. - Experience working with government, defence, or heavily regulated customers (public sector, defence contractors). - Proven track record managing complex, multi-stakeholder technical programs with stringent compliance requirements. - Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; advanced degree or technical certs a plus. Technical Background: - Strong understanding of enterprise software deployment architectures (cloud, on-premises, hybrid, air-gapped) - Working knowledge of or experience with modern AI: LLMs, agentic systems, MCP, RAG, fine-tuning, evals, and responsible AI would be a strong differentiator - Comfortable discussing API integrations, model inference, data pipelines, and ML operations with technical stakeholders. Government & Defence Acumen: - Deep understanding of how government organisations procure, evaluate, and deploy technology - Familiarity with UK government requirements: data sovereignty, privacy laws (Privacy Act), accessibility standards, official languages obligations, security classifications - Understanding of defence and national security considerations in AI deployment - Experience with Algorithmic Impact Assessments or AI ethics frameworks is a strong asset - Eligible to obtain UK government security clearance (Top Secret preferred) Nice to Have: - Active UK government security clearance (Secret or Top Secret) - preference for active Top Secret clearance - Background in or strong familiarity with UK defence, intelligence, or critical infrastructure sectors - Experience with GC Cloud services (Azure, AWS GovCloud) or Protected B/C environments - Project management certification (PMP, PgMP) or government-specific methodologies. Security Clearance Requirements This role requires eligibility for UK government security clearance. Preference will be given to candidates who currently hold an active UK government Top Secret (TS) clearance, as this will enable immediate engagement with our most sensitive defence and national security customers. However, we will also consider exceptional candidates who: - Currently hold UK government Secret clearance and are eligible for TS upgrade - Do not currently hold clearance, but are eligible and willing to undergo the Top Secret clearance process - Have a previous government security clearance that has lapsed Please note that obtaining Top Secret clearance can take 12-18 months. Candidates without active clearance will work on non-classified public sector accounts while the clearance process is underway. What Makes This Role Unique This isn't typical program management—it's a highly specialised role at the intersection of frontier AI, national security, and public sector digital transformation. You'll work on some of the UK’s most sensitive and impactful AI deployments, helping government organisations harness cutting-edge technology while maintaining the highest standards of security, ethics, and accountability. If you're passionate about responsible AI adoption, understand the unique constraints and opportunities within government, and want to have an outsized impact on how the UK leverages AI to serve its citizens, this role is for you. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are seeking an experienced public opinion researcher to build and expand Anthropic's in-house polling and research function. This role will be fundamental to understanding how key audiences — from policymakers and third-party groups to the general public — perceive and respond to Anthropic's policy positions, messages, and campaigns. This is a foundational role: you'll establish the research function from the ground up, with high autonomy and limited precedent. The Central Policy team sits at the operational heart of Anthropic's policy function — distinct from government relations and communications, but essential to enabling both. You'll work cross-functionally to ensure our policy and communications strategy is grounded in a rigorous understanding of stakeholder sentiment. The polling insights you generate will directly feed into high-visibility campaigns and will be a key asset in our policy efforts in Washington and beyond. Anthropic is equal parts research lab, policy think-tank, and technology startup. We care deeply about the safe development of AI systems and build partnerships with governments through proactive, opinionated, substantive policy conversations. This role offers a unique opportunity to be at the forefront of AI policy, bringing rigorous research discipline to policy strategy. Success in this role means establishing trusted relationships with leading polling firms around the world, delivering high-quality research on a regular cadence, and becoming the internal expert on how key audiences perceive AI, Anthropic, and Anthropic's positions and messages. You'll translate polling insights into strategic recommendations that measurably improve campaign effectiveness, and build scalable processes that allow the function to grow efficiently as demand increases. Key responsibilities Develop a comprehensive strategy for our in-house political research function that aligns with Anthropic's policy goals Identify, evaluate, and establish relationships with leading research and polling firms, ensuring coverage across demographics, geographies, and political perspectives Conduct detailed, proactive research to test core messages, policy proposals, and campaign themes, and to evaluate Anthropic's brand perception and performance Execute rapid-response polling to quickly assess Anthropic's messaging strategy in response to external events, policymaker actions, competitive developments, or emerging opportunities Work with external affairs colleagues (federal, state, and international) and policy communications to identify research priorities, interpret findings, and translate insights into actionable strategic recommendations Develop and maintain a knowledge management system for polling data, insights, and recommendations that ensures findings are accessible and actionable Manage polling vendors at scale, including vendor performance management Participate in strategy sessions and provide thought partnership on the design of messages, policy proposals, and campaigns ahead of polling and testing Create clear, compelling deliverables that distill polling findings into insights and recommendations Identify opportunities to build and scale the polling function over time, including staffing needs, process improvements, and capability expansion Track and report on the impact and utility of research, measuring how insights translate into more effective campaigns and strategic decisions Minimum qualifications Experience designing and executing public opinion research, including survey and questionnaire design, sampling approaches, and message testing Ability to analyze quantitative and qualitative polling data and translate findings into clear, decision-ready written recommendations Experience selecting, briefing, and managing external polling or research vendors Strong writing and presentation skills, including distilling complex research for senior, non-technical audiences Preferred qualifications 8+ years of professional experience in political or public opinion research, ideally spanning multiple campaign cycles and policy environments Corporate public affairs experience, ideally in a highly scrutinized or regulated industry Strategic thinking that spots emergent issues, identifies and tests the right messages, and translates those insights into tactical recommendations A track record of building relationships with vendors, external experts, and complex stakeholder ecosystems Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, maintain clear priorities, and deliver on tight timelines Comfort operating in ambiguous environments, taking ownership of problems, and proactively driving initiatives with limited precedent A resourceful, collaborative working style and genuine commitment to being a strong teammate Passion for AI policy and alignment with Anthropic's safety mission and commitment to responsible AI development The description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads. It needs to serve petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. In this role, you’d have an opportunity to build this system from the ground up. You’d be a key contributor, working on a problem few teams have had to solve at this scale. In this role, you will: - Design, build, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation. - Run this system multiple on Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale. - Work with researchers and training-infra teams on how jobs actually read and write data, and turn that into throughput, latency, and durability requirements - Work through the networking, I/O, and consistency problems of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time-to-insight as the measures of success You may be a good fit if you have: - Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management. - Strong coding ability. We work in Python and Go; experience in either is enough, but you should be willing to pick up the other - Experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets. - Hands-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX-style filesystems. It’s a bonus if you have: - Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre. - Familiarity with the data-loading and checkpointing patterns used in large-scale model training. - An interest in how large models are trained and evaluated, including the trajectory and eval data those runs generate, and a desire to understand the workloads the platform is serving. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

description: 40 Application Deadline: Applications are now open for the 2027 Ghent University Doctoral Scholarships. With support from its “Special Research Fund” (BOF) Ghent University grants annually 15 PhD “sandwich” scholarships to promising PhD students from Global South countries who wish to carry out half of their PhD research at Ghent University (‘North’) and the other half at a university in the Global South (‘South’). Ghent University only finances the part of the research that will be carried out in Ghent (24 months). The candidate must have full-time funding for the other 24 months of research to be carried out in the South. Requirements Candidates need to come from – and have the nationality of – one of the selected Global South countries (see country list ). The proposals must be jointly submitted by the candidate, a supervisor (promoter) at Ghent University and a supervisor at the partner university (Global South country). No restrictions are imposed on the field of research, nevertheless preference will be given to topics that are relevant within the South-North context. South-North context relevance relates to the extent to which the objectives of a proposal are consistent with beneficiaries’ requirements, synergy opportunities, global priorities and partners’ and donors’ policies. Only degree students (students who intend to obtain a (joint) PhD degree at Ghent University) can apply. Exchange students cannot apply for this scholarship. This program is meant for students at the beginning of their PhD. To a limited extent, PhD students are allowed to have already completed preliminary research. At the time the fellowship will start (1/10/2027), a minimum of 36 months of doctoral research must still be required to complete the PhD. Ghent University wants to encourage more female researchers to apply for this scholarship. That is why a Ghent University supervisor can support a maximum of 2 candidates per call on condition they are both of a different gender. Scholarship Duration 8 months: 24 months funded by Ghent University + 24 months funded by the partner institution in the Global South. Co-funding is mandatory with this scholarship. Consult the call documents below for more information on what kind of co-funding is allowed. In general, the following conditions must be guaranteed by the partner in the Global South: There must be a local PhD supervisor at the partner university/research center in the Global South. A written statement from the partner university/research center is requested stating that the candidate will receive a fulltime local PhD scholarship or salary for a period of 24 months when working on the PhD at the partner university in the Global South. The candidate will be sufficiently exempted from teaching or other assignments as to be able to fully concentrate on the PhD research in the South. Applicants can dedicate maximum 10 % of their time (fulltime appointment) to other tasks (teaching and other tasks). The following mobility scheme is mandatory: Students need to start and end with a research stay of 3 -12 months in at Ghent University. The first research stay at Ghent University needs to be started between 1 October 2027 and 28 February 2028. At least 24 months of locally funded research in the Global South must be scheduled in between the first and last research stay at Ghent University. Exceptions to the mandatory mobility scheme mentioned above: Applicants who can demonstrate that they are unable to start their 4-year PhD research with a research stay at Ghent University because the partner university/research center in the Global South requires a successful completion of a PhD study program in their university before commencing further research activities, can request an exception to the mobility scheme. Applicants who can demonstrate that they are unable to start their 4-year PhD research with a research stay at Ghent University because they must first complete a period of field research in the Global South can apply for an exception to the mobility scheme. Applicants who can demonstrate that they have successfully completed a full-time funded PhD study period (of maximum 12 months) at the partner university/research center in the Global South can request to integrate this period in the required 24 months of locally funded research stay in the Global South. Applicants who can demonstrate that they have successfully completed a full-time funded PhD study period (of maximum 12 months) at Ghent University can request to integrate this period in the required 24 months of research period at Ghent University. Budget PhD scholarship at Ghent University (in total 24 months). The Ghent University promoter receives a bench fee of € 310/per month of research in Ghent + € 8.000 travel budget to cover (part of) the operational costs, as well as part of the travelling costs of the student and both the Ghent University and the local promoter. How to Apply Find a supervisor (promotor) at Ghent University. All candidates must have the support of a Ghent University professor (ZAP) who is willing to act as the supervisor for their PhD. Candidates looking for a supervisor can consult the list of faculties and available research topics on the Ghent University Research Explorer . Ghent University professors can decide whether or not to accept a PhD student. Without the support of a Ghent University professor the application is not eligible. Find a supervisor at a partner University/Research Center in the Global South who is willing to supervise the PhD. Make sure the partner University/Research centrer in the Global South is willing to provide a full-time appointment/scholarship for the part that should be caried out in the Global South (24 months co-funding) and guarantees the candidate will be sufficiently exempted from teaching or other assignments whilst executing part of the PhD at the Global South (official statement). Application forms must be submitted (in English) electronically to [email protected] For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the Ghent University Doctoral Scholarships

description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a design engineer to help build and maintain Waypoint, our design system, across both the Figma library and the production codebase. This is not a "designer who codes a little" or an "engineer who dabbles in Figma" role. You should be genuinely fluent on both sides, comfortable defining a component's behavior and states in Figma one hour and shipping the same component to npm the next. You'll take direct ownership of the Figma side of our library (structure, variants, tokens, documentation) while also contributing to the core Waypoint system: our component packages, our token pipeline, and the tooling that keeps design and code in sync. If the idea of being the single point of continuity between a Figma frame and a production component sounds exciting rather than exhausting, this is your role. We're also thinking beyond the system we have today. Waypoint isn't just meant to serve designers and engineers, it's meant to become something a model can read, reason about, and build with directly. We want someone who can help us get there: grounded enough to do the unglamorous work of making today's system solid, and forward looking enough to help define what an intelligent design system looks like next. WHY THIS ROLE Waypoint is still early enough that the decisions you make now will shape how the system scales. You'll have real ownership, not just a queue of component tickets, and you'll be working alongside a team that treats design and engineering as one discipline rather than two departments that hand work back and forth. And you'll be helping define what a design system becomes when it has to serve a third audience: the models that will increasingly build with it. RESPONSIBILITIES - Own and evolve the Figma library for Waypoint: component structure, variants, properties, and documentation, so it stays a reliable source of truth for design teams. - Build and maintain core Waypoint components, contributing directly to our component packages alongside the design engineering team. - Work across our token pipeline, keeping design tokens in Figma and their code representations (CSS custom properties, Tailwind config) tightly synced. - Partner with product designers to translate new patterns into system components, and with product engineers to make sure those components are easy to adopt correctly. - Help define and refine the workflows and tooling that connect Figma and code (sync scripts, plugins, documentation sites) rather than relying on manual handoff. - Write clear documentation and usage guidance so the system scales without you being the bottleneck. - Weigh in on system architecture decisions: when to add a new component versus extend an existing one, how to version and package changes, how to keep the system consistent as it grows. - Help shape how Waypoint evolves to serve a third consumer beyond designers and engineers: the model itself. That means thinking about how components, tokens, and patterns get structured so they're legible to AI systems, not just to humans. QUALIFICATIONS - 6+ years of combined design and/or engineering experience, with real depth in both. We care less about your job titles and more about whether you can move fluidly between Figma and code without losing fidelity in either direction. - Strong command of Figma at a systems level: component architecture, variants, auto layout, variables and tokens, and library management, not just using components someone else built. - Solid front end engineering skills, ideally TypeScript and React, with the ability to build accessible, well tested, production quality components. - Experience working with or building design tokens and understanding how they flow from design tool to codebase. - A systems mindset. You think in terms of reusable, composable patterns rather than one off solutions, and you can explain the tradeoffs of a system level decision to both designers and engineers. - Strong communication skills. You'll be the connective tissue between design and engineering, so you need to be able to advocate for system decisions to both audiences. - Comfort with ambiguity. Design systems work means constantly balancing consistency against the need to move fast and support new product surfaces. - A genuine interest in where design systems are headed, not just where they are. You should be able to hold the practical reality of today's system alongside a point of view on what it means to build for a future where AI is a first class consumer of your system, not just an afterthought. NICE-TO-HAVES - Experience building or contributing to design-to-code sync tooling (Figma plugins, token pipelines, MCP-based workflows, or similar). - Familiarity with accessibility standards (WCAG) and how to bake them into components rather than bolt them on. - Experience packaging and versioning component libraries for multiple consuming teams (npm scoped packages, semver, changelogs). - Exposure to multi-platform design systems work (iOS/SwiftUI, Android/Jetpack Compose, or token build tools like Style Dictionary). - Experience in an AI native product environment or genuine interest in how AI changes the way design systems get built and used. description: 151 Application Deadline: Applications are now open for the 2027 SA-CERN Programme Excellence MSc/PhD Bursary Program. The SA-CERN programme is a national programme funded by the Department of Science and Innovation and the National Research Foundation to provide South African researchers, students, engineers and technicians with an opportunity to participate in the world’s premier and largest international research facility at CERN The main aim of the SA – CERN programme is to make the facilities at the European Centre for Nuclear Research ( CERN ) in Geneva, Switzerland available to South African researchers, engineers, technicians and students. These facilities include ISOLDE (Isotope Separator On Line Device) and the LHC (Large Hadron Collider), the latter being a particle accelerator with a circumference of 27 kilometres, the largest and most powerful of its kind in the world. These facilities have been built to make new discoveries. The SA-CERN programme gives scientists and research students in South Africa access to the data obtained at CERN and allows them to take part in the running of experiments in Geneva. The outcomes are world class research, participation in global science, high level capacity development, innovation and technology transfer leading to competitive industry and infrastructure, the attraction of high quality young South Africans into the Science and Technology system and the development of the public understanding of science. The SA-CERN programme collects together several research thrusts in a collaborative and coherent way, building the network of science linkages within the country, and connecting them internationally. Programme Details The SA-CERN Programme Excellence Bursaries will provide full-cost-of-study support for successful applicants commencing their studies in the 2027 academic year, for the duration of their studies. This includes sponsorship of research trips to CERN aligned with the selected students’ projects. The bursary is open only to applicants starting their MSc or PhD studies in 2027. The bursary values per annum are as follows: ● MSc level: up to R150 000. ● PhD level: up to R200 000. Requirements: Applicants must meet the following requirements: ● A proven track record of excellence and clear evidence of outstanding future potential. The ideal candidate should have completed their previous degree with an aggregate of 65%. ● The research project and supervisor within the SA-CERN Programme: – The project must align with one of the Programme’s pillars: ALICE, ATLAS, ISOLDE, THEORY or Technology Transfer. – The supervisor must be an SA-CERN member. ● Registration at a South African university for full-time MSc or PhD studies commencing in 2027. ● South African citizenship. To apply: Complete this form by clicking the “ NEXT ” button and upload the following required documents. An up-to-date CV. A copy of your full academic record. A statement of purpose addressing: 1. The proposed research topic. 2. The proposed supervisor. A copy of your South African ID document. Three letters of recommendation. Copies of any research publications/reports you have authored or co-authored. A copies of your dissertation from your previous level of study. For More Information: Visit the Official Webpage of the SA-CERN Programme Excellence MSc/PhD Bursary Program

You do not need to tick every box or have every skill listed below, if you are motivated to learn, we encourage you to apply. Join CERN's Storage and Data Management Group and help evolve the storage systems behind the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), while learning large-scale storage, cloud-native technologies and open-source software with the support of an experienced team. You will work on CERNBox, the cloud storage used by the whole CERN community, from scientists to administrative staff. Your main task is to help make it interoperable with research infrastructures across Europe, through the Open Cloud Mesh (OCM) standard, and easy to deploy anywhere using Kubernetes. You will also explore how AI can help users find and use their data. If you enjoy open standards, open source and building tools that many institutions can adopt, this is the place for you! You will be supported by experienced colleagues and learn from the whole team. Your responsibilities Develop and integrate backend and frontend software components. Package and deploy interoperable services in distributed environments. Support CERN community: you will join our operations team, troubleshooting incidents and supporting users. Contribute your code, features and fixes back to the CERNBox open-source projects, working alongside a broader open-source community. Work with partner institutions and research infrastructures across Europe to test, validate and refine these tools together. Support users and partner teams as they adopt these tools, helping with troubleshooting and guidance. Explore and prototype AI/ML capabilities for CERNBox, working with users to identify practical use cases. Prior AI/ML experience is welcome but not required. Your profile Experience with backend development in Go, and an interest in full-stack development. Comfortable working in Linux environments and troubleshooting software and systems. Familiarity with frontend development, ideally using JavaScript/TypeScript and Vue.js. Software development experience from studies, projects, internships or open-source contributions, with a willingness to take ownership of features and to collaborate with others. Ability to collaborate with users, technical teams and external partners. Interest in open-source software, distributed systems and interoperability. Skills Backend: Go and API development. Frontend: Modern frameworks such as Vue.js or similar technologies. Systems: Linux, troubleshooting and software integration. Cloud-native technologies: Containers, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm and CI/CD pipelines are an advantage. Collaboration: Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders. Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French. Eligibility criteria: You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State . You have a professional background in Computing Engineer (or a related field) and have either: a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience; or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience. You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before. Job closing date: 29.11.2026 at 23:59 CET. Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum. Working hours: 40 hours per week Job flexibility: Fully Onsite Target start date: 01-February-2027 This position involves: Stand-by duty, when required by the needs of the Organization. Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization. Job reference: IT-SD-GSS-2026-174-GRAP Field of work: Information Technologies Benchmark job: 200020 - Computing Engineer Global Benefits A monthly net stipend of either 6372 or 7004 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree. 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure. Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund. Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances. A relocation package (installation grant and travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances. Possibility to extend your contract up to 36 months. On-the-job and formal training including language classes. Overview of CERN - Discover a world where the impossible is made possible! At CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, we are pushing the frontiers of science and technology. Our groundbreaking work brings together not only physicists but also a diverse range of professionals from engineering, technical, scientific, and administrative fields. Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive. Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. We meet these challenges through the diverse perspectives within our teams, ensuring every contribution is valued and driving our shared sense of inclusion and purpose. Diversity is a core value of CERN since its foundation, and it remains central to our mission and continued success. If you are ready to be part of a dynamic, inclusive community pushing the boundaries of knowledge, CERN is the place where your curiosity and skills can thrive. description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! About North: North https://cohere.com/north is Cohere's cutting-edge AI workspace platform, designed to revolutionize the way enterprises utilize AI. It offers a secure and customizable environment, allowing companies to deploy AI while maintaining control over sensitive data. North integrates seamlessly with existing workflows, providing a trusted platform that connects AI agents with workplace tools and applications. Why this role: The Data Abstractions & Tools team is the group inside North responsible for how users bring their data into the platform and put it to work. We own the systems that let users upload, organize, and share their files and knowledge bases, the framework for extending agents with skills and third-party integrations, and the data-sync pipeline that connects enterprise data sources to North's agents. North connects to a growing set of external tools and data sources so its agents can act on a user's real workflow. This role owns the integration pipeline end-to-end: adding new integrations to the platform, helping other engineers do the same, and becoming the owner of the process that makes that repeatable. You will also create the evals and tests that make sure those integrations work as expected and keep working as the platform evolves. In this role, you will: - Build new integrations (tools) on the North agentic platform, and maintain the ones already in production. - Own the integration pipeline: the process for adding a new tool, from design to shipping to ongoing maintenance. - Help other engineers add integrations of their own, and raise the bar for how the team does it. - Create evals and tests to make sure integrations work as expected and alert on regressions. - Tune tool descriptions to improve performance based on feedback and evals. - Use AI actively in your work, while staying accountable for the quality and reliability of what you ship. You may be a good fit if: - You have shipped production code and are comfortable building integrations against external APIs. - You have a background in evaluating agentic systems (ideal), or at minimum know what an eval is and are comfortable with prompt engineering and tool-description tuning. - You excel in fast-paced environments and can execute while priorities are a moving target. - You bring high agency: you learn quickly and drive change without waiting for perfect instructions. - You've owned things end-to-end before and care about the quality of what ships, not just that it shipped. - You enjoy helping other engineers succeed, not just shipping your own work. Working Location: This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

description: At CERN , the European Organization for Nuclear Research, physicists and engineers are probing the fundamental structure of the universe. Using the world's largest and most complex scientific instruments, they study the basic constituents of matter - fundamental particles that are made to collide together at close to the speed of light. The process gives physicists clues about how particles interact, and provides insights into the fundamental laws of nature. Introduction The CERN ATLAS Team plays a major role in the construction and integration of the future silicon ATLAS Inner Tracker (ITk). The different parts of the ITk system are being constructed and integrated in institutes and then transported to CERN where the entire ITk will be assembled. As an applied physicist or engineer in the CERN-ATL Team, you will join the Tracker section (EP-ATL-TRK) and work closely with the teams in the different institutes to synchronise the integration testing of the ATLAS ITk parts on surface, support their integration and commissioning into the ATLAS ITk and prepare the cavern commissioning. Functions Testing and verification of integrated ITk Strip Barrel and Endcap structures and services in the surface integration facility (SR1) at CERN. Work closely with integration sites off CERN, e.g. DESY or NIKHEF, synchronise the testing and provide trouble shooting support for integration teams including support at the sites. Develop software and hardware elements for the integration testing of ITk Barrel and Endcaps in the various integration sites and validate the procedures in SR1. Streamline and document procedures for ITk integration testing and service validation and extend the testing procedures for the ITk Detector after installation and during commissioning. Participate hands-on in the ITk Detector integration work in the ATLAS SR1 cleanroom and during ITk installation in the cavern including the preparation of equipment in the cavern. Master's degree or PhD or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Applied Physicist or Engineering or a related field. Experience: Proven experience in the integration, testing and operation of silicon detectors for high energy physics experiments. Proven experience in integration and commissioning of silicon trackers including services validation. Demonstrated experience in the development of DAQ/online software or detector control systems for silicon detectors in high energy physics experiments. Demonstrated experience in developing and streamlining testing procedures. Demonstrated experience in integration and commissioning of silicon trackers including services validation. The following experience would be an advantage: Previous work on particle detector operation in an experiment. Assembly of sensitive equipment in a clean room environment. Technical competencies: Testing and validation of detector, accelerator and beam line components. Assembly and integration of detectors. Construction, test and installation of electromechanical equipment and systems. Development of application software. Assembly and integration of infrastructure for detectors or experimental facilities. Behavioural competencies: Achieving Results: delivering high quality work on time and fulfilling expectations. Demonstrating Flexibility: adapting quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements. Working in Teams: building and maintaining constructive and effective work relationships. Managing Self: working well autonomously; taking on activities and tasks without prompting. Communicating Effectively: expressing opinions, ideas and suggestions with conviction and in a logical/structured manner; keeping to the point. Language skills: Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French. Employment Conditions Contract type: Limited duration contract (4 years). Subject to certain conditions, holders of limited-duration contracts may apply for an indefinite position. Working Hours: 40 hours per week Job Flexibility: Fully Onsite This position involves: Work in Radiation Areas. Interventions in underground installations. A valid driving licence. Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization. In this role, you will be an in-house regulatory lawyer for Anthropic's US AI regulation and a key contributor to our global frontier AI compliance strategy. You will provide regulatory-readiness counseling as new laws are developed, day-to-day advice once they are in force, and legal support for Anthropic's non-contentious engagement with US regulators and standards bodies. While the role is US-focused, AI regulation is inherently global: you will help ensure a consistent worldwide compliance posture, coordinate closely with colleagues leading our EU and international workstreams, and contribute to EU AI Act and other international work where it overlaps with your areas. You will work at the intersection of novel legal questions, fast-moving product development, and a high-profile regulatory environment, cross-functionally with Legal, Compliance, Safeguards, Security, Policy, Research, and product teams.
